000400 | ## 8b. The scope ceiling — how far Prash can go, and what stays permanently out of reach
000401 | [blank]
000402 | Written 2026-08-26, following straight from the positioning-gap finding above.
000403 | The team keeps adding connectors, actions, and diagnosis coverage — this is
000404 | the honest answer to "where does that road actually end," so the target
000405 | stays clear as scope grows instead of drifting into "eventually it does
000406 | everything" (the exact failure mode §5's inclusion rule already warns
000407 | against).
000408 | [blank]
000409 | **Tier 1 — real today.** CI failures (GitHub/GitLab Actions) and Kubernetes
000410 | pods: full diagnosis, a concrete proposed fix, human approves, Prash
000411 | executes and verifies.
000412 | [blank]
000413 | **Tier 2 — the actual target, reached by building more, not by removing
000414 | constraints.** For *any* system Prash has a connector into: real
000415 | root-cause diagnosis, a concrete proposed action, human approves before
000416 | anything executes. This is achievable for the full connector list and
000417 | whatever gets added later — it is only engineering work (extend the brain
000418 | per domain, define what "a fix" means there, add the action). **The human
000419 | approval step is exactly what makes this ceiling high**: Prash never has
000420 | to be autonomous-safe, it only has to be correct enough that approving is
000421 | fast and easy. Target framing for the team: *"diagnose and propose a real
000422 | fix for anything Prash has a connector into, always human-approved before
000423 | execution."*
000424 | [blank]
000425 | **The permanent floor — four things that stay true no matter how much
000426 | gets built:**
000427 | [blank]
000428 | 1. **No connector, no fix.** Zero visibility into a system means zero
000429 |    ability to diagnose or touch it. Shrinks as connectors are added, never
000430 |    reaches zero — there is always something not yet integrated.
000431 | 2. **Not a technical problem.** A vendor's pricing change, an unhappy
000432 |    customer, a legal call, a real feature-vs-bug tradeoff — these are
000433 |    judgment calls, not bugs. Out of scope by definition of what a DevOps
000434 |    agent is, not a gap to close.
000435 | 3. **The physical world.** A dead server, a bad cable, someone needing to
000436 |    walk into a data center. No API reaches that; Prash can alert a human,
000437 |    it cannot act.
000438 | 4. **Genuinely first-of-its-kind failures.** Diagnosis reasons from
000439 |    patterns and available evidence; a truly novel failure mode will
000440 |    sometimes be diagnosed wrong or incompletely, permanently, no matter
000441 |    how good the model gets. This is *why* the human-approval system is
000442 |    permanent infrastructure, not a training-wheels phase to remove once
000443 |    Prash is "good enough" — a human catching a wrong diagnosis before it
000444 |    executes is the actual safety net, always.

000475 | [blank]
000476 | **Where this came from.** Aradhya reviewed the read-only/write-capable split (5 read-only: Vercel, Datadog, Grafana, Snyk, Gitleaks; 5 write-capable: Kubernetes, GitHub, GitLab, AWS, PagerDuty) and called it out directly: *"that does not support the whole point of making Prash and that is 'it can actually solve your errors.'"* This is the same tension the positioning lock (§2, earlier same day) already named — "act within its permission tier," "replace a company's whole DevOps layer" — but the read-only-first posture several connectors shipped with hours earlier that same day quietly contradicted it. Anant independently confirmed the same read on the team WhatsApp thread the same afternoon (Azure/GCP write actions already done on his side; his words: *"read only ka faida kya hai"* — "what's the point of read-only" — and *"remove the read only part from the md as well"*), so this isn't a unilateral call, the team converged on it independently from two directions.
000477 | [blank]
000478 | **The one genuine scoping question, decided before building, not guessed at:** every other connector's write action mutates the same system it reads from (mute the monitor you're reading, resolve the incident you're reading) — but Gitleaks has no cloud account of its own to mutate. A leaked secret isn't fixed by anything gitleaks itself controls; it's fixed by rotating the credential in whatever system it actually belongs to, which a local scanner has no way to know. Three options were weighed: (a) trigger an incident/notification when a leak is found — escalates to a human fast, reuses a connector Prash already has write access to; (b) stay read-only, since there's genuinely nothing safe to auto-mutate; (c) auto-redact the file and commit a fix — rejected outright, since it doesn't rotate the actual credential (still valid, still leaked in git history/logs/wherever else it was copied) and would misrepresent a cosmetic change as a real fix. **Aradhya chose (a).** Built as `gitleaks-escalate`: scans, and on a real finding opens a genuine PagerDuty incident via the Events API (a different PagerDuty product/auth model from the REST API `pagerduty-acknowledge`/`-resolve` already use — see `pagerduty.py`'s own docstring) — never including the actual secret text, same safety property `poll_state()`/`fetch_logs()` already enforce.
000479 | [blank]
000480 | **What got built, full detail in §10:** `vercel-redeploy` (SAFE) / `vercel-rollback` (APPROVAL), `datadog-mute-monitor` (SAFE), `grafana-silence-alert` (SAFE), `snyk-ignore-issue` (APPROVAL — accepting a known vulnerability is a real judgment call, not neutral noise suppression), `gitleaks-escalate` (SAFE — escalating a real problem is the opposite of suppressing one). Risk tiers follow the same reasoning already established for every action in this codebase, not re-litigated per action: SAFE for reversible/low-blast-radius/easily-corrected, APPROVAL for anything that's a consequential claim (changes what's live in prod, accepts a security risk) or suppresses future signal.

000501 | - **Autopilot and Copilot are not competing products — they're two modes of one product**, not a contradiction to pick a winner from. *Autopilot* (cloud/environment-resident, 24×7, watches → notifies over the team's channel → acts within its permission tier) is the hero and the literal answer to tension #2 — it's on when the human is asleep. *Copilot* (local CLI + REPL) is what the same engineer drops into when they want to drive directly: deep-dive an incident, brainstorm the fix with Prash, watch it land. 000502 | - **ICP correction, overriding Anant's enterprise-ceiling framing: startups and small tech companies are the beachhead, not enterprise.** Reasoning: those are the teams where the engineers *are* the on-call rotation, so the pain is sharpest and most personal; they can say yes to a new tool in a week, where an enterprise security review of an AI agent with prod write access is a 6-month gate that would stall the company waiting on it. §4's local-credentials trust model is specifically what lets a startup say yes *without* that review. 000629 | - **Investigation budget.** `max_steps=2` is fine for CI (the failing logs are already in the prompt) but starves manifest work, which needs search → fetch → submit. 000630 | - **GitHub code search is unreliable for discovery.** `search_code` returned **zero results** for a file that provably exists in the repo, so the model correctly-but-wrongly concluded *"the manifest is not in this repository"* and declined. Verified: it finds the exact file search missed. **Generalizable lesson: never build discovery on GitHub's code-search index — its lag makes absence-of-results meaningless.**

000638 | **2026-08-17 — File-fidelity fix: `edits` (exact search/replace) replaces whole-file `new_content` regeneration as the default fix mechanism for existing files. Fixes the bug logged 2026-08-16.**
000639 | [blank]
000640 | The bug (§10, 2026-08-16 entry): stress-testing `apply-manifest-fix` on two new failure shapes found both real PRs contained the correct fix **plus** unrequested deletions of unrelated content elsewhere in the same file — one dropped two lines of an explanatory comment, the other dropped three instruction lines, with the model's own `fix_description` claiming *"everything else is untouched"* in the case where the diff proved otherwise. Root cause: `_ApplyFixBase.execute()` trusted `FileChange.new_content` as a complete, faithful replacement file and wrote it straight to a blob — there was no mechanism to verify the model actually reproduced everything it didn't mean to change, and extensive prompt-only enforcement (the six numbered "FILE CONTENT RULES" this replaces, some dating back to the v1 port) had already been tried and evidently wasn't sufficient.
000641 | [blank]
000642 | **Options considered (presented to Aradhya, he picked diff/patch application):**
000643 | - (a) Tighten the prompt further — cheapest, but the existing rules were already extensive and still failed live; LLMs are unreliable at "reproduce this exactly except X" as files grow.
000644 | - (b) **Diff/patch application — chosen.** Change the schema so the model emits exact-match search/replace edits instead of a whole file; apply them programmatically against the file's real fetched content.
000645 | - (c) Post-generation drift check — a safety net, not a fix for the root cause, and risks blocking real fixes on false positives.
000646 | [blank]
000647 | **What "diff/patch" means here, specifically — and why it's NOT the same as the "patch" field the old prompt explicitly warned against** (*"Patches are fragile and break on whitespace differences"*): that earlier warning was about traditional unified-diff hunks with line numbers and context windows, which really are brittle. The new `FileEdit` (`prash/brain/schemas.py`) is exact-substring search/replace instead — `old_content` must match the current file exactly and uniquely (same contract as Prash's own coding-agent Edit tool, deliberately, since it's a pattern models are already well-trained to produce). No line numbers to get wrong: it either matches or it fails loudly, it cannot silently misapply.
000648 | [blank]
000649 | **Implementation:**
000650 | - `FileChange` gained `edits: list[FileEdit]`; `new_content` is now new-file-only (validated: exactly one of `edits`/`new_content` must be set, never both, never neither).
000651 | - `FileChange.apply(original_content)` is the single mechanism that reconciles a change against real content — used both by `_ApplyFixBase.execute()` (fetches the real file via new `GitHubConnector.get_file_content()`, applies edits, writes the result) and by the M4 dependency-chain-completeness check (`_check_dependency_chain_completeness`, now takes `current_files` to reconstruct the resulting package.json when the fix used edits instead of new_content).
000652 | - The "drop empty content" filter in `diagnose_failure` (around `raw_args.get("files_changed")`) had to be updated to check `edits` too — checking `new_content` alone would have silently dropped every edits-based fix, exactly the "Prash quietly does nothing" failure this project exists to avoid. Caught in review before it shipped, not live.
000653 | - Prompt rewrite (`diagnosis_agent.py`): tool schema, all FILE CONTENT RULES, and every few-shot example (1-19, 20b) converted to teach `edits` as the default for existing files, `new_content` only for genuinely new ones.

000662 | **2026-08-15 — "Ask, don't quit" schema + prompt landed (Track D half of §6b criterion #5). 000663 | - **Purely additive, not a replacement.** `recommended_action` is untouched for confident single-action cases — nothing about today's behavior changes unless the model actually populates `options`.
000664 | - **Auto-derives `recommended_action` from the default option when unset**, so every existing call site (the whole CLI/dispatcher today, until Track A's rendering lands) degrades gracefully instead of going silently quiet — an ambiguous case still gets treated as a single best-guess recommendation through the normal approval pipeline, same safety gates as always, just without the richer picker UI yet.
000665 | - **Schema enforces the anti-crutch guard structurally, not just via prompt instruction:** `options` must have 2+ entries (a 1-option "menu" is rejected — that's just `recommended_action`) and exactly one `is_default` — both hard validation errors, not soft suggestions.

The pairing exists specifically to teach the model the line between real ambiguity and reaching for a menu to avoid committing.
000667 | - **`--noninteractive` decided, not deferred:** when `options` is present, an unattended run must report them and take zero automated action — never auto-pick the top-ranked option. 000743 | - **The audit log should record the choice, not just the outcome** — "user selected option 2 of 3 (restart_pod)" is materially better provenance than "restart_pod executed."
000744 | - **`--noninteractive` needs a defined answer.** There is nobody to ask in an unattended run. Auto-picking the top-ranked option in unattended mode is exactly the blast-radius risk the circuit breaker exists to prevent — the safe default is to report the options and take no action, but this must be decided explicitly, not defaulted into.
000745 | - **Guard against it becoming a crutch.** If the brain can always punt to a menu, it may stop committing to a diagnosis when it genuinely knows the answer. Confident cases should still propose *one* action; the menu is for genuine ambiguity only.

000749 | **What's being added and why.** Live-testing `prash fix --ci` (TESTING_CHECKLIST.md §2) against a real GitHub Actions run with two deliberately-induced independent failures surfaced that the CI multi-failure path is diagnosis-only: `cmd_fix`'s `--ci` branch (`prash/cli.py`) calls `diagnose_ci_run()`, prints the result, and returns — it never touches the dispatcher. `--mode`/`--dry-run`/`--noninteractive` are parsed but silently ignored for `--ci`. Worse, the output headline reads **"Fixed 5 of 5 independent failures"** when nothing was fixed at all — `MultiFailureResult.fixed_count` (`prash/brain/multi_diagnosis.py:79`) just counts sub-diagnoses that have `files_changed` populated, i.e. "the model proposed something," not "a PR exists." A real user reading that headline would reasonably think their CI is unblocked when it's exactly as broken as before. Confirmed with Aradhya this needs a real fix, not just a wording patch: build the actual capability.
000750 | [blank]
000751 | **What's new here, specifically:** every action registered today (`open-pr`, `request-secret`, `restart-pod`, `rollback`) either reads existing state or acts on infrastructure that already exists. `open-pr` itself only opens a PR between two branches that **already exist** — it doesn't write files or create commits. Nothing in the codebase can currently take a diagnosis's proposed file content and put it in a real branch. `apply-ci-fix` is the first action where Prash writes AI-generated code into a real repository.

000754 | 1. **New action `apply-ci-fix`**, registered in `_build_dispatcher()` (`prash/cli.py`) exactly like the existing 4 — SAFE tier, reversible, same `ActionSpec`/`plan()`/`execute()`/`verify()` shape as `open-pr` etc.
000755 | 2. **No local git clone.** GitHub's Git Data API does it over the REST API `GitHubConnector` already uses: get base branch's ref/commit/tree → create a blob per changed file (`FileChange.new_content` is already the complete file content, already has a path-traversal guard in `prash/brain/schemas.py`) → create a new tree → create a commit → create a new ref (branch) → then the existing `create_pr()`.
000756 | 3. **One combined PR per CI run, not one per failure.** `MultiFailureResult.combined_files_changed()` (`prash/brain/multi_diagnosis.py:82`) already exists, deduped and ready — it was just never consumed anywhere. 000862 | | 2026-08-30 | Aradhya (agent-assisted) | Fix — `tests/test_intent.py` pytest-hang root-caused + hardened; closes the 2026-08-24 "hangs under pytest" finding | **Root cause (finally):** the REPL intent LLM fallback's sync bridge (`_run_llm_intent_sync` in `prash/intent.py`) called `asyncio.run()` directly on the calling thread. That is only safe when no event loop is already running in that thread — the assumption the original comment documented (repl = blocking loop, tui worker = plain OS thread). But it breaks in exactly the environments that hang: a pytest run with an event loop active, or any async caller — `asyncio.run()` raises `RuntimeError` there, and in some environments a `wait_for`-cancelled task that's sync-blocked (e.g. mid-httpx-connect) leaves `asyncio.run()` waiting on non-cancellable cleanup, which reads as an **indefinite hang under pytest** while direct Python scripts (no event loop in the main thread) work fine — matching the "environment-specific, reproduced via git stash" report exactly. **Fix:** the sync bridge now runs the bounded `asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(...))` in a dedicated daemon worker thread with a bounded `join(timeout=+5s)` and a `t.is_alive()` give-up — so it can never collide with a running loop and never blocks the caller beyond the timeout even if the coroutine ignores cancellation. Same honest contract (degrades to `None`), zero behavior change on the fast path. **Verified:** 31 original `test_intent.py` tests pass fast, a new regression test (`test_run_llm_intent_sync_never_hangs_on_stuck_coroutine`) proves a never-completing coroutine returns `None` in bounded time (~12s) instead of hanging forever, full suite **447 passed / 7 skipped**. The hang itself did not reproduce on this machine (current code was already bounded), so this closes the latent hang vector rather than a live one. |

000865 | | 2026-08-30 | Aradhya (agent-assisted) | Fix — repeated-identical-failure machinery wired up via a new `--reconcile` loop; closes the TESTING_SETUP.md known-gap | **The dead-code finding was real and worse than "unused": there was no retry loop at all.** `compute_error_signature()` and `diagnose_failure(..., repeated_failure=True)` were correct but zero real callers used them, and `cmd_fix --ci` was strictly one-shot (diagnose → `apply-ci-fix` opens a PR → exit) — a wrong hypothesis was never revisited. **Fixed by adding the v1 reconciler loop back**: `prash fix <owner>/<repo> --ci --run-id <n> --reconcile` now (1) applies the diagnosis's fix, (2) waits for the fix branch's (`prash/fix-run-<id>`) CI run to complete (bounded poll, fails fast rather than hanging), (3) if it failed, fetches the fresh logs and compares `compute_error_signature()` against the original run — **identical signature → re-diagnose with `repeated_failure=True`** (forces a different hypothesis), **changed signature → re-diagnose normally**, (4) applies the new diagnosis to the same branch and repeats, bounded by `PRASH_CI_RECONCILE_MAX_ITERATIONS` (default 2), stopping the moment a run passes. Never silently drops a partial fix. Provider-agnostic (GitHub + GitLab paths both thread `repeated_failure`/`iteration`/`previous_diagnosis` through `diagnose_multi_failure`'s existing `**diagnose_kwargs`). **Deliberately opt-in** (`--reconcile`) so existing one-shot `prash fix --ci` behavior is unchanged. 5 new tests in `tests/test_fix.py`. Full suite 446 passed / 7 skipped. |

Fixed by guarding both `learn()` and the mirror bare-target-prefixing branch in `apply_context()` with `not getattr(args, "ci", False)`. (2) `shlex.split(line)` raises `ValueError` on any line with an unbalanced quote character — in practice almost always an English contraction (`what's`, `it's`, `let's`) typed into something explicitly advertised as talkable-to. Fixed by giving the `ValueError` path the same stage-2 fallback the `SystemExit` path already has. Both live-repro'd before and after the fix (not just asserted in tests): the CI-context bug now correctly asks "Which pod should I fix?" instead of misfiring, and the contraction crash is gone. 3 new regression tests (`tests/test_repl.py`). 000902 | | 2026-08-16 | Aradhya (agent-assisted) | Bug (P1-ish) — manifest-fix regenerates files instead of patching them, drops unrelated content | **Stress-tested `apply-manifest-fix` on two new failure shapes beyond the already-verified image-tag typo, and found a reproducible fidelity bug in how the brain returns `files_changed`.** Built two new fixtures (`prash/connectors/testdata/configmap-mismatch.yaml`: a Deployment volume referencing a ConfigMap name that doesn't match the one defined, real `FailedMount` event → `StuckPending`; `oom-limit.yaml`: `polinux/stress` allocating 150M against a 20Mi limit, the standard k8s-docs OOM-demo pattern, real `OOMKilled` every run). Both live-verified end to end against the real cluster and real GitHub PRs: OOM → correct diagnosis (95% confidence) → correct one-line fix (`limits.memory: 20Mi → 200Mi`) → real PR #10. ConfigMap → correct diagnosis → correct one-line fix (`web-cfg → web-cfg-v2`) → real PR #11. **Both closed without merging, fixtures left broken and reusable, same convention as PR #6.** The bug: in both PRs, the diff included the correct fix *plus* unrequested deletions of unrelated comment lines from the same file (OOM: two lines of the fixture's own explanatory comment vanished, breaking the sentence; ConfigMap: three `Apply:`/`Watch:`/`Events:` instruction lines vanished, leaving a stray blank line) — and in the ConfigMap case the model's own `fix_description` explicitly claimed *"everything else is untouched,"* which the diff proves false. Root cause is architectural, not a prompt typo: `_ApplyFixBase.execute()` (`prash/actions/apply_ci_fix.py`) takes `FileChange.new_content` as the complete replacement file and writes it via a blob, so any content the model fails to faithfully reproduce while regenerating "the complete corrected file" is silently lost — there's no diff/patch step to catch drift, and nothing today verifies the non-target parts of the file survived. Low risk on these two fixtures (only comments), but the mechanism has no reason to spare *code* the model doesn't fully attend to on a larger real manifest. **Not fixed here — flagging for a decision**: options are (a) tighten the prompt to more forcefully demand byte-for-byte preservation outside the changed lines, (b) move to an actual diff/patch application instead of whole-file regeneration, or (c) add a post-generation check that only the intended lines changed and refuse the fix otherwise. Also noted: end-to-end latency for a manifest diagnosis with `--repo` is real — one `--noninteractive` run alone (investigation_max_steps=5, no `--dry-run` caching) took over 2 minutes, consistent with the existing p90 55s eval latency plus GitHub round-trips; not a bug, just a number worth having in mind before assuming a hang. `--dry-run` / `--noninteractive` (ask mode) / `--mode auto-safe --noninteractive` all gated correctly on both fixtures — no execution without the right flag combination in every case tried. |

000905 | | 2026-08-16 | Aradhya | **Root cause + fix — supersedes the four "model is being appropriately cautious" entries below** | **Prash could not fix Kubernetes problems because it had no mechanism to, not because the brain was timid — and the fix is live.** Full analysis in §9 (2026-08-16). 000906 | | 2026-08-16 | Aradhya | Finding — third attempt, a more precise answer than "try again" | **Third live attempt at triggering `Diagnosis.options`, and this one actually solved the mystery of why the first two didn't.** Built a new fixture (`prash/connectors/testdata/silent-crash-pod.yaml`: `busybox` running `sh -c "exit 1"` — completely silent, no echo, immediate exit) and this time caught the exact `restart_count=1` window live by polling the real restart count every second and firing `prash fix` the instant it hit 1 (the window holds for ~10-12s before climbing to 2 — tight but real). Confirmed: **still a confident, correct decline, not `options`.** But the reasoning why is now clear and it's not "the model needs more convincing" — a container that fails via `exit 1` has genuinely **zero plausible source of run-to-run variability**: no I/O, no randomness, no external dependency, nothing that could ever make one attempt behave differently from another. There's no real ambiguity to detect at *any* restart count, because the failure mode itself can't vary. This refines EXAMPLE 24's framing in the prompt (`prash/brain/diagnosis_agent.py`) slightly: "low restart_count" alone isn't what makes a case genuinely ambiguous — it's whether the failure has an actual mechanism that *could* produce a different outcome next time (a race, a timing-dependent external call, genuine resource contention). The model isn't over-pattern-matching "restart_count=1 → ambiguous," which is reassuring: it's still reasoning about the real evidence, not the example's surface shape. **Conclusion: hand-crafted k8s YAML tricks are the wrong tool for this** — genuine ambiguity is something real production failures have and synthetic fixtures mostly don't, by construction. Recommending this stop being chased via more fixture engineering; criterion #5's live-case half will close either from real future usage surfacing a genuinely ambiguous failure, or stays open pending that. Cluster torn back down to just the standard `broken-app` fixture. |

000001 | # Lear — the AI DevOps agent
000002 | [blank]
000003 | A local-first agent that watches your infrastructure — CI, Kubernetes, deployments —
000004 | and **acts** on what it finds, not just diagnoses it. Credentials stay in your own
000005 | environment; nothing is uploaded to Drufiy's servers.
000006 | [blank]
000007 | This is the ground-up rebuild. The original hosted CI-repair service
000008 | ([`prash-backend`](https://github.com/Drufiy/prash-backend)) stays live and unmodified
000009 | at prash.drufiy.com — this repo is not replacing it in the current sprint.
000010 | [blank]
000011 | **Read [`PRASH_V2.md`](./PRASH_V2.md) before writing any code.** It is the single source
000012 | of truth — architecture, task division, decisions, and the running bug/idea log. If
000013 | something isn't in that file, treat it as undecided, not assumed.
000014 | [blank]
000015 | ---
000016 | [blank]
000017 | ## Setup
000018 | [blank]
000019 | Requires **Python 3.10+**. Takes about two minutes.
000020 | [blank]
000021 | ```bash
000022 | git clone https://github.com/Drufiy/Lear-backend.git
000023 | cd Lear-backend
000024 | python3 -m venv .venv
000025 | source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
000026 | pip install -e ".[dev]"
000027 | ```
000028 | [blank]
000029 | Confirm the `prash` command resolved:
000030 | [blank]
000031 | ```bash
000032 | prash --help
000033 | ```
000034 | [blank]
000035 | Then create your local config from the template:
000036 | [blank]
000037 | ```bash
000038 | cp .env.example .env
000039 | ```
000040 | [blank]
000041 | Open `.env` and fill in **one model key** — either `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` or
000042 | `KIMI_API_KEY`. Everything else can stay blank to start. `.env` is gitignored and
000043 | never leaves your machine.
000044 | [blank]
000045 | > **Read this before you edit `.env`.** Leave unused keys *completely blank*
000046 | > (`KUBECONFIG=`), never a placeholder like `KUBECONFIG=none`. Prash treats a blank
000047 | > value as "not configured" and falls back to the sensible default; a placeholder is
000048 | > taken literally and will break in confusing ways. This exact thing broke the very
000049 | > first real install (`PRASH_V2.md` §10, 2026-08-14).
000050 | [blank]
000051 | Check it loaded — this never prints secret values, only which keys it found:
000052 | [blank]
000053 | ```bash
000054 | prash config
000055 | ```
000056 | [blank]
000057 | Run the test suite (should be **457 passed, 7 skipped** — the skips are live-cluster
000058 | tests that only run in CI):
000059 | [blank]
000060 | ```bash
000061 | pytest -q
000062 | ```
000063 | [blank]
000064 | That's enough to develop against. Everything below is only needed for the
000065 | Kubernetes features.
000066 | [blank]
000067 | ---
000068 | [blank]
000069 | ## Optional: a local Kubernetes cluster
000070 | [blank]
000071 | Needed for `prash fix`, `prash watch`, and `restart-pod`. Requires Docker Desktop
000072 | running, plus [`kind`](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io) and `kubectl`
000073 | (`brew install kind kubectl` on macOS).
000074 | [blank]
000075 | ```bash
000076 | kind create cluster --name prash-dev
000077 | kubectl apply -f prash/connectors/testdata/broken-pod.yaml
000078 | ```
000079 | [blank]
000080 | `kind` sets your kubectl context automatically. Put these in `.env`:
000081 | [blank]
000082 | ```
000083 | KUBE_CONTEXT=kind-prash-dev
000084 | KUBE_NAMESPACE=prash-demo
000085 | ```
000086 | [blank]
000087 | The fixture pod reaches a real `CrashLoopBackOff` in about 15 seconds — verify with
000088 | `kubectl get pods -n prash-demo`. Tear it all down with
000089 | `kind delete cluster --name prash-dev`.
000090 | [blank]
000091 | ---
000092 | [blank]
000093 | ## Trying it
000094 | [blank]
000095 | ```bash
000096 | prash repl                    # persistent session — best place to start
000097 | prash actions                 # every action, with its risk tier
000098 | prash config                  # local config, secrets redacted
000099 | prash tui                     # dashboard-style terminal UI
000100 | ```
000101 | [blank]
000102 | Once a cluster is up:
000103 | [blank]
000104 | ```bash
000105 | prash watch                                    # poll for broken pods, notify on new ones
000106 | prash fix prash-demo/<pod-name>                # diagnose a pod, act on the verdict
000107 | prash fix prash-demo/<pod-name> --repo <owner/repo>   # ...and propose a manifest fix as a PR
000108 | ```
000109 | [blank]
000110 | For CI failures:
000111 | [blank]
000112 | ```bash
000113 | prash fix <owner>/<repo> --ci --run-id <n>     # needs GITHUB_TOKEN
000114 | ```
000115 | [blank]
000116 | **Safety, worth knowing before you run anything:** every action goes through a
000117 | permission engine (`read-only` / `ask` / `auto-safe` / `environment-scoped` /
000118 | `bypass`, default `ask`), a circuit breaker that halts repeated action on one
000119 | resource, and an append-only audit log (`prash audit`). Add `--dry-run` to any
000120 | command to see the plan without touching anything real.
000121 | [blank]
000122 | ---
000123 | [blank]
000124 | ## The commands
000125 | [blank]
000126 | | Command | What it does |
000127 | |---|---|

000132 | | `prash watch` | Poll a namespace, notify on newly broken pods |
000133 | | `prash investigate <resource>` | Read-only connector probe |

000137 | | `prash circuit` | Inspect or reset the circuit breaker |

000132 | ## Reliability Engineering
000133 | [blank]
000134 | | ID | Task | Owner | Priority | Exit Criteria |
000135 | |---|---|---|---|---|
000136 | | R-01 | **Global error handling middleware** — catch all unhandled exceptions in FastAPI. Return structured error responses (`{"error": str, "code": str, "request_id": str}`). Never leak stack traces to clients. Log full traces server-side with request context. | Aryan | P0 | Zero raw 500 responses in normal operation. Every error response has a `request_id`. Error logs include request method, path, duration, user context. |
000137 | | R-02 | **Connector resilience: timeout + retry + circuit breaker per-connector** — every connector's `authenticate()`, `poll_state()`, `fetch_logs()`, `get_stats()` must have: configurable timeout (default 10s), retry with exponential backoff (max 3), per-connector circuit breaker (open after 5 consecutive failures, half-open after 30s). | Anant | P0 | Each connector wrapped with timeout/retry/breaker. Test: mock a connector that fails 6 times, breaker opens, subsequent calls fail-fast without network hit, after 30s half-open, next success closes it. |
000138 | | R-03 | **Graceful degradation on the dashboard** — if a connector is down, its widgets show a clear "unavailable" state with last-known-good data + timestamp, not a crash or blank. | Avi | P0 | Manually disconnect a connector, its dashboard widgets show "Last data: 2m ago - Connector unavailable" with a muted visual state. No React error boundaries triggered. |
000139 | | R-04 | **WebSocket reconnection with backoff** — desktop `useWatcher.ts` must handle: server restart, network blip, token expiry. Reconnect with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 30s). Show connection status indicator in the UI. | Avi | P1 | Kill the backend server, UI shows "Reconnecting..." indicator, restart server, UI reconnects automatically within 10s, status returns to "Connected". |
000140 | | R-05 | **Health check endpoint** — `GET /api/health` returns `{"status": "ok", "uptime_seconds": N, "connectors": {...}, "version": "..."}`. This is the load balancer probe target. | Parv | P0 | Endpoint returns 200 when healthy, 503 when critical connectors are down. Response time under 50ms (no connector calls, just cached state). |
000141 | | R-06 | **Structured logging with correlation IDs** — replace all `print()` and ad-hoc `logger.info()` calls with structured JSON logging. Every request gets a UUID correlation ID propagated through all log entries. | Aryan | P1 | All logs are JSON. `grep` for a correlation ID returns the full request lifecycle. Zero `print()` statements in `prash/` (except CLI user-facing output). |
000142 | | R-07 | **Watcher crash recovery** — if a watcher poll loop crashes, it must: log the error, send a notification about the crash itself, restart the loop after a backoff, never silently die. | Anant | P1 | Kill a watcher thread mid-poll, notification fires about watcher failure, loop restarts within 10s, normal operation resumes. Audit log captures the event. |

000364 | - `poll_state()` on the leaky repo → `FAILED`, `leak_count: 2`, findings
000365 |   scrubbed (only `rule_id` / `file` / `line` / `fingerprint` — the raw
000366 |   `Match`/`Secret` text is stripped, confirmed the secret value never
000367 |   appears in connector or `prash investigate` output)
000368 | - `fetch_logs()` → 2 real lines (`generic-api-key in config.py:1` etc.)
000369 | - `poll_state()` on a clean working tree (`no_git=True`) → `HEALTHY`
000370 | - Full CLI path: `prash investigate <path> --provider gitleaks` → `failed`
000371 |   with the scrubbed findings
000372 | [blank]
000373 | Two fixture gotchas worth recording: gitleaks' default rules deliberately
000374 | skip the AWS documentation example key (`<REDACTED_CREDENTIAL_LITERAL>` — contains
000375 | the `example` stopword) and any token containing the literal
000376 | `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz` substring (global allowlist stopword). A
000377 | realistic live fixture needs genuinely random high-entropy secrets, not
000378 | docs-style examples.
000379 | [blank]
000380 | Unit tests (`tests/test_gitleaks_connector.py`, 12) still mock the binary;
000381 | the live run above proves the connector's subprocess/report-parsing path
000382 | works against the real thing.
000383 | [blank]
000384 | ## Terraform
000385 | [blank]
000386 | **Status: pending.** Anant says his connector is done, pushing tonight.
000387 | Fixture setup (a real `.tf` plan with an intentional break) to follow once
000388 | the connector lands and its shape is known.
000389 | [blank]
000390 | ---
000391 | [blank]
000392 | ## Known non-connector gap, found auditing the diagnosis brain (2026-08-26)
000393 | [blank]
000394 | The June 2026 backend audit identified two systematic diagnosis weaknesses
000395 | (masked exceptions, repeated-identical-failure). Re-checked against the
000396 | current `prash/brain/diagnosis_agent.py` (this code was ported from
000397 | `drufiy-backend` into this repo):
000398 | [blank]
000399 | - **Masked-exception handling: real and wired up.**
000400 |   `_detect_masked_exception_risk()` flags a log where the failing evidence
000401 |   is a downstream status assertion with no revealing exception visible;
000402 |   `diagnose_failure()` then directs the model to fetch the producing
000403 |   function's source and reason about swallowed exceptions. Working as
000404 |   designed.
000405 | - **Confidence calibration: real and wired up.**
000406 |   `_recalibrate_confidence()` caps a model's self-reported confidence at
000407 |   `verified_rate + 0.2` based on real outcome history, plus a hard
000408 |   downgrade path for low-confidence `safe_auto_apply`/`review_recommended`
000409 |   fixes.
000410 | - **Repeated-identical-failure handling: wired up (2026-08-30), opt-in.**
000411 |   `compute_error_signature()` exists and is correct, and
000412 |   `diagnose_failure(..., repeated_failure=True)` correctly forces a
000413 |   different-hypothesis directive when set. **The gap that made it dead code
000414 |   was real: nothing in the actual retry path called either.** `prash/fix.py`
000415 |   and `prash/brain/multi_diagnosis.py` (the two real callers) never
000416 |   computed a signature or passed `repeated_failure=True`, and — the deeper
000417 |   issue — there was no retry loop at all: `cmd_fix --ci` was one-shot
000418 |   (diagnose → apply → exit), so a wrong hypothesis was never revisited. A
000419 |   stale comment referenced a `push_handler.py` retry flow that doesn't
000420 |   exist in this repo (leftover from the `drufiy-backend` port). **Fixed by
000421 |   adding the reconcile loop back:** `prash fix <owner>/<repo> --ci
000422 |   --run-id <n> --reconcile` now applies the fix, waits for the fix branch's
000423 |   CI run, compares `compute_error_signature()` between the original and fix
000424 |   branch runs, and re-diagnoses with `repeated_failure=True` when the
000425 |   signature is identical (forcing a different hypothesis) or normally when
000426 |   it changed. Bounded by `PRASH_CI_RECONCILE_MAX_ITERATIONS` (default 2),
000427 |   stops the moment a run passes, and never silently drops a partial fix —
000428 |   the already-open PR stays open for a human if the budget is exhausted.
000429 |   Default behavior is unchanged (one-shot) unless `--reconcile` is passed.
````

### `agent_guidelines.md`
````text
000001 | # Lear — Agent Guidelines
000002 | [blank]
000003 | This document outlines the coding traditions, architectural guidelines, and workflows to be followed by any AI agents (like Claude Code, Antigravity, etc.) working on this repository.
000004 | [blank]
000005 | ## 1. Project Philosophy
000006 | **Lear is a local-first AI DevOps agent.**
000007 | - **Credentials:** Credentials NEVER leave the user's machine. They are stored locally (e.g. in `.env`) and passed into connectors at runtime. No cloud-hosted backend stores these keys.
000008 | - **Cross-Platform:** This is a CLI tool that runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Path handling (`pathlib`), shell quoting, and line endings must be OS-agnostic. 
000009 | [blank]
000010 | ## 2. CLI-First Architecture
000011 | Prash is built as a **CLI-based app**. The UI revolves around text interfaces and interactive TUIs (via `rich` and `textual`).
000012 | - **Commands:** Every new feature should map to a clear, actionable CLI command or subcommand.
000013 | - **Interface:** Avoid assumptions about a GUI. The primary user interaction happens in the terminal (e.g., `prash fix`, `prash watch`).
000014 | [blank]
000015 | ## 3. Architecture Flow
000016 | The repository is split into distinct tracks. Respect these boundaries and don't create tight coupling where none should exist:
000017 | - **Track A (CLI & Permissions):** Owns the interface, the action registry, permission engine, circuit breaker, and audit log.
000018 | - **Track B (Connectors):** Owns the read-only view into infrastructure. Connectors MUST implement the `Connector` base pattern (`authenticate -> locate -> fetch_logs -> poll_state`). They never hold credentials themselves; they receive them per call.
000019 | - **Track C (Write Actions):** Owns operations that mutate infrastructure (e.g., restarting pods). Must be verifiable and respect the permission model.
000020 | - **Track D (Brain):** Owns diagnosis. It ingests state from connectors and outputs a `Diagnosis` (with an optional `options` list for ambiguity). It has zero ties to a web stack.
000021 | - **Track E (Watcher):** Background process polling connectors to detect anomalies and alert the user.
000022 | [blank]
000023 | ## 4. Documentation & Logging (Zero Exception Rule)
000024 | If it isn't documented, it didn't happen.
000025 | - **PRASH_V2.md:** This is the single source of truth.
000026 |   - New bugs, ideas, or completed milestones MUST be logged in `§10 running log`.
000027 |   - Architectural or cross-track decisions MUST be logged in `§9 decision log`.
000028 | - **CHANGELOG.md:** Any new feature (like adding a new connector or CLI command) MUST be documented in `CHANGELOG.md` as a distinct entry.
000029 | [blank]
000030 | ## 5. Testing
000031 | - Every connector and action needs tests.
000032 | - Since we can't always hit live infrastructure in CI, use robust mocking (e.g., `botocore.stub.Stubber` for AWS).
000033 | - UI flows and permission gates must be tested, especially edge cases like missing credentials or rate limits.
````

000001 | import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
000002 | import Dashboard from './components/Dashboard';
000003 | import Wizard from './components/Wizard';
000004 | import Sidebar from './components/Sidebar';
000005 | import Projects from './components/Projects';

000010 | import NotificationToast from './components/NotificationToast';
000011 | import Chatbot from './components/Chatbot';
000012 | import ChatWorkspace from './components/ChatWorkspace';
000013 | import ErrorBoundary from './components/ErrorBoundary';
000014 | import { LearProvider, useLear } from './context/LearContext';
000015 | [blank]
000016 | function AppContent() {
000017 |   const [isSetupComplete, setIsSetupComplete] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
000018 |   const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
000019 | [blank]
000020 |   const {
000021 |     activeTab,
000022 |     setActiveTab,
000023 |     activeProject,
000024 |     activeEnvironment,
000025 |     refreshProjects,
000026 |     toasts,
000027 |     dismissToast,
000028 |     chatOpen,
000029 |     closeChat,
000030 |     chatContext,
000031 |   } = useLear();
000032 | [blank]
000033 |   const checkConfig = async () => {
000034 |     try {
000035 |       const resConfig = await fetch('/api/config');
000036 |       if (resConfig.ok) {
000037 |         const data = await resConfig.json();
000038 |         const hasConfigured = data.services && Object.keys(data.services).length > 0;
000039 |         setIsSetupComplete(hasConfigured);
000040 |       }
000041 |     } catch (e) {
000042 |       console.error('Error checking setup status:', e);
000043 |       setIsSetupComplete(false);
000044 |     } finally {
000045 |       setLoading(false);
000046 |     }
000047 |   };
000048 | [blank]
000049 |   useEffect(() => {
000050 |     checkConfig();
000051 |     try {
000052 |       const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
000053 |       const tabParam = params.get('tab');
000054 |       if (tabParam) {
000055 |         setActiveTab(tabParam);
000056 |       } else if (params.get('session')) {
000057 |         setActiveTab('chat');
000058 |       }
000059 |     } catch {}
000060 |   }, []);
000061 | [blank]
000062 |   const handleSetupComplete = () => {
000063 |     setIsSetupComplete(true);
000064 |     checkConfig();
000065 |     refreshProjects();
000066 |   };
000067 | [blank]
000068 |   if (loading) {
000069 |     return (
000070 |       <div className="min-h-screen bg-background flex flex-col items-center justify-center text-white space-y-3">
000071 |         <div className="w-8 h-8 rounded-full border-2 border-accent border-t-transparent animate-spin" />
000072 |         <span className="text-xs font-mono text-gray-400">Initializing Lear Intelligence Engine...</span>
000073 |       </div>
000074 |     );
000075 |   }
000076 | [blank]
000077 |   return (
000078 |     <>
000079 |       {!isSetupComplete ? (
000080 |         <Wizard onComplete={handleSetupComplete} />
000081 |       ) : (
000082 |         <div className="flex h-screen w-full relative z-10 overflow-hidden bg-background">
000083 |           <Sidebar />
000084 | [blank]
000085 |           <main className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto">
000086 |             <ErrorBoundary fallbackTitle="View Error" fallbackMessage="There was a problem rendering this section.">
000087 |               {activeTab === 'dashboard' && (
000088 |                 <Dashboard
000089 |                   activeProject={activeProject}
000090 |                   activeEnvironment={activeEnvironment}
000091 |                   onOpenWizard={() => setIsSetupComplete(false)}
000092 |                 />
000093 |               )}
000094 |               {activeTab === 'chat' && <ChatWorkspace />}
000095 |               {activeTab === 'projects' && <Projects />}
000096 |               {activeTab === 'integrations' && <Integrations />}
000097 |               {activeTab === 'activity' && <ActivityLog />}
000098 |               {activeTab === 'notifications' && <Notifications />}
000099 |               {activeTab === 'settings' && (
000100 |                 <Settings onReconfigure={() => setIsSetupComplete(false)} />
000101 |               )}
000102 |             </ErrorBoundary>
000103 |           </main>
000104 | [blank]
000105 |           {/* Global Slide-In Alerts / Toasts */}
000106 |           <NotificationToast toasts={toasts} onDismiss={dismissToast} />
000107 | [blank]
000108 |           {/* Global Lear Copilot Chatbot */}
000109 |           <Chatbot
000110 |             isOpen={chatOpen}
000111 |             onClose={closeChat}
000112 |             serviceContext={chatContext}
000113 |           />
000114 |         </div>
000115 |       )}
000116 |     </>
000117 |   );
000118 | }
000119 | [blank]
000120 | function App() {
000121 |   return (
000122 |     <ErrorBoundary fallbackTitle="Lear Application Error" fallbackMessage="A critical error occurred while loading the application.">
000123 |       <LearProvider>
000124 |         <AppContent />
000125 |       </LearProvider>
000126 |     </ErrorBoundary>
000127 |   );
000128 | }
000129 | [blank]
000130 | export default App;
````

000026 | function renderInlineFormatting(line: string): React.ReactNode[] {
000027 |   const parts: React.ReactNode[] = [];
000028 |   const regex = /(`[^`]+`|\*\*[^*]+\*\*)/g;

000031 | [blank]

000035 |     }
000036 |     const token = match[0];
000037 |     if (token.startsWith('`') && token.endsWith('`')) {
000038 |       const codeText = token.slice(1, -1);
000039 |       parts.push(
000040 |         <code
000041 |           key={`code-${match.index}`}
000042 |           className="px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded bg-black/40 border border-border-subtle text-accent font-mono text-[11px]"
000043 |         >
000044 |           {codeText}
000045 |         </code>
000046 |       );
000047 |     } else if (token.startsWith('**') && token.endsWith('**')) {

000051 |           {boldText}
000052 |         </strong>
000053 |       );
000054 |     }
000055 |     lastIndex = regex.lastIndex;
000056 |   }
000057 | [blank]

000059 |     parts.push(line.substring(lastIndex));
000060 |   }
000061 | [blank]

000001 | import { Component, ErrorInfo, ReactNode } from 'react';
000002 | import { AlertTriangle, RefreshCw } from 'lucide-react';
000003 | [blank]
000004 | interface Props {
000005 |   children: ReactNode;
000006 |   fallbackTitle?: string;
000007 |   fallbackMessage?: string;
000008 | }
000009 | [blank]
000010 | interface State {
000011 |   hasError: boolean;
000012 |   error: Error | null;
000013 | }
000014 | [blank]
000015 | export class ErrorBoundary extends Component<Props, State> {
000016 |   public state: State = {
000017 |     hasError: false,
000018 |     error: null,
000019 |   };
000020 | [blank]
000021 |   public static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error): State {
000022 |     return { hasError: true, error };
000023 |   }
000024 | [blank]
000025 |   public componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) {
000026 |     console.error('Uncaught error in component tree:', error, errorInfo);
000027 |   }
000028 | [blank]
000029 |   private handleReset = () => {
000030 |     this.setState({ hasError: false, error: null });
000031 |   };
000032 | [blank]
000033 |   public render() {
000034 |     if (this.state.hasError) {
000035 |       return (
000036 |         <div className="p-6 rounded-2xl bg-surface/80 border border-rose-500/30 text-white my-4 max-w-2xl mx-auto shadow-2xl backdrop-blur-md">

000038 |             <div className="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-rose-500/10 border border-rose-500/30 flex items-center justify-center text-rose-400 shrink-0">

000040 |             </div>
000041 |             <div className="flex-1">
000042 |               <h3 className="text-base font-bold text-rose-200">
000043 |                 {this.props.fallbackTitle || 'Component Error'}
000044 |               </h3>
000045 |               <p className="text-xs text-gray-300 mt-1 mb-3">
000046 |                 {this.props.fallbackMessage || 'An unexpected rendering error occurred in this view.'}
000047 |               </p>
000048 |               {this.state.error && (
000049 |                 <pre className="text-[11px] font-mono bg-background/80 p-3 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle text-rose-300 overflow-x-auto max-h-32 mb-4">
000050 |                   {this.state.error.message || String(this.state.error)}
000051 |                 </pre>
000052 |               )}
000053 |               <button
000054 |                 onClick={this.handleReset}
000055 |                 className="flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 rounded-lg bg-accent text-gray-950 font-bold text-xs hover:bg-accent-light transition-all cursor-pointer shadow"
000056 |               >
000057 |                 <RefreshCw size={13} /> Try Again
000058 |               </button>
000059 |             </div>
000060 |           </div>
000061 |         </div>
000062 |       );
000063 |     }
000064 | [blank]
000065 |     return this.props.children;
000066 |   }
000067 | }
000068 | [blank]
000069 | export default ErrorBoundary;

000013 | export const MetricCard: React.FC<MetricCardProps> = ({

000016 |   unit = '',
000017 |   change,
000018 |   history,
000019 |   icon,
000020 | }) => {

000022 | [blank]

000032 |     points = history.map((val, i) => {

000036 |     }).join(' ');

### `evals/README.md`
````text
000001 | # Prash Eval Harness — Golden Benchmark
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Ported from `prash-backend/evals/` (2026-08-09, Track D day 3). A reproducible
000004 | benchmark built from real production runs. Use it to gate every prompt / model /
000005 | schema change to the diagnosis brain: run before and after, compare scorecards.
000006 | [blank]
000007 | ## Why this exists
000008 | [blank]
000009 | Track D (days 4-8) extends the `Diagnosis` schema with runtime categories and
000010 | teaches the brain Kubernetes — a domain it has never seen (69 CI-specific
000011 | references in the prompt, zero runtime ones). Without this harness there is no
000012 | way to tell whether that work made CI diagnosis quality better, worse, or just
000013 | different. Every change to `prash/brain/` gets run through this before it's
000014 | considered done.
000015 | [blank]
000016 | ## Layout
000017 | [blank]
000018 | ```
000019 | evals/
000020 |   cases/            # golden cases (one JSON per run), ported from v1 verbatim
000021 |   score.py          # scoring rubric + scorecard rendering (zero external deps)
000022 |   run_eval.py       # replay cases through diagnose_failure(), score, write results
000023 |   results/          # scorecards per run (gitignored, except the baseline below)
000024 | ```
000025 | [blank]
000026 | ## The pre-Track-D baseline
000027 | [blank]
000028 | `results/2026-08-09-pre-track-d-port-baseline.json` was captured against the
000029 | **unmodified v1 brain** (still running in `prash-backend`, not yet ported here),
000030 | model `deepseek-v4-flash`, on 2026-08-09 — before any Track D schema/prompt
000031 | changes. 15/15 cases, 100% valid_diagnosis, 100% category accuracy, 93.3%
000032 | actionability, 86.7% fix_type accuracy, file_recall 1.0. Diff every future run
000033 | against this to catch regressions from the schema extension and Kubernetes
000034 | prompt work:
000035 | [blank]
000036 | ```bash
000037 | python -m evals.run_eval --baseline evals/results/2026-08-09-pre-track-d-port-baseline.json
000038 | ```
000039 | [blank]
000040 | ## Not runnable yet
000041 | [blank]
000042 | `run_eval.py` imports `prash.brain.diagnosis_agent` / `prash.brain.kimi_client`,
000043 | which don't exist until Track D days 4-5 port the brain (see `PRASH_V2.md` §6).
000044 | Ported now, checked in, and wired to the right import paths so it's ready to run
000045 | the moment the brain lands — porting the harness twice would be wasted work.
000046 | [blank]
000047 | ## What did NOT get ported
000048 | [blank]
000049 | `seed_from_db.py` — it pulls new golden cases from v1's Supabase, and v2 has no
000050 | database by design (§4). Cases are portable data (just JSON), so they moved over;
000051 | the seeding mechanism stays a v1-only operational tool. To add a new case here,
000052 | either hand-author one (see v1's `evals/README.md` for the exact JSON shape) or
000053 | run v1's `seed_from_db.py` there and copy the resulting file into `evals/cases/`.
000054 | [blank]
000055 | ## Running
000056 | [blank]
000057 | ```bash
000058 | # full run against the ported brain, once Track D lands it
000059 | python -m evals.run_eval
000060 | [blank]
000061 | # quick smoke (2 cases)
000062 | python -m evals.run_eval --limit 2
000063 | [blank]
000064 | # compare against the pre-port baseline
000065 | python -m evals.run_eval --baseline evals/results/2026-08-09-pre-track-d-port-baseline.json
000066 | ```
000067 | [blank]
000068 | By default the harness runs the **single-shot path** (files supplied in-prompt,
000069 | no GitHub calls) — reproducible and isolates model + prompt + schema quality.
000070 | `--live` adds the real investigation loop, matching how `prash fix` actually
000071 | runs, but needs `GH_TOKEN`.
000072 | [blank]
000073 | `agent_calls`-equivalent logging is monkeypatched to a no-op before import, so
000074 | eval runs never write to anywhere persistent.
000075 | [blank]
000076 | ## Known limitations (inherited from v1, still true here)
000077 | [blank]
000078 | 1. **Category coverage is biased.** The golden set only has ground truth for
000079 |    `code` and `dependency` (13 of 15 cases) plus one `workflow_config` case.
000080 |    `environment` has zero cases. This harness cannot yet measure whether the
000081 |    Kubernetes work (a brand-new category Track D is adding) is any good —
000082 |    **hand-authoring `environment`/runtime-category cases is part of days 6-8,
000083 |    not optional polish.**
000084 | 2. **~60-70% of v1's production traffic was internal smoke testing** (per v1's
000085 |    README) — the case set reflects that skew.
000086 | 3. **Single-shot ≠ the real `prash fix` path**, which runs the full investigation
000087 |    loop. Use `--live` periodically to catch loop-specific regressions.
````

### `evals/run_eval.py`
````text
000001 | """
000002 | Golden-benchmark runner — ported from prash-backend/evals/run_eval.py (2026-08-09).
000003 | [blank]
000004 | Replays every case in evals/cases/ through the CURRENT diagnose_failure() pipeline
000005 | and scores the output against the known-good outcome. Use it to gate every prompt /
000006 | model / schema change: run it before and after, compare the scorecards.
000007 | [blank]
000008 |     python -m evals.run_eval                      # full run, current model
000009 |     python -m evals.run_eval --limit 5            # quick smoke
000010 |     python -m evals.run_eval --concurrency 4      # parallelize model calls
000011 |     python -m evals.run_eval --baseline evals/results/2026-08-09-pre-track-d-port-baseline.json
000012 | [blank]
000013 | Runnable since Track D days 4-5 ported prash.brain.diagnosis_agent /
000014 | prash.brain.kimi_client. The baseline in evals/results/ was captured against
000015 | the UNMODIFIED v1 brain (prash-backend, deepseek-v4-flash) on 2026-08-09,
000016 | before any Track D changes -- diff every future run against it with
000017 | --baseline. A second checkpoint, 2026-08-09-post-track-d-port.json, was
000018 | captured right after the days 4-5 port (zero regression) and right before
000019 | days 6-8 taught the prompt Kubernetes -- diff against that one specifically
000020 | to isolate what the Kubernetes prompt work changed, vs. what the port itself
000021 | changed (nothing).
000022 | """
000023 | from __future__ import annotations
000024 | [blank]
000025 | import argparse
000026 | import asyncio
000027 | import json
000028 | import os
000029 | import time
000030 | from datetime import datetime, timezone
000031 | from pathlib import Path
000032 | [blank]
000033 | # ── neutralize prod side effects BEFORE importing the pipeline ────────────────
000034 | import prash.brain.kimi_client as _kc
000035 | [blank]
000036 | _kc._log_agent_call = lambda *a, **k: None          # don't write to agent_calls
000037 | _kc.mark_agent_run_outcome = lambda *a, **k: None
000038 | [blank]
000039 | from evals.score import CaseResult, aggregate, render_scorecard
000040 | from prash.brain.diagnosis_agent import diagnose_failure
000041 | from prash.brain.kimi_client import DiagnosisValidationError
000042 | from prash.credentials import CredentialStore
000043 | [blank]
000044 | CASES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "cases"
000045 | RESULTS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "results"
000046 | [blank]
000047 | # Keys kimi_client.py reads straight from the process environment (see its
000048 | # lazy singleton getters), not passed through as function arguments -- same

000057 | def load_env_credentials() -> None:
000058 |     """Load .env's model API keys into the process environment before any

000063 |     running it in a shell that hadn't already exported DEEPSEEK_API_KEY/
000064 |     KIMI_API_KEY silently fell back to whichever client had no key at all,
000065 |     which reads as a near-total model failure rather than a missing
000066 |     credential. See PRASH_V2.md §10.

000068 |     creds = CredentialStore.from_env().load()
000069 |     for key in _BRAIN_ENV_PASSTHROUGH:

000129 | async def main_async(args) -> None:

000132 |         print(f"No cases in {CASES_DIR}.")

000134 | [blank]

000136 |     sem = asyncio.Semaphore(args.concurrency)
000137 | [blank]
000138 |     async def _guarded(c):
000139 |         async with sem:
000140 |             r = await run_case(c, args.live, args.gh_token, model=args.model)
000141 |             mark = "✓" if r.valid_diagnosis else "✗"
000142 |             print(f"  {mark} {r.case_id} ({r.source})  {r.latency_ms}ms"
000143 |                   + (f"  cat={r.predicted_category}/{r.expected_category}" if r.valid_diagnosis and r.source == "verified" else ""))
000144 |             return r

000146 |     results = await asyncio.gather(*[_guarded(c) for c in cases])

000162 | def _print_diff(baseline: dict, current: dict) -> None:
000163 |     b = baseline["aggregate"]
000164 |     print("\n── DIFF vs baseline " + baseline.get("label", "?") + " ──")
000165 |     pairs = [
000166 |         ("valid_diagnosis_rate_pct", current["valid_diagnosis_rate_pct"], b["valid_diagnosis_rate_pct"]),
000167 |         ("category_acc", current["verified_cohort"]["category_accuracy_pct"], b["verified_cohort"]["category_accuracy_pct"]),
000168 |         ("actionability", current["verified_cohort"]["actionability_pct"], b["verified_cohort"]["actionability_pct"]),
000169 |         ("file_recall", current["verified_cohort"]["mean_file_recall"], b["verified_cohort"]["mean_file_recall"]),
000170 |         ("latency_p90", current["latency_ms"]["p90"], b["latency_ms"]["p90"]),
000171 |     ]
000172 |     for name, cur, base in pairs:
000173 |         if cur is None or base is None:
000174 |             continue
000175 |         delta = round(cur - base, 2)
000176 |         arrow = "▲" if delta > 0 else ("▼" if delta < 0 else "=")
000177 |         print(f"   {name:20} {base} → {cur}  {arrow}{abs(delta)}")

### `evals/score.py`
````text
000001 | """Scoring rubric for the golden benchmark.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | The metrics are deliberately ordered by what the production data says matters most:
000004 | [blank]
000005 |   1. valid_diagnosis  — did the model return a schema-valid Diagnosis at all?
000006 |                         (29% of prod runs die here — this is the headline number)
000007 |   2. category_match   — correct failure classification (drives routing)
000008 |   3. actionability    — did it produce a fix when a fix was the right call?
000009 |   4. file_recall      — did it target the right file(s)?
000010 |   5. fix_type_match   — exact fix_type agreement (softer signal)
000011 |   6. latency_ms       — wall-clock per diagnosis
000012 | [blank]
000013 | Ground truth is only trusted for cases with source == "verified". Negative cases
000014 | score only `valid_diagnosis` (we have no known-good fix for them).
000015 | [blank]
000016 | Track D days 6-8 adds a 7th metric, recommended_action_match, scoped to its own
000017 | "runtime cohort" (cases with expected category="runtime") rather than mixed into
000018 | the main verified cohort -- for CI cases recommended_action is always null/null,
000019 | which would trivially "match" and dilute the number rather than measure anything.
000020 | """
000021 | from __future__ import annotations
000022 | [blank]
000023 | from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
000024 | [blank]
000025 | [blank]
000026 | @dataclass
000027 | class CaseResult:
000028 |     case_id: str
000029 |     source: str
000030 |     valid_diagnosis: bool
000031 |     error: str | None = None
000032 |     latency_ms: int | None = None
000033 | [blank]
000034 |     # populated only when a diagnosis was produced
000035 |     predicted_category: str | None = None
000036 |     expected_category: str | None = None
000037 |     predicted_fix_type: str | None = None
000038 |     expected_fix_type: str | None = None
000039 |     produced_files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
000040 |     expected_files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
000041 |     predicted_recommended_action: str | None = None
000042 |     expected_recommended_action: str | None = None
000043 | [blank]
000044 |     # derived
000045 |     category_match: bool | None = None
000046 |     fix_type_match: bool | None = None
000047 |     actionable_match: bool | None = None
000048 |     file_recall: float | None = None
000049 |     recommended_action_match: bool | None = None
000050 | [blank]
000051 |     def score(self) -> CaseResult:
000052 |         if not self.valid_diagnosis or self.source != "verified":
000053 |             return self
000054 |         self.category_match = self.predicted_category == self.expected_category
000055 |         self.fix_type_match = self.predicted_fix_type == self.expected_fix_type
000056 |         # "actionable" = both sides agree on whether a code fix should exist
000057 |         exp_actionable = self.expected_fix_type in ("safe_auto_apply", "review_recommended")
000058 |         got_actionable = bool(self.produced_files)
000059 |         self.actionable_match = exp_actionable == got_actionable
000060 |         if self.expected_files:
000061 |             hit = sum(1 for p in self.expected_files if p in self.produced_files)
000062 |             self.file_recall = round(hit / len(self.expected_files), 3)
000063 |         if self.expected_category == "runtime":
000064 |             self.recommended_action_match = self.predicted_recommended_action == self.expected_recommended_action
000065 |         return self
000066 | [blank]
000067 |     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
000068 |         return asdict(self)
000069 | [blank]
000070 | [blank]
000071 | def aggregate(results: list[CaseResult]) -> dict:
000072 |     n = len(results)
000073 |     verified = [r for r in results if r.source == "verified"]
000074 |     diagnosed = [r for r in results if r.valid_diagnosis]
000075 |     ver_diag = [r for r in verified if r.valid_diagnosis]
000076 |     runtime_diag = [r for r in ver_diag if r.expected_category == "runtime"]
000077 | [blank]
000078 |     def pct(num, den):
000079 |         return round(100 * num / den, 1) if den else None
000080 | [blank]
000081 |     lats = [r.latency_ms for r in results if r.latency_ms is not None]
000082 |     lats.sort()
000083 | [blank]
000084 |     def p(q):
000085 |         return lats[min(int(len(lats) * q), len(lats) - 1)] if lats else None
000086 | [blank]
000087 |     file_recalls = [r.file_recall for r in ver_diag if r.file_recall is not None]
000088 | [blank]
000089 |     agg = {
000090 |         "n_cases": n,
000091 |         "valid_diagnosis_rate_pct": pct(len(diagnosed), n),          # <- headline
000092 |         "verified_cohort": {
000093 |             "n": len(verified),
000094 |             "valid_diagnosis_pct": pct(len(ver_diag), len(verified)),
000095 |             "category_accuracy_pct": pct(sum(1 for r in ver_diag if r.category_match), len(ver_diag)),
000096 |             "actionability_pct": pct(sum(1 for r in ver_diag if r.actionable_match), len(ver_diag)),
000097 |             "fix_type_accuracy_pct": pct(sum(1 for r in ver_diag if r.fix_type_match), len(ver_diag)),
000098 |             "mean_file_recall": round(sum(file_recalls) / len(file_recalls), 3) if file_recalls else None,
000099 |         },
000100 |         "latency_ms": {"p50": p(0.5), "p90": p(0.9), "max": lats[-1] if lats else None},
000101 |         "errors": [{"case": r.case_id, "error": r.error} for r in results if not r.valid_diagnosis],
000102 |     }
000103 |     if runtime_diag:
000104 |         agg["runtime_cohort"] = {
000105 |             "n": len(runtime_diag),
000106 |             "recommended_action_accuracy_pct": pct(
000107 |                 sum(1 for r in runtime_diag if r.recommended_action_match), len(runtime_diag)
000108 |             ),
000109 |         }
000110 |     return agg
000111 | [blank]
000112 | [blank]
000113 | def render_scorecard(agg: dict, label: str) -> str:
000114 |     vc = agg["verified_cohort"]
000115 |     lat = agg["latency_ms"]
000116 |     lines = [
000117 |         f"\n┌─ EVAL SCORECARD — {label} " + "─" * max(0, 40 - len(label)),
000118 |         f"│ cases: {agg['n_cases']}   valid_diagnosis: {agg['valid_diagnosis_rate_pct']}%   "
000119 |         f"(THE headline metric — prod is ~71%)",
000120 |         f"│ verified cohort (n={vc['n']}):",
000121 |         f"│    valid_diagnosis : {vc['valid_diagnosis_pct']}%",
000122 |         f"│    category_acc    : {vc['category_accuracy_pct']}%",
000123 |         f"│    actionability   : {vc['actionability_pct']}%   (produced a fix when one was expected)",
000124 |         f"│    fix_type_acc    : {vc['fix_type_accuracy_pct']}%",
000125 |         f"│    file_recall     : {vc['mean_file_recall']}",
000126 |         f"│ latency: p50={lat['p50']}ms  p90={lat['p90']}ms  max={lat['max']}ms",
000127 |         f"│ failures: {len(agg['errors'])}",
000128 |     ]
000129 |     if "runtime_cohort" in agg:
000130 |         rc = agg["runtime_cohort"]
000131 |         lines.append(f"│ runtime cohort (n={rc['n']}): recommended_action_acc: {rc['recommended_action_accuracy_pct']}%")
000132 |     lines.append("└" + "─" * 50)
000133 |     for e in agg["errors"]:
000134 |         lines.append(f"   ✗ {e['case']}: {e['error']}")
000135 |     return "\n".join(lines)
````

000001 | """Action: apply-ci-fix.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Closes the gap found live-testing `prash fix --ci` (PRASH_V2.md §9,
000004 | 2026-08-15, CROSS-TRACK entry): the CI multi-failure path diagnosed real
000005 | problems and proposed real file changes, but never actually did anything
000006 | with them -- the "Fixed X of N" headline was true only in the sense that
000007 | the model had *proposed* a fix, not that one existed anywhere.
000008 | [blank]
000009 | This is the first action where Prash writes AI-generated code into a real
000010 | repository, rather than reading state or acting on infrastructure that
000011 | already exists (restart-pod, rollback) or opening a PR between two branches
000012 | that already exist (open-pr). No local git clone: everything goes through
000013 | GitHub's Git Data API, which `GitHubConnector` already has the plumbing for.
000014 | """
000015 | [blank]

000017 | [blank]
000018 | from typing import Any
000019 | [blank]

000022 |     Action,
000023 |     ActionContext,
000024 |     ActionResult,
000025 |     ActionResultStatus,
000026 |     ActionSpec,
000027 |     Plan,
000028 |     PlanStep,
000029 |     RiskTier,
000030 |     VerificationResult,
000031 | )
000032 | [blank]
000033 | [blank]
000034 | class _ApplyFixBase(Action):
000035 |     """Shared implementation: turn a diagnosis's proposed file changes into a
000036 |     real branch + commit + pull request, entirely over GitHub's Git Data API.
000037 | [blank]
000038 |     Subclasses differ only in identity (action id, so the audit log says
000039 |     honestly what happened), branch naming, and the wording of the PR. The
000040 |     actual write path is identical -- a CI fix and a Kubernetes manifest fix
000041 |     are the same operation on different files.
000042 |     """
000043 | [blank]
000044 |     _source_label = "diagnosis"
000045 | [blank]
000046 |     def _github(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> GitHubConnector:
000047 |         return ctx.extra["connectors"]["github"]
000048 | [blank]
000049 |     def _branch_name(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> str:
000050 |         return "prash/fix"
000051 | [blank]
000052 |     def _file_changes(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> list[Any]:
000053 |         # Every entry here has either `edits` or `new_content` populated --
000054 |         # guaranteed by FileChange's own model validator (prash/brain/schemas.py).
000055 |         return ctx.extra.get("file_changes", [])
000056 | [blank]

000060 |         changes = self._file_changes(ctx)
000061 |         steps = [

000063 |             PlanStep(description=f"Create branch '{branch}' from the default branch"),
000064 |         ]
000065 |         for fc in changes:
000066 |             steps.append(PlanStep(description=f"Write {fc.path}", impact=fc.explanation))
000067 |         steps.append(PlanStep(description=f"Open pull request '{branch}' -> default branch"))
000068 |         return Plan(action_id=self.spec.id, reversible=True, risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier, steps=steps)

000071 |         gh = self._github(ctx)
000072 |         if not gh.authenticate():

000075 |                 summary="GitHub authentication failed (GITHUB_TOKEN missing or invalid)",
000076 |             )
000077 | [blank]
000078 |         changes = self._file_changes(ctx)
000079 |         if not changes:
000080 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="no file changes with content to apply")
000081 | [blank]
000082 |         repo = ctx.target.resource
000083 |         branch = self._branch_name(ctx)
000084 | [blank]
000085 |         try:
000086 |             base_branch = gh.get_repo(repo)["default_branch"]
000087 |             base_sha = gh.get_branch_head_sha(repo, base_branch)
000088 |             base_tree_sha = gh.get_commit_tree_sha(repo, base_sha)
000089 | [blank]
000090 |             entries = []
000091 |             for fc in changes:
000092 |                 # edits apply against the file's real current content, fetched fresh
000093 |                 # against base_sha -- this is what guarantees anything the model
000094 |                 # didn't explicitly edit survives untouched, unlike trusting a
000095 |                 # regenerated new_content to be a faithful complete file (the bug
000096 |                 # found live 2026-08-16/17: two verification PRs each contained the
000097 |                 # correct fix plus unrequested deletions elsewhere in the file).
000098 |                 original = gh.get_file_content(repo, fc.path, base_sha) if fc.edits else None
000099 |                 content = fc.apply(original)
000100 |                 blob_sha = gh.create_blob(repo, content)
000101 |                 entries.append({"path": fc.path, "mode": "100644", "type": "blob", "sha": blob_sha})
000102 |             new_tree_sha = gh.create_tree(repo, base_tree_sha, entries)
000103 | [blank]
000104 |             message = ctx.extra.get("commit_message") or f"Prash: fix {len(changes)} file(s) from {self._source_label}"
000105 |             commit_sha = gh.create_commit(repo, message, new_tree_sha, base_sha)
000106 | [blank]
000107 |             gh.create_ref(repo, branch, commit_sha)
000108 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — report honestly, never fake a fix
000109 |             detail = str(exc)
000110 |             if "Reference already exists" in detail:
000111 |                 return ActionResult(
000112 |                     status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED,
000113 |                     summary=f"a fix was already proposed on branch '{branch}' — check for an existing PR before retrying",
000114 |                 )
000115 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"could not write the fix commit: {exc}")
000116 | [blank]
000117 |         title = ctx.extra.get("title") or f"Prash: fix {len(changes)} file(s) from {self._source_label}"
000118 |         body = ctx.extra.get("body") or (
000119 |             f"Automated fix by Prash, from a {self._source_label}.\n\n"
000120 |             + "\n".join(f"- `{fc.path}`: {fc.explanation}" for fc in changes)
000121 |         )
000122 |         try:

000124 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001

000130 | [blank]
000131 |         return ActionResult(

000133 |             summary=f"opened PR #{pr['number']} with {len(changes)} file(s): {pr['html_url']}",
000134 |             detail={"pr_number": pr["number"], "html_url": pr["html_url"], "branch": branch},
000135 |         )

000138 |         if "pr_number" not in result.detail:

000142 |         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001

000178 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.SAFE,
