### `prash/actions/contract.py`
````text
000001 | """The Lear action contract.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | This is the Days 1-2 shared foundation. Every action in the system must
000004 | implement this contract, and every permission engine decision is made against
000005 | it. Nothing about the contract is web-stack-specific; it ports to any agent
000006 | body.
000007 | [blank]
000008 | The contract answers five questions for every action:
000009 | [blank]
000010 | 1. What does it do?           -> Action.summary / Action.plan
000011 | 2. What is its risk tier?     -> Action.spec.risk_tier
000012 | 3. Is it reversible?          -> Action.spec.reversible
000013 | 4. How do you dry-run it?     -> Action.dry_run (never touches infrastructure)
000014 | 5. How do you verify it?      -> Action.verify (checks reality afterward)
000015 | """
000016 | [blank]
000017 | from __future__ import annotations
000018 | [blank]
000019 | import abc
000020 | import enum
000021 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
000022 | from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
000023 | [blank]
000024 | [blank]
000025 | class RiskTier(enum.Enum):
000026 |     """Risk classification used by the permission engine.
000027 | [blank]
000028 |     SAFE:      can run without asking in permissive modes (re-run a job,
000029 |                restart a crash-looping pod, open a fix PR, request a secret).
000030 |     APPROVAL:  always requires an explicit per-action grant, even in bypass
000031 |                mode (rollback, scale, config change).
000032 |     NEVER:     never executed in v1, unconditionally refused (migrations,
000033 |                data destruction, production without an explicit per-action
000034 |                grant).
000035 |     """
000036 | [blank]
000037 |     SAFE = "safe"
000038 |     APPROVAL = "approval"
000039 |     NEVER = "never"
000040 | [blank]
000041 | [blank]
000042 | class Decision(enum.Enum):
000043 |     """The permission engine's verdict for a requested action."""
000044 | [blank]
000045 |     ALLOW = "allow"
000046 |     PROMPT = "prompt"
000047 |     REFUSE = "refuse"
000048 | [blank]
000049 | [blank]
000050 | class ActionResultStatus(enum.Enum):
000051 |     SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
000052 |     FAILED = "failed"
000053 |     NEEDS_APPROVAL = "needs_approval"
000054 |     NEEDS_INPUT = "needs_input"
000055 |     SKIPPED = "skipped"
000056 | [blank]
000057 | [blank]
000058 | @dataclass(frozen=True)
000059 | class ActionSpec:
000060 |     """Static description of an action. Decided once, in code, never at runtime."""
000061 | [blank]
000062 |     id: str
000063 |     summary: str
000064 |     risk_tier: RiskTier
000065 |     reversible: bool
000066 |     capabilities: tuple[str, ...] = ()
000067 |     approval_hint: str = ""
000068 | [blank]
000069 |     @property
000070 |     def always_asks(self) -> bool:
000071 |         return self.risk_tier in (RiskTier.APPROVAL, RiskTier.NEVER)
000072 | [blank]
000073 | [blank]
000074 | @dataclass
000075 | class Target:
000076 |     """What the action is acting on, and where.
000077 | [blank]
000078 |     ``environment`` drives environment-scoped permission mode (staging is
000079 |     auto, production always prompts).
000080 |     """
000081 | [blank]
000082 |     resource: str
000083 |     environment: str = "staging"
000084 |     labels: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
000085 | [blank]
000086 | [blank]
000087 | @dataclass
000088 | class ActionContext:
000089 |     """Everything an action needs to plan, act, and verify."""
000090 | [blank]
000091 |     target: Target
000092 |     credentials: Dict[str, Any]
000093 |     secrets: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
000094 |     dry_run: bool = False
000095 |     grant: bool = False
000096 |     extra: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
000097 | [blank]
000098 | [blank]
000099 | @dataclass
000100 | class PlanStep:
000101 |     description: str
000102 |     impact: str = ""
000103 |     dry_run_only: bool = False
000104 | [blank]
000105 | [blank]
000106 | @dataclass
000107 | class Plan:
000108 |     """What the action intends to do. Shown to the user before any approval."""
000109 | [blank]
000110 |     action_id: str
000111 |     steps: list[PlanStep]
000112 |     reversible: bool
000113 |     risk_tier: RiskTier
000114 | [blank]
000115 |     def describe(self) -> str:
000116 |         return "\n".join(f"- {s.description}" + (f" [{s.impact}]" if s.impact else "") for s in self.steps)
000117 | [blank]
000118 | [blank]
000119 | @dataclass
000120 | class VerificationResult:
000121 |     ok: bool
000122 |     detail: str = ""
000123 | [blank]
000124 | [blank]
000125 | @dataclass
000126 | class ActionResult:
000127 |     status: ActionResultStatus
000128 |     summary: str
000129 |     verification: Optional[VerificationResult] = None
000130 |     detail: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
000131 | [blank]
000132 | [blank]
000133 | class Action(abc.ABC):
000134 |     """Base class every Prash action implements."""
000135 | [blank]
000136 |     spec: ActionSpec
000137 | [blank]
000138 |     @abc.abstractmethod
000139 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000140 |         """Return the intended steps. Must not touch infrastructure."""
000141 | [blank]
000142 |     @abc.abstractmethod
000143 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000144 |         """Perform the action against the target using ctx.credentials."""
000145 | [blank]
000146 |     @abc.abstractmethod
000147 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000148 |         """Check whether the action actually worked. Reports honestly if not."""
000149 | [blank]
000150 |     def dry_run(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000151 |         """The dry-run contract: plan without executing a single write."""
000152 |         ctx = ActionContext(**{**vars(ctx), "dry_run": True})
000153 |         return self.plan(ctx)
000154 | [blank]
000155 |     def ask_for_secret(self, name: str, hint: str = "") -> str:
000156 |         """Raise a structured request for a missing secret value.
000157 | [blank]
000158 |         Track C #1 depends on this: Prash can *ask* for the value rather than
000159 |         dead-ending on ``needs_secret``.
000160 |         """
000161 |         raise MissingSecretError(name=name, hint=hint)
000162 | [blank]
000163 | [blank]
000164 | class MissingSecretError(Exception):
000165 |     """Raised when an action needs a secret the user has not supplied."""
000166 | [blank]
000167 |     def __init__(self, name: str, hint: str = ""):
000168 |         self.name = name
000169 |         self.hint = hint
000170 |         super().__init__(f"missing secret: {name}")
````

````text
000001 | """Action: datadog-alert (CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC §4b, milestone M4).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | APPROVAL tier: posting an event is outbound and team-visible -- the whole
000004 | point is that the team sees it in Datadog's event stream -- and Datadog's
000005 | API has no event deletion, so it can't be cleanly reversed. That's the

000027 |     VerificationResult,

000041 |     @staticmethod

000044 |         if isinstance(extra_tags, str):
000045 |             tags = [tag.strip() for tag in extra_tags.split(",") if tag.strip()]
000046 |         elif isinstance(extra_tags, (list, tuple)):
000047 |             tags = [str(tag).strip() for tag in extra_tags if str(tag).strip()]
000048 |         else:
000049 |             tags = []
000050 |         return tags or None
000051 | [blank]
000052 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000053 |         title = ctx.extra.get("title") or f"Prash alert: {ctx.target.resource}"
000054 |         priority = ctx.extra.get("priority") or "normal"
000055 |         tags = self._tags(ctx.extra.get("tags"))
000056 |         return Plan(
000057 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000058 |             reversible=False,
000059 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000060 |             steps=[
000061 |                 PlanStep(
000062 |                     description=f"Post Datadog event '{title}' (priority {priority})"
000063 |                     + (f" tagged {', '.join(tags)}" if tags else ""),
000064 |                     impact=f"Visible to the whole team in the Datadog event stream; events cannot be deleted via the API",
000065 |                 )
000066 |             ],
000067 |         )
000068 | [blank]
000069 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000070 |         dd = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("datadog")
000071 |         if not dd:
000072 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="Datadog connector is missing or not configured.")
000073 |         title = ctx.extra.get("title") or f"Prash alert: {ctx.target.resource}"
000074 |         text = ctx.extra.get("text") or ctx.extra.get("message") or ctx.target.resource
000075 |         priority = ctx.extra.get("priority") or "normal"
000076 |         tags = self._tags(ctx.extra.get("tags"))
000077 |         try:
000078 |             resp = dd.post_event(title, text, tags=tags, priority=priority)
000079 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
000080 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"alert failed: {exc}")
000081 |         event_id = ""
000082 |         if isinstance(resp, dict):
000083 |             event_id = str((resp.get("data") or {}).get("id") or "")
000084 |         return ActionResult(
000085 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000086 |             summary=f"Datadog event '{title}' posted" + (f" (event id {event_id})" if event_id else ""),
000087 |             detail={"event_id": event_id, "title": title, "priority": priority, "tags": tags or []},
000088 |         )
000089 | [blank]
000090 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000091 |         dd = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("datadog")
000092 |         if not dd:
000093 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail="could not verify: Datadog connector missing")
000094 |         event_id = result.detail.get("event_id")

000097 |             # returned one; without it there is nothing to confirm.
000098 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail="could not verify: no event id was returned")
000099 | [blank]
000100 |         def _matches(resp: object) -> bool:
000101 |             """The GET-by-id returning a payload proves existence; Datadog 404s
000102 |             when an event is absent. Identity is checked when the id is visible:
000103 |             v1 intake echoes the numeric id as data.id, while v2 GET of the same

000106 |             if not isinstance(resp, dict) or not resp.get("data"):

000109 |             if str(data.get("id") or "") == str(event_id):
000110 |                 return True
000111 |             nested = data.get("attributes") or {}
000112 |             evt = nested.get("attributes", {}).get("evt", {}) if isinstance(nested, dict) else {}
000113 |             return str(evt.get("id") or "") == str(event_id)
000114 | [blank]
000115 |         # Found live (2026-09-07): a just-posted event is not queryable for a
000116 |         # few seconds (intake -> searchability propagation), so the first GET
000117 |         # can 404 while the event exists. Bounded retry: confirm as soon as
000118 |         # reality catches up; if it never does, report exactly that instead
000119 |         # of claiming a verified success.
000120 |         last = ""
000121 |         for attempt in range(3):
000122 |             try:
000123 |                 resp = dd.get_event(event_id)
000124 |             except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
000125 |                 last = f"event {event_id} not found: {exc}"
000126 |                 if attempt < 2:
000127 |                     time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
000128 |                 continue
000129 |             if _matches(resp):
000130 |                 return VerificationResult(ok=True, detail=f"event {event_id} exists in the Datadog event stream")
000131 |             last = f"event {event_id} not found in Datadog (may still be propagating)"
000132 |             if attempt < 2:
000133 |                 time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
000134 |         return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail=last)
````

### `prash/actions/exec_command.py`
````text
000001 | """Action: exec (Track C, sprint-2 Kubernetes Depth, PRASH_V2.md §7b).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Last piece of "Kubernetes Actions." Deliberately different in kind from
000004 | restart-pod/rollback/scale/edit-configmap/edit-secret, not just in degree:
000005 | every other action here does one well-defined Kubernetes API mutation.
000006 | This runs an arbitrary command inside a live container -- unbounded blast
000007 | radius, bounded only by what the container's own user and filesystem
000008 | permit. Discussed explicitly with Aradhya before building (2026-08-17,
000009 | PRASH_V2.md §9): scoped to RiskTier.APPROVAL, same permission pattern as
000010 | every other action here, no command allowlist and no automated-brain
000011 | carve-out -- the permission system is the safety net, consistent with how
000012 | this whole action model already works. A stricter posture (restricted
000013 | command set, keeping it out of brain-automated paths) was considered and
000014 | explicitly not chosen for this first version.
000015 | [blank]
000016 | Wired to Track B's Kubernetes connector (prash/connectors/kubernetes.py,
000017 | owned by Aradhya) -- same split as every other action: the connector runs
000018 | the single operation, this action owns planning, permission gating, and
000019 | verification.
000020 | """
000021 | [blank]
000022 | from __future__ import annotations
000023 | [blank]
000024 | from ..connectors.kubernetes import exec_in_pod, get_pod_status
000025 | from .contract import (
000026 |     Action,
000027 |     ActionContext,
000028 |     ActionResult,
000029 |     ActionResultStatus,
000030 |     ActionSpec,
000031 |     Plan,
000032 |     PlanStep,
000033 |     RiskTier,
000034 |     VerificationResult,
000035 | )
000036 | [blank]
000037 | # Same cap as the connector's own truncation -- keeps the summary/detail
000038 | # shown to the user (and written to the audit log) bounded even if the
000039 | # connector layer's cap is ever changed independently.
000040 | _SUMMARY_OUTPUT_PREVIEW = 500
000041 | [blank]
000042 | [blank]
000043 | class ExecAction(Action):
000044 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000045 |         id="exec",
000046 |         summary="Run a command inside a pod and capture its output",
000047 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.APPROVAL,
000048 |         reversible=False,
000049 |         capabilities=("exec_in_pod",),
000050 |         approval_hint="Always prompts, even in bypass mode -- this runs anything the container's own permissions allow, the highest blast-radius action Prash has.",
000051 |     )
000052 | [blank]
000053 |     def _split(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> tuple[str, str]:
000054 |         namespace, _, pod = ctx.target.resource.partition("/")
000055 |         return (namespace or "default", pod)
000056 | [blank]
000057 |     def _command(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> str | None:
000058 |         return ctx.extra.get("exec_command")
000059 | [blank]
000060 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000061 |         namespace, pod = self._split(ctx)
000062 |         command = self._command(ctx) or "(no command given)"
000063 |         container = ctx.extra.get("container")
000064 |         target = f"{pod} in {namespace}" + (f", container {container}" if container else "")
000065 |         return Plan(
000066 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000067 |             reversible=False,
000068 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000069 |             steps=[
000070 |                 PlanStep(description=f"Check pod {pod} exists in {namespace}", impact="read-only"),
000071 |                 PlanStep(description=f"Exec into {target}: `{command}`"),
000072 |                 PlanStep(description="Capture stdout/stderr and exit code"),
000073 |             ],
000074 |         )
000075 | [blank]
000076 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000077 |         namespace, pod = self._split(ctx)
000078 |         command = self._command(ctx)
000079 |         if not command:
000080 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="no --exec-command given")
000081 | [blank]
000082 |         # Checked explicitly before attempting the WebSocket exec: a
000083 |         # nonexistent pod doesn't fail with a clean, single exception shape
000084 |         # the way a plain REST call does (get_configmap()/scale_deployment()
000085 |         # can just catch ApiException(404) and return None/False) -- found
000086 |         # live 2026-08-17, a missing pod surfaced as a raw
000087 |         # AttributeError('NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode') deep
000088 |         # inside the WebSocket client, not a clean "not found." Checking
000089 |         # first with the same get_pod_status() every other pod-targeting
000090 |         # action already uses avoids depending on that internal shape.
000091 |         pods = get_pod_status(namespace, pod)
000092 |         if not pods:
000093 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"pod {namespace}/{pod} not found")
000094 |         # get_pod_status() resolves a Deployment/friendly name (e.g.
000095 |         # "broken-app") to the actual running pod -- exec into THAT pod,
000096 |         # not the friendly name the WebSocket exec API has never heard of.
000097 |         pod = pods[0].name
000098 | [blank]
000099 |         container = ctx.extra.get("container")
000100 |         try:
000101 |             result = exec_in_pod(namespace, pod, ["sh", "-c", command], container=container)
000102 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — report honestly, never fake a result
000103 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"exec failed: {exc}")
000104 | [blank]
000105 |         # SUCCEEDED means "Prash ran the command and captured a real
000106 |         # result," not "the command exited 0" -- those are different
000107 |         # things. A diagnostic command that legitimately exits non-zero
000108 |         # (grep finding nothing, a health check reporting unhealthy) is
000109 |         # still a successful exec, and the exit code is right there in the
000110 |         # summary/detail for the user to read, not silently collapsed into
000111 |         # a single success/fail bit.
000112 |         stdout_preview = result["stdout"][:_SUMMARY_OUTPUT_PREVIEW]
000113 |         return ActionResult(
000114 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000115 |             summary=f"{namespace}/{pod}: `{command}` exited {result['exit_code']}" + (f" — {stdout_preview}" if stdout_preview.strip() else ""),
000116 |             detail={
000117 |                 "namespace": namespace,
000118 |                 "pod": pod,
000119 |                 "command": command,
000120 |                 "exit_code": str(result["exit_code"]),
000121 |                 "stdout": result["stdout"],
000122 |                 "stderr": result["stderr"],
000123 |             },
000124 |         )
000125 | [blank]
000126 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000127 |         # There is no independent way to verify an arbitrary command's
000128 |         # *effect* was correct -- "correct" isn't a thing this action can
000129 |         # know. verify() here only confirms the exec genuinely ran and
000130 |         # returned a real exit code, not that a bug slipped past silently.
000131 |         if result.status is not ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED:
000132 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail="exec did not complete")
000133 |         exit_code = result.detail.get("exit_code")
000134 |         return VerificationResult(ok=exit_code is not None, detail=f"exit_code={exit_code}")
````

### `prash/actions/github_alert.py`
````text
000001 | """Action: github-open-issue (CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC §4b, G0 decision).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | The CI surface's "alert" is an escalation, not a fix. Lear's primary CI value
000004 | is the open-pr / apply-ci-fix flow -- it fixes the failure. This action is what
000005 | it reaches for when it has a diagnosis but *no safe auto-fix*: file a GitHub
000006 | issue carrying that diagnosis as a durable, team-visible record.
000007 | [blank]
000008 | APPROVAL tier, reversible=True: outbound and team-visible (an issue shows up in
000009 | the repo's tracker and can notify watchers), so it gets the same approval gate
000010 | as datadog-alert / pagerduty-page -- but unlike a page or a Datadog event, a
000011 | GitHub issue can simply be closed, so it is genuinely reversible.
000012 | """
000013 | [blank]
000014 | from __future__ import annotations
000015 | [blank]
000016 | from .contract import (
000017 |     Action,
000018 |     ActionContext,
000019 |     ActionResult,
000020 |     ActionResultStatus,
000021 |     ActionSpec,
000022 |     Plan,
000023 |     PlanStep,
000024 |     RiskTier,
000025 |     VerificationResult,
000026 | )
000027 | [blank]
000028 | [blank]
000029 | class GitHubOpenIssueAction(Action):
000030 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000031 |         id="github-open-issue",
000032 |         summary="Open a GitHub issue escalating a CI failure Lear can't safely auto-fix",
000033 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.APPROVAL,
000034 |         reversible=True,
000035 |         capabilities=("alert",),
000036 |         approval_hint="This will open a visible issue in the repo's tracker",
000037 |     )
000038 | [blank]
000039 |     @staticmethod
000040 |     def _title(ctx: ActionContext) -> str:
000041 |         return ctx.extra.get("title") or f"Lear: CI failure on {ctx.target.resource}"
000042 | [blank]
000043 |     @staticmethod
000044 |     def _body(ctx: ActionContext) -> str:
000045 |         return ctx.extra.get("body") or (
000046 |             f"Lear detected a CI failure on `{ctx.target.resource}` and is escalating it "
000047 |             f"because no safe automated fix was available.\n\n"
000048 |             f"(Opened by Lear. Close this issue once it's handled.)"
000049 |         )
000050 | [blank]
000051 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000052 |         return Plan(
000053 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000054 |             reversible=True,
000055 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000056 |             steps=[
000057 |                 PlanStep(
000058 |                     description=f"Open issue '{self._title(ctx)}' on {ctx.target.resource}",
000059 |                     impact="Visible in the repo's issue tracker and may notify watchers; reversible by closing the issue",
000060 |                 )
000061 |             ],
000062 |         )
000063 | [blank]
000064 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000065 |         gh = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("github")
000066 |         if not gh:
000067 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="GitHub connector is missing or not configured.")
000068 |         repo = ctx.target.resource
000069 |         title = self._title(ctx)
000070 |         try:
000071 |             resp = gh.create_issue(repo, title, self._body(ctx))
000072 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
000073 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"open-issue failed: {exc}")
000074 |         number = resp.get("number") if isinstance(resp, dict) else None
000075 |         url = resp.get("html_url", "") if isinstance(resp, dict) else ""
000076 |         return ActionResult(
000077 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000078 |             summary=f"opened issue #{number} on {repo}" + (f" ({url})" if url else ""),
000079 |             detail={"repo": repo, "number": number, "url": url, "title": title},
000080 |         )
000081 | [blank]
000082 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000083 |         gh = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("github")
000084 |         if not gh:
000085 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail="could not verify: GitHub connector missing")
000086 |         number = result.detail.get("number")
000087 |         if not number:
000088 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail="could not verify: no issue number was returned")
000089 |         repo = result.detail.get("repo") or ctx.target.resource
000090 |         try:
000091 |             issue = gh.get_issue(repo, number)
000092 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
000093 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail=f"issue #{number} not found: {exc}")
000094 |         confirmed = isinstance(issue, dict) and issue.get("number") == number and issue.get("state") == "open"
000095 |         if confirmed:
000096 |             return VerificationResult(ok=True, detail=f"issue #{number} is open on {repo}")
000097 |         return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail=f"issue #{number} not found or not open on {repo}")
````

### `prash/actions/gitleaks_escalate.py`
````text
000001 | """Action: gitleaks-escalate (Sprint 2 Tier 3, PRASH_V2.md §7b).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Deliberately not "gitleaks-fix" -- there is nothing gitleaks itself can
000004 | mutate to fix a leaked secret (see gitleaks.py's own docstring: it has no
000005 | cloud account, and the actual fix is rotating the credential in whatever
000006 | system it belongs to, which a local scanner has no way to know). Discussed
000007 | explicitly before building (see PRASH_V2.md §9/§10, 2026-08-19): the honest
000008 | write action here is escalation, not remediation -- when a scan finds
000009 | leaks, open a real PagerDuty incident so a human rotates the credential
000010 | fast, rather than either doing nothing or pretending to fix something this
000011 | connector structurally cannot fix.
000012 | [blank]
000013 | The first genuinely cross-connector action in this codebase: needs BOTH
000014 | the gitleaks connector (to run the scan) and the pagerduty connector (to
000015 | escalate what it finds) present in ctx.extra["connectors"]. Every other
000016 | action here acts through exactly one connector; this one doesn't, and
000017 | that's a deliberate, documented exception, not an accidental coupling.
000018 | [blank]
000019 | SAFE tier: escalating a real problem to a human is the opposite of
000020 | suppressing one (contrast with pagerduty-resolve, APPROVAL, which
000021 | suppresses paging) -- low blast radius, and worst case it's a noisy but
000022 | harmless incident. Never includes the actual secret value in the incident
000023 | payload -- only rule id, file, line, and gitleaks' own fingerprint, same
000024 | safety property gitleaks.py's poll_state()/fetch_logs() already enforce.
000025 | """
000026 | [blank]
000027 | from __future__ import annotations
000028 | [blank]
000029 | from ..connectors.pagerduty import PagerDutyError
000030 | from .contract import (
000031 |     Action,
000032 |     ActionContext,
000033 |     ActionResult,
000034 |     ActionResultStatus,
000035 |     ActionSpec,
000036 |     Plan,
000037 |     PlanStep,
000038 |     RiskTier,
000039 |     VerificationResult,
000040 | )
000041 | [blank]
000042 | [blank]
000043 | class GitleaksEscalateAction(Action):
000044 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000045 |         id="gitleaks-escalate",
000046 |         summary="Scan for leaked secrets and open a PagerDuty incident if any are found",
000047 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.SAFE,
000048 |         reversible=False,
000049 |         capabilities=("secret_scan", "trigger_event"),
000050 |     )
000051 | [blank]
000052 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000053 |         return Plan(
000054 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000055 |             reversible=False,
000056 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000057 |             steps=[
000058 |                 PlanStep(description=f"Scan {ctx.target.resource} for leaked secrets", impact="read-only"),
000059 |                 PlanStep(description="If any are found, open a PagerDuty incident naming the rule/file/line only -- never the secret value"),
000060 |             ],
000061 |         )
000062 | [blank]
000063 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000064 |         gitleaks = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("gitleaks")
000065 |         pagerduty = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("pagerduty")
000066 |         if not gitleaks:
000067 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="Gitleaks connector is missing or not configured.")
000068 |         if not pagerduty:
000069 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="PagerDuty connector is missing or not configured -- needed to escalate a leak.")
000070 | [blank]
000071 |         state = gitleaks.poll_state(ctx.target.resource)
000072 |         findings = state.detail.get("findings", [])
000073 |         if not findings:
000074 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.SKIPPED, summary=f"no leaks found in {ctx.target.resource} -- nothing to escalate")
000075 | [blank]
000076 |         summary = f"gitleaks found {len(findings)} leaked secret(s) in {ctx.target.resource}"
000077 |         rule_ids = sorted({f.get("rule_id", "?") for f in findings})
000078 |         try:
000079 |             incident = pagerduty.trigger_event(
000080 |                 summary=summary,
000081 |                 source=ctx.target.resource,
000082 |                 severity="critical",
000083 |                 custom_details={"leak_count": len(findings), "rule_ids": rule_ids, "findings": findings},
000084 |             )
000085 |         except PagerDutyError as exc:
000086 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"scan found {len(findings)} leak(s) but escalation failed: {exc}")
000087 |         return ActionResult(
000088 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000089 |             summary=f"{summary} -- PagerDuty incident opened",
000090 |             detail={"leak_count": len(findings), "dedup_key": incident.get("dedup_key", "")},
000091 |         )
000092 | [blank]
000093 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000094 |         if result.status is ActionResultStatus.SKIPPED:
000095 |             return VerificationResult(ok=True, detail="no leaks found; nothing needed escalating")
000096 |         dedup_key = result.detail.get("dedup_key", "")
000097 |         return VerificationResult(ok=bool(dedup_key), detail=f"incident dedup_key={dedup_key or 'missing'}")
````

### `prash/actions/missing_secret.py`
````text
000001 | """Action: request-secret (Track C #1).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Closes the single most common dead end seen in v1 testing (``needs_secret``).
000004 | Instead of reporting "manual_required", Prash asks the user for the value,
000005 | stores it locally (never on Drufiy's servers), and re-triggers the blocked job.
000006 | [blank]
000007 | Precedence for the secret value:
000008 |     1. ctx.secrets[name]        (already supplied on the command line / env)
000009 |     2. credential store         (PRASH_SECRET_<name> in the local .env)
000010 |     3. interactive prompt       (via the interface's secret_input callable)
000011 | If none of those yield a value, the action returns NEEDS_INPUT and the
000012 | dispatcher records it honestly in the audit log.
000013 | """
000014 | [blank]
000015 | from __future__ import annotations
000016 | [blank]
000017 | from typing import Callable, Optional
000018 | [blank]
000019 | from ..credentials import CredentialStore
000020 | from .contract import (
000021 |     Action,
000022 |     ActionContext,
000023 |     ActionResult,
000024 |     ActionResultStatus,
000025 |     ActionSpec,
000026 |     Plan,
000027 |     PlanStep,
000028 |     RiskTier,
000029 |     VerificationResult,
000030 | )
000031 | [blank]
000032 | [blank]
000033 | class RequestSecretAction(Action):
000034 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000035 |         id="request-secret",
000036 |         summary="Request a missing secret, store it locally, then re-trigger the blocked job",
000037 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.SAFE,
000038 |         reversible=True,
000039 |         capabilities=("secret_store", "re_run_job"),
000040 |         approval_hint="The value is written to your local credentials file only.",
000041 |     )
000042 | [blank]
000043 |     def _name(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> str:
000044 |         return str(ctx.extra.get("secret_name", ""))
000045 | [blank]
000046 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000047 |         name = self._name(ctx)
000048 |         job = ctx.extra.get("job", ctx.target.resource)
000049 |         return Plan(
000050 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000051 |             reversible=True,
000052 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000053 |             steps=[
000054 |                 PlanStep(description=f"Request value for secret '{name}'"),
000055 |                 PlanStep(description=f"Store '{name}' in local credentials file", impact="local only"),
000056 |                 PlanStep(description=f"Re-trigger blocked job '{job}'"),
000057 |             ],
000058 |         )
000059 | [blank]
000060 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000061 |         name = self._name(ctx)
000062 |         if not name:
000063 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="no secret_name supplied")
000064 | [blank]
000065 |         value = ctx.secrets.get(name) or ctx.extra.get("secret_value")
000066 |         if not value:
000067 |             store = ctx.extra.get("store", CredentialStore.from_env())
000068 |             value = store.secrets().get(name)
000069 |         if not value:
000070 |             secret_input: Optional[Callable[[str, str], str]] = ctx.extra.get("secret_input")
000071 |             if secret_input is None:
000072 |                 return ActionResult(
000073 |                     status=ActionResultStatus.NEEDS_INPUT,
000074 |                     summary=f"secret '{name}' required; nothing to run until a value is provided",
000075 |                 )
000076 |             value = secret_input(name, ctx.extra.get("secret_hint", ""))
000077 |             if not value:
000078 |                 return ActionResult(
000079 |                     status=ActionResultStatus.NEEDS_INPUT,
000080 |                     summary=f"no value given for '{name}'",
000081 |                 )
000082 | [blank]
000083 |         store = ctx.extra.get("store", CredentialStore.from_env())
000084 |         store.set_secret(name, value)
000085 | [blank]
000086 |         runner = ctx.extra.get("runner")
000087 |         re_run = "not triggered"
000088 |         if runner is not None:
000089 |             try:
000090 |                 run_id = runner.re_run(ctx.target.resource)
000091 |                 re_run = f"triggered (run {run_id})"
000092 |             except NotImplementedError:
000093 |                 re_run = "queued (runner connector not wired)"
000094 |             except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - secret is stored; re-run failing is reported honestly
000095 |                 return ActionResult(
000096 |                     status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED,
000097 |                     summary=f"secret '{name}' stored locally, but job re-run failed: {exc}",
000098 |                     detail={"secret_name": name, "re_run": "failed"},
000099 |                 )
000100 | [blank]
000101 |         return ActionResult(
000102 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000103 |             summary=f"secret '{name}' stored locally; job re-run {re_run}",
000104 |             detail={"secret_name": name, "re_run": re_run},
000105 |         )
000106 | [blank]
000107 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000108 |         store = ctx.extra.get("store", CredentialStore.from_env())
000109 |         name = result.detail.get("secret_name")
000110 |         stored = name in store.secrets()
000111 |         return VerificationResult(ok=stored, detail=f"secret '{name}' present in local store: {stored}")
````

### `prash/actions/pagerduty_incident.py`
````text
000001 | """Actions: pagerduty-acknowledge, pagerduty-resolve (Sprint 2 Tier 3,
000002 | PRASH_V2.md §7b).
000003 | [blank]
000004 | Two distinct action ids sharing one base, same shape as edit-configmap/
000005 | edit-secret (prash/actions/edit_config.py) -- the plan/execute/verify
000006 | pattern is identical, only which status transition each requests differs.
000007 | [blank]
000008 | Risk tiers deliberately differ from each other, not copy-pasted:
000009 | - **acknowledge is SAFE.** Low blast radius, and it's literally the first
000010 |   thing an on-call engineer does by hand -- claiming "someone is looking at
000011 |   this" is a low-stakes, easily-corrected statement. Matches restart-pod's
000012 |   SAFE reasoning: routine, low-risk.
000013 | - **resolve is APPROVAL.** Declaring an incident resolved is a claim of
000014 |   fact that, if wrong, can suppress a real ongoing outage -- nobody gets
000015 |   paged again unless the underlying monitor independently re-triggers.
000016 |   Always needs an explicit human yes, matching rollback/scale/config-edit's
000017 |   existing reasoning in RiskTier's own docstring.
000018 | [blank]
000019 | Neither is marked reversible: PagerDuty's stable v2 API has no supported
000020 | transition back from acknowledged->triggered or resolved->anything -- the
000021 | only way "back" is a fresh trigger from the monitoring source itself. Not
000022 | claiming a reversibility guarantee this connector hasn't verified.
000023 | """
000024 | [blank]
000025 | from __future__ import annotations
000026 | [blank]
000027 | from ..connectors.pagerduty import PagerDutyError
000028 | from .contract import (
000029 |     Action,
000030 |     ActionContext,
000031 |     ActionResult,
000032 |     ActionResultStatus,
000033 |     ActionSpec,
000034 |     Plan,
000035 |     PlanStep,
000036 |     RiskTier,
000037 |     VerificationResult,
000038 | )
000039 | [blank]
000040 | [blank]
000041 | class _PagerDutyIncidentActionBase(Action):
000042 |     _status = ""
000043 |     _verb = ""
000044 | [blank]
000045 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000046 |         return Plan(
000047 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000048 |             reversible=self.spec.reversible,
000049 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000050 |             steps=[PlanStep(description=f"{self._verb} PagerDuty incident {ctx.target.resource}")],
000051 |         )
000052 | [blank]
000053 |     def _call(self, pd, incident_id: str) -> dict:
000054 |         raise NotImplementedError
000055 | [blank]
000056 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000057 |         pd = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("pagerduty")
000058 |         if not pd:
000059 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="PagerDuty connector is missing or not configured.")
000060 |         try:
000061 |             incident = self._call(pd, ctx.target.resource)
000062 |         except PagerDutyError as exc:
000063 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"{self._verb.lower()} failed: {exc}")
000064 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — report honestly, never fake a result
000065 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"{self._verb.lower()} failed: {exc}")
000066 |         return ActionResult(
000067 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000068 |             summary=f"incident {ctx.target.resource} {self._status}",
000069 |             detail={"incident_id": ctx.target.resource, "status": incident.get("status", self._status)},
000070 |         )
000071 | [blank]
000072 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000073 |         actual_status = result.detail.get("status", "")
000074 |         return VerificationResult(ok=actual_status == self._status, detail=f"incident status now={actual_status or 'unknown'}")
000075 | [blank]
000076 | [blank]
000077 | class PagerdutyAcknowledgeAction(_PagerDutyIncidentActionBase):
000078 |     _status = "acknowledged"
000079 |     _verb = "Acknowledge"
000080 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000081 |         id="pagerduty-acknowledge",
000082 |         summary="Acknowledge a PagerDuty incident",
000083 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.SAFE,
000084 |         reversible=False,
000085 |         capabilities=("acknowledge_incident",),
000086 |     )
000087 | [blank]
000088 |     def _call(self, pd, incident_id: str) -> dict:
000089 |         return pd.acknowledge_incident(incident_id)
000090 | [blank]
000091 | [blank]
000092 | class PagerdutyResolveAction(_PagerDutyIncidentActionBase):
000093 |     _status = "resolved"
000094 |     _verb = "Resolve"
000095 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000096 |         id="pagerduty-resolve",
000097 |         summary="Resolve a PagerDuty incident",
000098 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.APPROVAL,
000099 |         reversible=False,
000100 |         capabilities=("resolve_incident",),
000101 |         approval_hint="Always prompts, even in bypass mode — a false resolve can suppress a real ongoing outage.",
000102 |     )
````

````text
000001 | """Action: pagerduty-page (connector rewrite, Phase 3 rollout — PagerDuty).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | APPROVAL tier, hardcoded: paging the on-call engineer is the most
000004 | disruptive thing Prash can do -- a real human gets woken up -- and it is
000005 | irreversible in every sense that matters: the Events API has no un-page,
000006 | the incident can't be un-triggered (the only path "back" is someone
000007 | manually resolving it), and the phone already buzzed. Outbound +
000008 | irreversible + wakes a human is exactly the spec's default for APPROVAL
000009 | (same reasoning as pagerduty-resolve); nothing about this action is
000010 | internal, quiet, or undoable, so SAFE was never on the table.
000011 | [blank]
000012 | The mechanism is the Events API v2 (PAGERDUTY_ROUTING_KEY), not the REST
000013 | API -- triggering a NEW incident and updating an EXISTING one are
000014 | different PagerDuty products with different auth models (see the
000015 | connector's module docstring). verify() closes the loop honestly: the
000016 | Events API response carries no incident id, so it looks up the incident
000017 | by dedup key (server-side incident_key filter, alert_key fallback) with
000018 | a bounded retry for PagerDuty's intake -> listable propagation -- and
000019 | reports "not visible yet" rather than success if it never shows up.
000020 | """
000021 | [blank]
000022 | from __future__ import annotations

000051 |         return None
000052 | [blank]
000053 | [blank]
000054 | class PagerdutyPageAction(Action):
000055 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000056 |         id="pagerduty-page",
000057 |         summary="Page the on-call engineer with a new PagerDuty incident",
000058 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.APPROVAL,
000059 |         reversible=False,

000062 |     )

000065 |         summary = ctx.extra.get("summary") or f"Prash page: {ctx.target.resource}"
000066 |         severity = ctx.extra.get("severity", "critical")
000067 |         impact = "Pages the on-call engineer now; the incident cannot be un-triggered and must be resolved by hand"

000070 |             try:

000072 |                 if oncalls:
000073 |                     names = [o.get("user_name") for o in oncalls if o.get("user_name")]
000074 |                     if names:
000075 |                         impact += f" (Current on-call: {', '.join(names)})"
000076 |             except Exception:
000077 |                 pass
000078 |         return Plan(
000079 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000080 |             reversible=False,
000081 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000082 |             steps=[

000084 |                     description=f"Trigger PagerDuty incident '{summary}' (severity {severity}) via the Events API routing key",
000085 |                     impact=impact,
000086 |                 )
000087 |             ],
000088 |         )
000089 | [blank]
000090 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000091 |         pd = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("pagerduty")
000092 |         if not pd:
000093 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="PagerDuty connector is missing or not configured.")
000094 |         summary = ctx.extra.get("summary") or f"Prash page: {ctx.target.resource}"
000095 |         severity = ctx.extra.get("severity", "critical")
000096 |         source = ctx.extra.get("source", "prash")
000097 |         dedup_key = ctx.extra.get("dedup_key") or f"prash-page-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
000098 |         posted_at = _utcnow()
000099 |         try:
000100 |             resp = pd.page_oncall(

000102 |                 custom_details=ctx.extra.get("custom_details"),
000103 |             )
000104 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — report honestly, never fake a result
000105 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"page failed: {exc}")
000106 |         status = resp.get("status", "") if isinstance(resp, dict) else ""
000107 |         if status != "success":
000108 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"page not accepted by PagerDuty: {resp}")
000109 |         event = {
000110 |             "timestamp": posted_at.isoformat(),
000111 |             "connector": "pagerduty",
000112 |             "event_type": "page_oncall",
000113 |             "summary": summary,
000114 |             "severity": severity,
000115 |             "dedup_key": dedup_key,
000116 |         }
000117 |         return ActionResult(
000118 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000119 |             summary=f"on-call paged: '{summary}' (dedup key {dedup_key})",
000120 |             detail={
000121 |                 "dedup_key": dedup_key,
000122 |                 "severity": severity,
000123 |                 "summary": summary,
000124 |                 "posted_at": posted_at.isoformat(),
000125 |                 "event": event,
000126 |             },
000127 |         )

000129 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000130 |         pd = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("pagerduty")
000131 |         if not pd:
000132 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail="could not verify: PagerDuty connector missing")
000133 |         dedup_key = result.detail.get("dedup_key")
000134 |         if not dedup_key:
000135 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail="could not verify: no dedup key was recorded")
000136 |         posted_at = _parse_ts(result.detail.get("posted_at")) or _utcnow() - timedelta(minutes=30)
000137 |         # Found live (2026-09-09): a just-triggered Events v2 incident is not
000138 |         # listable via REST for a few seconds (intake -> incident propagation),
000139 |         # so a single immediate lookup reports "not verified" for a page that
000140 |         # is real. Same bounded retry as datadog_alert.verify: confirm as soon
000141 |         # as reality catches up; if it never does, report exactly that instead
000142 |         # of claiming a verified success.
000143 |         last = "could not verify: no lookup was attempted"
000144 |         for attempt in range(3):
000145 |             try:
000146 |                 incident = pd.find_incident_by_incident_key(dedup_key, since=posted_at)
000147 |             except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — verification must report, never crash
000148 |                 last = f"could not verify: {exc}"
000149 |                 if attempt < 2:
000150 |                     time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
000151 |                 continue
000152 |             if incident is not None:
000153 |                 return VerificationResult(
000154 |                     ok=True,
000155 |                     detail=f"incident {incident.get('id')} exists ({incident.get('status')}), matched by dedup key",
000156 |                 )
000157 |             # The Events API accepted the trigger (execute() would have
000158 |             # failed otherwise), but the incident isn't visible in the REST
000159 |             # window yet -- report that honestly instead of claiming success.
000160 |             last = f"no incident with incident_key {dedup_key} in the recent window (page may still be propagating)"
000161 |             if attempt < 2:
000162 |                 time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
000163 |         return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail=last)
````

````text
000061 |         reason = ctx.extra.get("reason")
````

### `prash/actions/vercel_deploy.py`
````text
000001 | """Actions: vercel-redeploy, vercel-rollback (Sprint 2 Tier 3, PRASH_V2.md
000002 | §7b).
000003 | [blank]
000004 | Different risk tiers, not copy-pasted: **redeploy is SAFE** -- it's a retry
000005 | of what's already deployed, same reasoning as restart-pod (routine,
000006 | low-risk, the thing you'd try first). **rollback is APPROVAL** -- it
000007 | changes what's actually live in production to a different build, the same
000008 | consequential-claim reasoning RiskTier's own docstring already applies to
000009 | Kubernetes' rollback action.
000010 | [blank]
000011 | redeploy is marked reversible (it's just "try again," nothing to undo).
000012 | rollback is marked reversible too -- rolling back TO a deployment can
000013 | itself be rolled back FROM by rolling forward to a later one, same
000014 | "the same action run again undoes it" logic this repo's edit-configmap/
000015 | scale actions already use for their own reversible=True.
000016 | """
000017 | [blank]
000018 | from __future__ import annotations
000019 | [blank]
000020 | from .contract import (
000021 |     Action,
000022 |     ActionContext,
000023 |     ActionResult,
000024 |     ActionResultStatus,
000025 |     ActionSpec,
000026 |     Plan,
000027 |     PlanStep,
000028 |     RiskTier,
000029 |     VerificationResult,
000030 | )
000031 | [blank]
000032 | [blank]
000033 | class VercelRedeployAction(Action):
000034 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000035 |         id="vercel-redeploy",
000036 |         summary="Redeploy the latest (or a specific) Vercel deployment",
000037 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.SAFE,
000038 |         reversible=True,
000039 |         capabilities=("redeploy",),
000040 |     )
000041 | [blank]
000042 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000043 |         deployment_id = ctx.extra.get("deployment_id")
000044 |         target = f"deployment {deployment_id}" if deployment_id else "the latest deployment"
000045 |         return Plan(
000046 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000047 |             reversible=True,
000048 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000049 |             steps=[PlanStep(description=f"Redeploy {target} for project {ctx.target.resource}")],
000050 |         )
000051 | [blank]
000052 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000053 |         vercel = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("vercel")
000054 |         if not vercel:
000055 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="Vercel connector is missing or not configured.")
000056 |         try:
000057 |             deployment = vercel.redeploy(ctx.target.resource, deployment_id=ctx.extra.get("deployment_id"))
000058 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
000059 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"redeploy failed: {exc}")
000060 |         return ActionResult(
000061 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000062 |             summary=f"redeployed {ctx.target.resource}: new deployment {deployment.get('id', deployment.get('uid', '?'))}",
000063 |             detail={"deployment": deployment},
000064 |         )
000065 | [blank]
000066 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000067 |         deployment = result.detail.get("deployment", {})
000068 |         ready_state = deployment.get("readyState", "")
000069 |         if ready_state in ("READY",):
000070 |             return VerificationResult(ok=True, detail="new deployment is READY")
000071 |         if ready_state in ("ERROR", "CANCELED"):
000072 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail=f"new deployment ended in {ready_state}")
000073 |         # BUILDING/QUEUED/INITIALIZING -- genuinely still in progress at the
000074 |         # moment of the API response, not a failure to report as ok=False.
000075 |         return VerificationResult(ok=True, detail=f"new deployment triggered, state={ready_state or 'unknown'} (still in progress)")
000076 | [blank]
000077 | [blank]
000078 | class VercelRollbackAction(Action):
000079 |     spec = ActionSpec(
000080 |         id="vercel-rollback",
000081 |         summary="Roll production back to a specific earlier Vercel deployment",
000082 |         risk_tier=RiskTier.APPROVAL,
000083 |         reversible=True,
000084 |         capabilities=("rollback",),
000085 |         approval_hint="Always prompts, even in bypass mode -- changes what's actually live in production.",
000086 |     )
000087 | [blank]
000088 |     def plan(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> Plan:
000089 |         deployment_id = ctx.extra.get("deployment_id")
000090 |         return Plan(
000091 |             action_id=self.spec.id,
000092 |             reversible=True,
000093 |             risk_tier=self.spec.risk_tier,
000094 |             steps=[PlanStep(description=f"Roll {ctx.target.resource} back to deployment {deployment_id or '<missing>'}", impact="changes what's live in production")],
000095 |         )
000096 | [blank]
000097 |     def execute(self, ctx: ActionContext) -> ActionResult:
000098 |         vercel = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("vercel")
000099 |         if not vercel:
000100 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="Vercel connector is missing or not configured.")
000101 |         deployment_id = ctx.extra.get("deployment_id")
000102 |         if not deployment_id:
000103 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary="no --deployment-id given -- rollback needs a specific target, not 'whatever's latest'")
000104 |         try:
000105 |             result = vercel.rollback(ctx.target.resource, deployment_id)
000106 |         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
000107 |             return ActionResult(status=ActionResultStatus.FAILED, summary=f"rollback failed: {exc}")
000108 |         return ActionResult(
000109 |             status=ActionResultStatus.SUCCEEDED,
000110 |             summary=f"{ctx.target.resource} rolled back to {deployment_id}",
000111 |             detail={"deployment_id": deployment_id, "result": result},
000112 |         )
000113 | [blank]
000114 |     def verify(self, ctx: ActionContext, result: ActionResult) -> VerificationResult:
000115 |         vercel = ctx.extra.get("connectors", {}).get("vercel")
000116 |         if not vercel:
000117 |             return VerificationResult(ok=False, detail="could not verify: Vercel connector missing")
000118 |         # Not poll_state() -- a rollback re-points production to an existing,
000119 |         # older deployment rather than creating a new one, so "most recently
000120 |         # created deployment" (poll_state's notion) never changes when a
000121 |         # rollback succeeds. Check what's actually aliased to production.
000122 |         current_id = vercel.production_deployment_id(ctx.target.resource)
000123 |         expected_id = result.detail.get("deployment_id", "")
000124 |         ok = current_id == expected_id
000125 |         return VerificationResult(ok=ok, detail=f"production deployment now={current_id or 'unknown'}")
````

````text
000686 |   <script>
000687 |     function addLog(type, msg) {
000688 |       const box = document.getElementById('consoleLog');
000689 |       const now = new Date().toLocaleTimeString();
000690 |       const div = document.createElement('div');
000691 |       div.className = 'log-line';
000692 |       let cls = 'log-info';
000693 |       if (type === 'ERR') cls = 'log-err';
000694 |       if (type === 'SUCC') cls = 'log-succ';
000695 |       div.innerHTML = `<span class="log-ts">[${now}]</span> <span class="${cls}">[${type}] ${msg}</span>`;
000696 |       box.appendChild(div);
000697 |       box.scrollTop = box.scrollHeight;
000698 |     }

000700 |     async function refreshClusterTelemetry() {
000701 |       try {
000702 |         const res = await fetch('/api/demo/health');
000703 |         if (!res.ok) return;
000704 |         const d = await res.json();
000705 |         
000706 |         // Pods list
000707 |         const list = document.getElementById('podList');
000708 |         if (d.pods && d.pods.length > 0) {
000709 |           list.innerHTML = '';
000710 |           d.pods.forEach(p => {
000711 |             const isOk = p.ready && p.status === 'Running';
000712 |             const item = document.createElement('div');
000713 |             item.className = 'pod-item';
000714 |             item.innerHTML = `
000715 |               <div class="pod-header">
000716 |                 <span class="pod-name">${p.name}</span>
000717 |                 <span class="pod-tag ${isOk ? 'tag-running' : 'tag-crash'}">${p.status}</span>
000718 |               </div>
000719 |               <div class="pod-meta">
000720 |                 <span>Ready: ${p.ready ? '1/1' : '0/1'}</span>
000721 |                 <span>Restarts: ${p.restarts}</span>
000722 |               </div>
000723 |             `;
000724 |             list.appendChild(item);
000725 |           });
000726 |         }
000727 | [blank]
000728 |         // ELB Card
000729 |         const elbCard = document.getElementById('cardElb');
000730 |         const dotElb = document.getElementById('dotElb');
000731 |         const valElb = document.getElementById('valElb');
000732 |         if (d.elb_healthy) {
000733 |           elbCard.className = 'metric-card healthy';
000734 |           dotElb.className = 'metric-status-dot dot-healthy';
000735 |           valElb.innerText = `200 OK (${d.latency_ms || 24}ms)`;
000736 |         } else {
000737 |           elbCard.className = 'metric-card down';
000738 |           dotElb.className = 'metric-status-dot dot-danger';
000739 |           valElb.innerText = '502 BAD GATEWAY';
000740 |         }
000741 | [blank]
000742 |         // Inspect checkout pod status
000743 |         const checkoutPod = (d.pods || []).find(p => p.name.includes('checkout-api'));
000744 |         const cardCheckout = document.getElementById('cardCheckout');
000745 |         const dotCheckout = document.getElementById('dotCheckout');
000746 |         const valCheckout = document.getElementById('valCheckout');
000747 |         if (checkoutPod) {
000748 |           if (checkoutPod.status === 'Running' && checkoutPod.ready) {
000749 |             cardCheckout.className = 'metric-card healthy';
000750 |             dotCheckout.className = 'metric-status-dot dot-healthy';
000751 |             valCheckout.innerText = '1/1 RUNNING';
000752 |           } else {
000753 |             cardCheckout.className = 'metric-card down';
000754 |             dotCheckout.className = 'metric-status-dot dot-danger';
000755 |             valCheckout.innerText = checkoutPod.status.toUpperCase();

000757 |         }
````

### `prash/audit.py`
````text
000001 | """Append-only audit log of every action Prash takes.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | The log is append-only by construction: it is opened in append mode and never
000004 | rewritten in place. Every entry carries a monotonic sequence, UTC timestamp,
000005 | the action id, risk tier, permission mode, environment, decision, outcome, and
000006 | verification. This is the user's record of "what did Prash do, when, and did it
000007 | work".
000008 | """
000009 | [blank]
000010 | from __future__ import annotations
000011 | [blank]
000012 | import json
000013 | import os
000014 | import time
000015 | import uuid
000016 | from pathlib import Path
000017 | from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
000018 | [blank]
000019 | from .actions.contract import ActionResult, Decision, RiskTier
000020 | from .permissions import PermissionMode
000021 | [blank]
000022 | [blank]
000023 | def _utc_now() -> str:
000024 |     return time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
000025 | [blank]
000026 | [blank]
000027 | class AuditLog:
000028 |     def __init__(self, path: Optional[Path] = None):
000029 |         self.path = (path or Path(os.environ.get("PRASH_AUDIT_LOG_PATH", ".prash/audit.log"))).expanduser().resolve()
000030 | [blank]
000031 |     def _open_append(self):
000032 |         if not self.path.parent.exists():
000033 |             self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
000034 |         return self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8")
000035 | [blank]
000036 |     def append(
000037 |         self,
000038 |         action_id: str,
000039 |         risk_tier: RiskTier,
000040 |         mode: PermissionMode,
000041 |         decision: Decision,
000042 |         result: ActionResult,
000043 |         environment: str = "staging",
000044 |         actor: str = "local",
000045 |         extra: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
000046 |     ) -> str:
000047 |         entry_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
000048 |         entry: Dict[str, Any] = {
000049 |             "id": entry_id,
000050 |             "ts": _utc_now(),
000051 |             "seq": self._next_seq(),
000052 |             "action": action_id,
000053 |             "risk_tier": risk_tier.value,
000054 |             "mode": mode.value,
000055 |             "decision": decision.value,
000056 |             "environment": environment,
000057 |             "actor": actor,
000058 |             "status": result.status.value,
000059 |             "summary": result.summary,
000060 |             "verification_ok": bool(result.verification) and result.verification.ok,
000061 |             "extra": extra or {},
000062 |         }
000063 |         with self._open_append() as fh:
000064 |             fh.write(json.dumps(entry) + "\n")
000065 |         return entry_id
000066 | [blank]
000067 |     def _next_seq(self) -> int:
000068 |         if not self.path.exists():
000069 |             return 1
000070 |         last = None
000071 |         with self.path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
000072 |             for line in fh:
000073 |                 if line.strip():
000074 |                     last = line
000075 |         if last is None:
000076 |             return 1
000077 |         try:
000078 |             return int(json.loads(last)["seq"]) + 1
000079 |         except (ValueError, KeyError):
000080 |             return 1
000081 | [blank]
000082 |     def read(self, limit: Optional[int] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
000083 |         if not self.path.exists():
000084 |             return []
000085 |         entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
000086 |         with self.path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
000087 |             for line in fh:
000088 |                 if line.strip():
000089 |                     entries.append(json.loads(line))
000090 |         return entries[-limit:] if limit else entries
````

### `prash/brain/correlation.py`
````text
000001 | """Multi-connector correlation (CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC §4c/§6, M6).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | The competitive bet in one function: a pod crash, a Datadog metric spike, and a
000004 | recent deploy that all happen inside the same minute are ONE incident with one
000005 | root cause — not three unrelated alerts. Every connector already emits the same
000006 | `ConnectorEvent` shape (base.py §4c: timestamp/connector/event_type/summary/raw),
000007 | so correlation is a pure operation over that shared timeline: merge events from
000008 | N connectors, sort by time, and cluster the ones that coincide.
000009 | [blank]
000010 | This module is deliberately pure and connector-agnostic — it takes events that
000011 | were already fetched via each connector's get_stats() and joins them. It does no
000012 | I/O and imports no connector, so it's unit-testable headlessly and works the
000013 | moment any two connectors return events on the same clock (real Datadog is M4;
000014 | until then the same logic runs against a stubbed Datadog get_stats — the join
000015 | doesn't care where the events came from).
000016 | """
000017 | [blank]
000018 | from __future__ import annotations
000019 | [blank]
000020 | import datetime
000021 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
000022 | [blank]
000023 | # ConnectorEvent is a TypedDict (base.py §4c); at runtime it's a plain dict, so
000024 | # this module only ever does dict access on events.
000025 | ConnectorEvent = dict
000026 | [blank]
000027 | # Default: events within two minutes of each other are treated as coincident.
000028 | # A pod's CrashLoopBackOff and the metric spike it causes land seconds apart in
000029 | # practice; two minutes is generous without chaining genuinely separate
000030 | # incidents together.
000031 | DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS = 120
000032 | [blank]
000033 | [blank]
000034 | def _as_utc(ts: datetime.datetime) -> datetime.datetime:
000035 |     """Normalize to tz-aware UTC so events from connectors that return naive
000036 |     timestamps (some GCP paths) sort and subtract cleanly against tz-aware
000037 |     ones (k8s, AWS)."""
000038 |     if ts.tzinfo is None:
000039 |         return ts.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
000040 |     return ts.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc)
000041 | [blank]
000042 | [blank]
000043 | @dataclass
000044 | class CorrelatedIncident:
000045 |     """A cluster of ConnectorEvents that coincide in time and therefore likely
000046 |     share one root cause. `connectors` is the distinct set involved, in the
000047 |     order first seen on the timeline."""
000048 | [blank]
000049 |     events: list[ConnectorEvent]
000050 |     connectors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
000051 | [blank]
000052 |     @property
000053 |     def start(self) -> datetime.datetime:
000054 |         return _as_utc(self.events[0]["timestamp"])
000055 | [blank]
000056 |     @property
000057 |     def end(self) -> datetime.datetime:
000058 |         return _as_utc(self.events[-1]["timestamp"])
000059 | [blank]
000060 |     @property
000061 |     def is_multi_source(self) -> bool:
000062 |         """True when the incident spans >=2 connectors — the case where
000063 |         correlation changes the diagnosis (cross-check beats single source)."""
000064 |         return len(self.connectors) >= 2
000065 | [blank]
000066 | [blank]
000067 | def _make_incident(events: list[ConnectorEvent]) -> CorrelatedIncident:
000068 |     connectors: list[str] = []
000069 |     for e in events:
000070 |         c = e.get("connector", "unknown")
000071 |         if c not in connectors:
000072 |             connectors.append(c)
000073 |     return CorrelatedIncident(events=list(events), connectors=connectors)
000074 | [blank]
000075 | [blank]
000076 | def correlate(
000077 |     events: list[ConnectorEvent],
000078 |     window_seconds: int = DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS,
000079 | ) -> list[CorrelatedIncident]:
000080 |     """Merge ConnectorEvents from any number of connectors onto one timeline and
000081 |     cluster the ones that coincide. Events (from any mix of connectors) that are
000082 |     within `window_seconds` of the running cluster join it; a larger gap starts a
000083 |     new incident. Returns incidents in chronological order.
000084 | [blank]
000085 |     The join is what makes "pod crash + Datadog spike" resolve to ONE incident
000086 |     with two connectors instead of two separate single-source alerts.
000087 |     """
000088 |     if not events:
000089 |         return []
000090 | [blank]
000091 |     ordered = sorted(events, key=lambda e: _as_utc(e["timestamp"]))
000092 |     incidents: list[CorrelatedIncident] = []
000093 |     cluster: list[ConnectorEvent] = [ordered[0]]
000094 | [blank]
000095 |     for event in ordered[1:]:
000096 |         gap = (_as_utc(event["timestamp"]) - _as_utc(cluster[-1]["timestamp"])).total_seconds()
000097 |         if gap <= window_seconds:
000098 |             cluster.append(event)
000099 |         else:
000100 |             incidents.append(_make_incident(cluster))
000101 |             cluster = [event]
000102 |     incidents.append(_make_incident(cluster))
000103 |     return incidents
000104 | [blank]
000105 | [blank]
000106 | def format_incident_context(incident: CorrelatedIncident) -> str:
000107 |     """Render one correlated incident as the unified-timeline text block the
000108 |     diagnosis brain reads — so a multi-source incident is presented as a single
000109 |     thing to diagnose, not N separate log streams. Mirrors the =SECTION= style
000110 |     of diagnosis_agent.py's format_*_context helpers."""
000111 |     n_conn = len(incident.connectors)
000112 |     header = (
000113 |         f"=== CORRELATED INCIDENT ({len(incident.events)} events across "
000114 |         f"{n_conn} connector{'s' if n_conn != 1 else ''}: {', '.join(incident.connectors)}) ==="
000115 |     )
000116 |     lines = [header, "", "=== UNIFIED TIMELINE ==="]
000117 |     for e in incident.events:
000118 |         ts = _as_utc(e["timestamp"]).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
000119 |         lines.append(f"- {ts} [{e.get('connector', '?')}/{e.get('event_type', '?')}] {e.get('summary', '')}")
000120 |     lines.append("")
000121 |     if incident.is_multi_source:
000122 |         lines.append(
000123 |             "These events span multiple connectors within one time window and "
000124 |             "very likely share ONE root cause — diagnose them together as a "
000125 |             "single incident, cross-checking the signals, not as separate alerts."
000126 |         )
000127 |     else:
000128 |         lines.append(
000129 |             "Single-source incident — no corroborating signal from another "
000130 |             "connector in this window."
000131 |         )
000132 |     return "\n".join(lines)
000133 | [blank]
000134 | [blank]
000135 | def correlate_and_format(
000136 |     events: list[ConnectorEvent],
000137 |     window_seconds: int = DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS,
000138 | ) -> str:
000139 |     """Convenience: correlate, then render every incident into one block for the
000140 |     brain. Multi-source incidents are listed first — they're the ones where
000141 |     correlation improves the diagnosis."""
000142 |     incidents = correlate(events, window_seconds=window_seconds)
000143 |     incidents.sort(key=lambda inc: (not inc.is_multi_source, inc.start))
000144 |     return "\n\n".join(format_incident_context(inc) for inc in incidents)
````

````text
000436 | For any file that already exists, you MUST follow these rules without exception:
000437 | [blank]
000438 | 1. USE edits, NOT new_content, FOR EXISTING FILES. This is the most important rule in \
000439 |    this section. Regenerating a whole file and calling it new_content depends on you \
000440 |    perfectly reproducing every line you didn't mean to touch — and live testing proved \
000441 |    this fails in practice: two separate real fixes (2026-08-17) each contained the \
000442 |    correct change PLUS unrelated deleted comment lines, silently, with no way to catch \
000443 |    it before the PR shipped. edits cannot have this failure mode BY CONSTRUCTION — \
000444 |    content outside what old_content matches is never touched, because it's never even \
000445 |    regenerated. (This is not the "patch" field you may have seen warnings about \
000446 |    elsewhere — that was traditional line-numbered unified-diff hunks, which really are \
000447 |    fragile against whitespace drift. edits use exact substring matching instead: no \
000448 |    line numbers, no context-window fuzziness, just "this exact text becomes that exact \
000449 |    text." It either matches or it fails loudly — it cannot silently apply wrong.)
000450 | [blank]
000451 | 2. old_content MUST BE COPIED VERBATIM from the real file content you were shown or \
000452 |    fetched — exact whitespace, exact indentation, exact surrounding characters. Do not \
000453 |    retype it from memory or "clean it up." If you paraphrase even slightly, the edit \
000454 |    will fail to match and the whole fix is rejected.
000455 | [blank]
000456 | 3. old_content MUST BE UNIQUE in the file. If the line you're changing could appear \
000457 |    more than once (a common variable name, a repeated pattern), include enough \
000458 |    surrounding lines in old_content to make the match unambiguous. An edit that matches \
000459 |    zero times OR more than once fails — it does not guess.
000460 | [blank]
000461 | 4. KEEP EACH EDIT SMALL. old_content should be the smallest span that still uniquely \
000462 |    identifies the right spot — usually the single changed line plus a line or two of \
000463 |    context, not the whole surrounding function. If two separate spots in the same file \
000464 |    need to change, submit two separate edits in the `edits` array rather than one giant \
000465 |    old_content spanning both.

000580 | When you see dependency version conflicts:
000581 |   npm: "ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree", "Could not resolve dependency"
000582 |   pip: "ResolutionImpossible", "ERROR: Cannot install X and Y because..."
000583 |   yarn: "has unmet peer dependency"
000584 | [blank]
000585 | FIX STRATEGY:
000586 | 1. Read the conflict message carefully — it tells you exactly which packages clash.
000587 | 2. For npm ERESOLVE: update the conflicting version range in package.json, \
000588 |    or add an "overrides" field. Prefer bumping to a compatible version.
000589 | 3. For pip: adjust version pins in requirements.txt/pyproject.toml to find a compatible set. \
000590 |    If pkg A needs X>=2.0 and pkg B needs X<2.0, check if either has a newer release.
000591 | 4. For peer dependency warnings: add the peer dep explicitly to package.json.
000592 | 5. Use one edits entry per version line you're changing — old_content is that one line \
000593 |    (e.g. `"react": "^17.0.2"`) copied verbatim from the file content you were shown.
000594 | 6. These are safe_auto_apply with high confidence when the conflict message is clear.
000595 | 7. DEPENDENCY CHAIN COMPLETENESS — when a package has known peer or type companions, bump ALL of \
000596 |    them together in the SAME package.json fix, matching major versions:
000597 |      react ↔ react-dom ↔ @types/react ↔ @types/react-dom
000598 |      vue ↔ @vue/compiler-sfc ↔ @vue/runtime-core
000599 |      @angular/core ↔ @angular/common ↔ @angular/compiler
000600 |    Bumping react to ^18 while leaving @types/react on ^17 is an INCOMPLETE fix — it will pass a \
000601 |    naive check but break the type build or runtime. A deterministic guardrail checks major-version \
000602 |    alignment across these pairs and downgrades to review_recommended if you miss one, so get it \
000603 |    right the first time: read every companion package's current version in the provided file \
000604 |    content, and submit a separate edit bumping every one that's out of sync with the package \
000605 |    you're actually fixing — not just the one named in the error message.

000622 | ROOT CAUSE VS SUPPRESSION — when a linter, type checker, or static analyzer fails
000623 | ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
000624 | [blank]
000625 | When PHPStan, ESLint, mypy, tsc, or a similar analysis tool fails, there are always
000626 | two ways to make the check pass: fix the code the tool is correctly flagging, or
000627 | loosen the tool so it stops flagging it. These are NOT equivalent fixes.
000628 | [blank]
000629 | FIX STRATEGY — in this order:
000630 | 1. Read what the tool is ACTUALLY complaining about (the specific type error, the
000631 |    specific rule violation) and fix that in the source: add the missing type
000632 |    annotation, add the null check, cast the value, add the missing return path.
000633 |    This is the real fix — prefer it whenever the change is small and scoped.
000634 | 2. Only fall back to loosening the tool itself (lowering a PHPStan `level`,
000635 |    dropping a tsconfig `strict` flag, disabling an ESLint rule, adding
000636 |    `# type: ignore` / `@ts-ignore` / `// eslint-disable`) when the real fix would
000637 |    require touching code far outside the scope of this failure, or you genuinely
000638 |    cannot determine the correct fix from the available context.
000639 | 3. If you DO fall back to loosening the check, you MUST say so explicitly and
000640 |    honestly in fix_description — state plainly that this suppresses the check
000641 |    rather than resolving what it caught, e.g. start the description with
000642 |    "Note: this relaxes the analyzer rather than fixing the underlying issue —".
000643 |    Do not describe a suppression as if it were a resolution. A confident-sounding
000644 |    description that hides what the fix actually does is worse than an honest
000645 |    low-confidence one.
````
