### `prash/connectors/pagerduty.py`
````text
000001 | """PagerDuty connector (Sprint 2 Tier 3, PRASH_V2.md §7b).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Read + a scoped pair of write actions (acknowledge/resolve an incident) --
000004 | per Aradhya's explicit call, since PagerDuty's actual value is arguably the
000005 | write side, not just reading state (unlike Datadog/Grafana, which stayed
000006 | read-only for their first pass, matching every other connector's v1
000007 | posture).
000008 | [blank]
000009 | `resource` is a PagerDuty *service* name or id -- the persistent thing you
000010 | check on, the same role a Datadog monitor or Grafana alert rule plays here.
000011 | poll_state() reports whatever triggered/acknowledged incidents currently
000012 | exist for that service; the write methods (acknowledge_incident /
000013 | resolve_incident, called from prash/actions/pagerduty_incident.py) then act
000014 | on one specific incident by its id, which poll_state()'s detail surfaces --
000015 | the same relationship this repo's other connectors already have between a
000016 | broad resource and a specific sub-target (a pod vs. its Deployment for
000017 | rollback; a monitor vs. the alert instance for Grafana).
000018 | [blank]
000019 | Auth is a REST API key via `Authorization: Token token=...` (works for both
000020 | account-level API keys and user-scoped tokens) -- checked against
000021 | `/abilities`, which needs nothing beyond a valid token. Writes additionally
000022 | require identifying WHO is making the change: PagerDuty's API rejects a
000023 | status update with no `From: <email>` header naming a real user on the
000024 | account, so PAGERDUTY_FROM_EMAIL is a second, write-only-required
000025 | credential -- reads work with just the API key.
000026 | [blank]
000027 | trigger_event() (added 2026-08-19, wired to the Gitleaks-escalation action)
000028 | uses a genuinely different PagerDuty mechanism from everything else in this
000029 | file: the Events API v2 (`events.pagerduty.com`, not `api.pagerduty.com`),
000030 | authenticated by a per-service integration/routing key
000031 | (PAGERDUTY_ROUTING_KEY), not the REST API key. This is intentional, not an
000032 | inconsistency to clean up -- creating a NEW incident from an external
000033 | system and updating the status of an EXISTING incident are different
000034 | PagerDuty products with different auth models; conflating them would mean
000035 | guessing at which key does what.
000036 | [blank]
000037 | Full autonomous loop (CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC §4a/§4b/§4c, Phase 3 rollout):
000038 | watch() returns a per-service WatchHandle that lists the service's incidents
000039 | each poll() and emits ConnectorEvents only on transitions -- new triggers,
000040 | acknowledgments, resolutions, and reassignments/escalations -- de-duplicated
000041 | by incident id + status + assignment signature across polls. get_stats()
000042 | normalizes either an incident's log-entry timeline or a service's incident
000043 | window (plus account change events as correlation context) into
000044 | ConnectorEvents. page_oncall() is the primitive behind the APPROVAL-gated

000123 | def _parse_ts(value: Any) -> Optional[datetime]:
000124 |     """Best-effort PagerDuty timestamp (ISO-8601) -> aware UTC datetime."""
000125 |     if value is None:
000126 |         return None
000127 |     if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
000128 |         if value > 1e11:  # epoch milliseconds
000129 |             value = value / 1000.0
000130 |         return datetime.fromtimestamp(value, tz=timezone.utc)
000131 |     text = str(value).strip()
000132 |     if not text:
000133 |         return None
000134 |     if text.replace(".", "", 1).isdigit():
000135 |         return _parse_ts(float(text))
000136 |     try:
000137 |         return datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace("Z", "+00:00")).astimezone(timezone.utc)
000138 |     except ValueError:
000139 |         return None

000142 | def _incident_severity(incident: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:

000144 | [blank]
000145 |     A triggered incident with no priority object still has urgency, and
000146 |     "high urgency, no priority" is worth more than a bare "unknown".
000147 |     """
000148 |     priority = (incident.get("priority") or {}).get("summary")
000149 |     if priority:
000150 |         return _PRIORITY_SEVERITY.get(str(priority).upper(), "medium")
000151 |     return "high" if incident.get("urgency") == "high" else "low"

000156 |         str((a.get("assignee") or {}).get("id") or "")
000157 |         for a in incident.get("assignments") or []

000161 | class _PagerDutyWatchHandle(WatchHandle):
000162 |     """Per-service watch handle: one poll() = one incident list, diffed per incident.
000163 | [blank]
000164 |     Dedup contract (the whole point of the watcher): the same incident in
000165 |     the same state across polls is silent -- only a NEW trigger, a status
000166 |     transition, or a reassignment/escalation emits an event.
000167 |     """
000168 | [blank]
000169 |     def __init__(self, connector: "PagerDutyConnector", target: str, service_id: str,
000170 |                  service_name: str, interval: int, last_state: Dict[str, Tuple[str, Tuple[str, ...]]]):
000171 |         self.connector = connector.name
000172 |         self.target = target
000173 |         self.interval = interval
000174 |         self.service_id = service_id
000175 |         self.service_name = service_name
000176 |         self._pd = connector
000177 |         self._last_state = last_state
000178 | [blank]
000179 |     def poll(self) -> List[ConnectorEvent]:
000180 |         incidents = self._pd._service_incidents(self.service_id)
000181 |         events: List[ConnectorEvent] = []
000182 |         for incident in incidents:
000183 |             inc_id = str(incident.get("id") or "")
000184 |             if not inc_id:
000185 |                 continue
000186 |             status = incident.get("status") or "unknown"
000187 |             sig = _assignments_sig(incident)
000188 |             previous = self._last_state.get(inc_id)
000189 |             self._last_state[inc_id] = (status, sig)
000190 |             if previous is None:
000191 |                 # First sighting: an open incident is page-worthy; a resolved
000192 |                 # one is history predating the watch -- baseline it silently.
000193 |                 if status != "resolved":
000194 |                     events.append(self._pd._incident_event(incident, "incident_triggered", self.service_name))
000195 |                 continue
000196 |             prev_status, prev_assignments = previous
000197 |             if prev_status == status and prev_assignments == sig:
000198 |                 continue  # the core dedup guarantee: same incident, same state -> silence
000199 |             if status != prev_status:
000200 |                 event_type = _STATUS_EVENT_MAP.get(status, "incident_state_changed")
000201 |             else:
000202 |                 # Same status, different assignees: escalation to the next
000203 |                 # rotation or a manual reassignment -- worth a fresh ping.
000204 |                 event_type = "incident_escalated"
000205 |             events.append(self._pd._incident_event(incident, event_type, self.service_name, previous_status=prev_status))
000206 |         return events

000230 |     def _refresh_credentials(self) -> bool:
000231 |         """Re-read the REST credentials from the environment (key rotation).
000232 | [blank]
000233 |         Returns True when the API key actually changed, i.e. a retry has a
000234 |         chance of succeeding. Absent env vars fall back to current values.
000235 |         """
000236 |         new_api = os.environ.get("PAGERDUTY_API_KEY") or self.api_key
000237 |         new_from = os.environ.get("PAGERDUTY_FROM_EMAIL") or self.from_email
000238 |         changed = bool(new_api) and new_api != self.api_key
000239 |         self.api_key = new_api
000240 |         self.from_email = new_from
000241 |         return changed

000243 |     @staticmethod
000244 |     def _backoff_seconds(attempt: int, exc: urllib.error.HTTPError) -> float:
000245 |         """Capped exponential backoff; a 429's Retry-After header wins when present."""
000246 |         if exc.code == 429:
000247 |             headers = getattr(exc, "headers", None)
000248 |             retry_after = headers.get("Retry-After") if headers is not None else None
000249 |             if retry_after:
000250 |                 try:
000251 |                     return float(retry_after)
000252 |                 except (TypeError, ValueError):
000253 |                     pass
000254 |         return min(2 ** attempt, _BACKOFF_CAP)

000256 |     def _request(self, method: str, path: str, body: Any = None, need_from: bool = False,
000257 |                  timeout: int = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) -> Any:
000258 |         data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8") if body is not None else None
000259 |         rotated = False
000260 |         attempt = 0
000261 |         while True:
000262 |             req = urllib.request.Request(f"{API_URL}{path}", data=data, headers=self._headers(need_from), method=method)
000263 |             try:
000264 |                 with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
000265 |                     raw = resp.read()
000266 |                     return json.loads(raw) if raw else {}
000267 |             except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
000268 |                 message = f"PagerDuty API {exc.code}: {exc.read().decode('utf-8', errors='replace')[:300]}"
000269 |                 if exc.code == 401 and not rotated:
000270 |                     # The key may have been rotated since startup; re-read the
000271 |                     # environment once before treating this as permanent.
000272 |                     rotated = True
000273 |                     if self._refresh_credentials():
000274 |                         continue
000275 |                     raise PagerDutyError(message) from exc
000276 |                 if exc.code in _TRANSIENT_STATUS and attempt < _MAX_RETRIES:
000277 |                     time.sleep(self._backoff_seconds(attempt, exc))
000278 |                     attempt += 1
000279 |                     continue
000280 |                 raise PagerDutyError(message) from exc
000281 |             except (socket.timeout, urllib.error.URLError) as exc:
000282 |                 if attempt < _MAX_RETRIES:
000283 |                     time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt, _BACKOFF_CAP))
000284 |                     attempt += 1
000285 |                     continue
000286 |                 raise PagerDutyError(f"PagerDuty API unreachable: {exc}") from exc

000300 |                 with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=SHORT_TIMEOUT) as resp:
000301 |                     raw = resp.read()

000305 |                 if exc.code in _TRANSIENT_STATUS and attempt < _MAX_RETRIES:
000306 |                     time.sleep(self._backoff_seconds(attempt, exc))
000307 |                     attempt += 1
000308 |                     continue
000309 |                 raise PagerDutyError(message) from exc
000310 |             except (socket.timeout, urllib.error.URLError) as exc:
000311 |                 if attempt < _MAX_RETRIES:
000312 |                     time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt, _BACKOFF_CAP))
000313 |                     attempt += 1

000317 |     def _paginate(self, path: str, cap: int = 200) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
000318 |         """Walk a REST v2 list endpoint (limit/offset + `more` flag, NOT
000319 |         cursor-based) under a hard cap -- the rate-limit-friendly guard
000320 |         against a runaway list call. Understands the collection keys of the
000321 |         five endpoints this connector actually paginates."""
000322 |         items: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
000323 |         offset = 0
000324 |         limit = 100
000325 |         while True:
000326 |             sep = "&" if "?" in path else "?"
000327 |             resp = self._request("GET", f"{path}{sep}offset={offset}&limit={limit}")
000328 |             if not isinstance(resp, dict):
000329 |                 break
000330 |             batch = (resp.get("incidents") or resp.get("log_entries")
000331 |                      or resp.get("services") or resp.get("change_events")
000332 |                      or resp.get("alerts") or [])
000333 |             items.extend(item for item in batch if isinstance(item, dict))
000334 |             if len(items) >= cap or not resp.get("more", False):
000335 |                 break
000336 |             offset += limit
000337 |         return items[:cap]

000339 |     def authenticate(self) -> bool:
000340 |         if not self.api_key:
000341 |             self.auth_error = "PagerDuty API key is required"
000342 |             return False
000343 |         try:
000344 |             # /abilities needs nothing beyond a valid token -- works for
000345 |             # both account-level and user-scoped REST API keys, per this
000346 |             # file's own module docstring -- so it's the liveness check,
000347 |             # not /users/me (which only a user-scoped token can answer).
000348 |             self._request("GET", "/abilities", timeout=SHORT_TIMEOUT)
000349 |         except PagerDutyError as exc:
000350 |             self.auth_identity = {}
000351 |             self.auth_error = str(exc)
000352 |             return False
000353 | [blank]
000354 |         # Best-effort identity enrichment. Found live 2026-09-16: a real,
000355 |         # valid account-level API key 400s on /users/me ("unable to
000356 |         # determine the user's identity... use a user-level token") -- a
000357 |         # token-type gap, not proof the connection is bad, so it must not
000358 |         # fail authenticate() outright once /abilities already proved the
000359 |         # token live.
000360 |         try:
000361 |             resp = self._request("GET", "/users/me", timeout=SHORT_TIMEOUT)
000362 |             user = resp.get("user", resp) if isinstance(resp, dict) else {}
000363 |             self.auth_identity = {
000364 |                 key: value for key, value in {
000365 |                     "user": user.get("name"),
000366 |                     "email": user.get("email"),
000367 |                 }.items() if value
000368 |             }
000369 |         except PagerDutyError:
000370 |             self.auth_identity = {}
000371 |         self.auth_error = None
000372 |         return True

000374 |     def locate(self, resource: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:

000378 |             resp = self._request("GET", f"/services?query={urllib.parse.quote(resource)}", timeout=SHORT_TIMEOUT)

000442 |     def watch(self, target: str, interval: int = 30) -> WatchHandle:
000443 |         """Begin watching a service (CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC §4a).
000444 | [blank]
000445 |         The returned handle lists the service's incidents (all statuses, so
000446 |         resolutions are visible) each poll() and emits ConnectorEvents only
000447 |         for transitions: new triggers, acknowledgments, resolutions, and
000448 |         reassignments/escalations -- de-duplicated across polls by incident
000449 |         id + status + assignment signature. Multiple services = multiple
000450 |         handles; the shared watcher loop owns the cadence.
000451 |         """
000452 |         handle = self.locate(target)
000453 |         if not handle:
000454 |             raise PagerDutyError(f"service not found: {target}")
000455 |         last_state: Dict[str, Tuple[str, Tuple[str, ...]]] = {}
000456 |         for incident in self._service_incidents(handle["service_id"]):
000457 |             inc_id = str(incident.get("id") or "")
000458 |             if inc_id:
000459 |                 last_state[inc_id] = (incident.get("status") or "unknown", _assignments_sig(incident))
000460 |         return _PagerDutyWatchHandle(self, target, handle["service_id"], handle.get("name") or target, interval, last_state)

000462 |     def get_stats(self, target: str, since: Optional[datetime] = None,
000463 |                   include_change_events: bool = True) -> List[ConnectorEvent]:
000464 |         """Normalized timeline for a PagerDuty target (CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC §4a).
000465 | [blank]
000466 |         Two modes, resolved automatically: an incident id gets its full
000467 |         log-entry timeline (trigger/ack/escalate/resolve per entry); a
000468 |         service name/id gets its incident window (one event per incident)
000469 |         plus account-wide change events as deploy-correlation context --
000470 |         the /change_events endpoint has no service filter, so these are
000471 |         context, not per-service facts. Ascending by timestamp, everything
000472 |         after `since` (default: the last hour). [] when nothing resolves.
000473 |         """
000474 |         if since is None:
000475 |             since = _utcnow() - timedelta(hours=1)
000476 |         elif since.tzinfo is None:
000477 |             since = since.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
000478 |         events = self._incident_log_events(target, since)
000479 |         if events is None:
000480 |             handle = self.locate(target)
000481 |             if not handle:
000482 |                 return []
000483 |             events = self._service_window_events(handle, since, include_change_events)
000484 |         events.sort(key=lambda event: event["timestamp"])
000485 |         return events

000487 |     def _incident_log_events(self, target: str, since: datetime) -> Optional[List[ConnectorEvent]]:
000488 |         """Log-entry timeline for one incident, or None when `target` isn't
000489 |         an incident id (falls through to service mode)."""
000490 |         try:
000491 |             resp = self._request("GET", f"/incidents/{target}", timeout=SHORT_TIMEOUT)
000492 |         except PagerDutyError:
000493 |             return None
000494 |         incident = resp.get("incident", resp) if isinstance(resp, dict) else {}
000495 |         if not isinstance(incident, dict) or not incident.get("id"):
000496 |             return None
000497 |         entries = self._paginate(f"/incidents/{target}/log_entries?include[]=channels")
000498 |         events: List[ConnectorEvent] = []
000499 |         for entry in entries:
000500 |             ts = _parse_ts(entry.get("created_at"))
000501 |             if ts is None or ts < since:
000502 |                 continue
000503 |             events.append(ConnectorEvent(
000504 |                 timestamp=ts,
000505 |                 connector=self.name,
000506 |                 event_type=_LOG_ENTRY_TYPE_MAP.get(str(entry.get("type", "")), "log_entry"),
000507 |                 summary=str(entry.get("summary") or entry.get("type") or "(log entry)"),
000508 |                 raw={"entry_id": entry.get("id"), "log_entry": entry, "incident_id": target},
000509 |             ))
000510 |         return events

000512 |     def _service_window_events(self, handle: Dict[str, Any], since: datetime,
000513 |                                include_change_events: bool) -> List[ConnectorEvent]:
000514 |         service_id = handle["service_id"]
000515 |         service_name = handle.get("name") or service_id
000516 |         status_query = "&".join(f"statuses[]={s}" for s in _WATCH_STATUSES)
000517 |         until = _utcnow()
000518 |         path = (f"/incidents?service_ids[]={service_id}&{status_query}"
````

````text
000001 | """Snyk connector (Sprint 2 Tier 3, PRASH_V2.md §7b).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Read-only for this sprint, same posture Datadog/Grafana shipped with --
000004 | security scanning state is worth surfacing before it's worth acting on
000005 | automatically (unlike PagerDuty, where Aradhya explicitly asked for write
000006 | actions from the start).
000007 | [blank]
000008 | Snyk is org-scoped end to end: every project lives under an org id, so
000009 | SNYK_ORG_ID is a required credential, not optional -- there is no
000010 | account-wide "just give me everything" call. `resource` is a project id
000011 | (a UUID) or project name, resolved by listing `/v1/org/{orgId}/projects`
000012 | and matching client-side (no server-side name filter on that endpoint,
000013 | same known limitation already documented in the Grafana connector for the
000014 | same reason -- fine for v1, worth revisiting against an org with many
000015 | projects).
000016 | [blank]
000017 | KNOWN BROKEN (found live, 2026-09-16): Snyk's v1 API is now fully removed,
000018 | not just deprecated -- /v1/org/{id} 404s with "unsupported url" against a
000019 | real account, confirmed live. authenticate() was migrated to the REST
000020 | equivalent (/rest/orgs/{id}), with the org-name lookup made best-effort
000021 | (the /rest/self check alone proves the token is live, per its own
000022 | default_org_context field) since a real token on a real account 403'd on
000023 | that specific call -- a token-scope gap, not proof of a bad connection.
000024 | locate() (line ~101) and ignore_issue()'s write path (line ~158) are NOT
000025 | yet migrated -- they still call the dead v1 API and will fail. Left
000026 | unmigrated deliberately: the only live token available to verify against
000027 | 403s on every org-scoped REST call tried (both /rest/orgs/{id} and
000028 | /rest/orgs/{id}/projects), so a locate() rewrite couldn't be verified to
000029 | actually work, and ignore_issue() is a write action that shouldn't be
000030 | migrated blind without a way to test-fire it safely. Needs a token with
000031 | proper org-read scope (and org-write for ignore_issue) before finishing
000032 | this migration.
000033 | [blank]
000034 | Snyk's own `issueCountsBySeverity` rollup on a project (critical/high/
000035 | medium/low counts) is the direct analog of a Datadog monitor's
000036 | overall_state or a Grafana alert rule's firing state -- one number per

000039 | follows the common security-team gating convention: critical or high
000040 | counts as FAILED (block-worthy), medium alone as DEGRADED (watch), only
000041 | low or clean as HEALTHY.
000042 | [blank]
000043 | fetch_logs() deliberately does NOT call Snyk's per-issue listing endpoint

000173 |     def ignore_issue(self, project_id: str, issue_id: str, reason: str, expires_days: int = 30) -> Dict[str, Any]:
000174 |         """Ignore a specific vulnerability on a project for a bounded time.
000175 |         Write action added 2026-08-19 (PRASH_V2.md §7b), deliberately

000177 |         is a real judgment call, not a neutral operation, so it always

000180 |         by `expires_days` -- an ignore that silently became permanent would
000181 |         misrepresent what was actually approved."""
000182 |         expires = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=expires_days)).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z")
000183 |         body = {
000184 |             "reason": reason,
000185 |             "reasonType": "temporary-ignore",
000186 |             "ignoredBy": {"name": "Prash"},
000187 |             "expires": expires,
000188 |         }
000189 |         return self._request(
000190 |             "POST",
000191 |             f"/v1/org/{urllib.parse.quote(self.org_id or '')}/project/{project_id}/ignore/{issue_id}",
000192 |             body=body,
000193 |         )
````

### `prash/connectors/testdata/wedged-pod.yaml`

````text
000001 | # Deliberately WEDGED (not deterministically broken) deployment, built to
000002 | # test the "brain recommends restart_pod" path in prash fix. Container runs
000003 | # `sleep infinity` -- it never exits, never restarts, writes nothing to logs
000004 | # -- but its readinessProbe points at a port nothing listens on, so it never
000005 | # becomes Ready. No scheduling-failure event, no crash, no descriptive error
000006 | # anywhere -- just a pod that looks like it might be a slow/stuck startup.
000007 | #
000008 | # Live-tested 2026-08-15 (PRASH_V2.md §10): the brain read this correctly as
000009 | # a deterministic wrong-image config issue (busybox has no HTTP server, so
000010 | # the probe can never pass) and declined to recommend restart_pod -- a
000011 | # defensible, well-reasoned call, not a bug. This is the second fixture
000012 | # (after the 2026-08-13 ConfigMap-flag one) built specifically to probe the
000013 | # ambiguous "restart might help" case and get a confident, correct decline
000014 | # instead. Kept as a reusable fixture regardless -- still exercises the
000015 | # StuckPending classification path -- but don't expect it alone to produce
000016 | # a live restart_pod recommendation; that needs either a genuinely
000017 | # recoverable-by-restart failure (hard to construct reliably) or the
000018 | # "ask, don't quit" options-flow work (§9, 2026-08-14) to make the case moot.
000019 | #
000020 | # Apply:  kubectl apply -f prash/connectors/testdata/wedged-pod.yaml
000021 | # Watch:  kubectl get pods -n prash-demo -w
000022 | # Clean:  kubectl delete -f prash/connectors/testdata/wedged-pod.yaml
000023 | apiVersion: apps/v1
000024 | kind: Deployment
000025 | metadata:
000026 |   name: wedged-app
000027 |   namespace: prash-demo
000028 | spec:
000029 |   replicas: 1
000030 |   selector:
000031 |     matchLabels:
000032 |       app: wedged-app
000033 |   template:
000034 |     metadata:
000035 |       labels:
000036 |         app: wedged-app
000037 |     spec:
000038 |       containers:
000039 |         - name: wedged-app
000040 |           image: busybox:latest
000041 |           command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
000042 |           readinessProbe:

000045 |             initialDelaySeconds: 5
000046 |             periodSeconds: 5
````

````text
000112 |     def production_deployment_id(self, resource: str) -> str | None:
000113 |         """The deployment currently aliased to production -- NOT the same as
000114 |         "most recent deployment" (poll_state's notion). A rollback re-points
000115 |         the production alias to an existing, older deployment without
000116 |         creating anything new, so the most-recently-created deployment never
000117 |         changes when a rollback succeeds. Verifying rollback against
000118 |         poll_state() was structurally guaranteed to report failure on every
000119 |         successful rollback -- found live, 2026-08-24, testing a real
000120 |         rollback that Vercel confirmed succeeded while verify() called it a
000121 |         failure. This reads /v9/projects/{id}'s targets.production.id, the
000122 |         field that actually reflects what's live."""
000123 |         handle = self.locate(resource)
000124 |         try:
000125 |             project = self._request("GET", f"/v9/projects/{handle['project']}")
000126 |         except VercelError:
000127 |             return None
000128 |         return (project.get("targets") or {}).get("production", {}).get("id")
000129 | [blank]
000130 |     def rollback(self, resource: str, deployment_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
000131 |         """Point production at a specific earlier deployment via Vercel's
000132 |         dedicated Rollback API. Unlike redeploy(), this requires an explicit
000133 |         deployment_id -- rolling back to "whatever's most recent" would just
000134 |         be a redeploy, not a rollback."""
000135 |         handle = self.locate(resource)
000136 |         return self._request("POST", f"/v9/projects/{handle['project']}/rollback/{deployment_id}")
````

### `prash/credentials.py`
````text
000001 | """Local credentials + secrets loader.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Credentials live in a local file under the user's control, always. Drufiy's
000004 | servers never receive them. This is the whole trust model of Lear, so the
000005 | loader is deliberately small and dependency-free.
000006 | [blank]
000007 | Format is a simple ``KEY=VALUE`` line file (``.env`` style). ``#`` starts a
000008 | comment. The same file also carries the secrets Prash has been given (e.g. the
000009 | missing-secret action), with ``PRASH_SECRET_<name>`` keys.
000010 | """
000011 | [blank]
000012 | from __future__ import annotations
000013 | [blank]
000014 | import os
000015 | import re
000016 | from dataclasses import dataclass
000017 | from pathlib import Path
000018 | from typing import Any, Dict, Mapping, Optional
000019 | [blank]
000020 | _LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=\s*(.*?)\s*$")
000021 | _SECRET_PREFIX = "PRASH_SECRET_"
000022 | [blank]
000023 | [blank]
000024 | @dataclass
000025 | class CredentialStore:
000026 |     path: Path
000027 | [blank]
000028 |     @classmethod
000029 |     def from_env(cls) -> "CredentialStore":
000030 |         explicit = os.environ.get("PRASH_ENV")
000031 |         if explicit:
000032 |             return cls(path=Path(explicit).expanduser())
000033 |         cwd_env = Path(".env")
000034 |         if cwd_env.exists():
000035 |             return cls(path=cwd_env)
000036 |         return cls(path=Path("~/.prash/.env").expanduser())
000037 | [blank]
000038 |     def load(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
000039 |         if not self.path.exists():
000040 |             return {}
000041 |         data: Dict[str, Any] = {}
000042 |         for raw in self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
000043 |             line = raw.strip()
000044 |             if not line or line.startswith("#"):
000045 |                 continue
000046 |             match = _LINE_RE.match(line)
000047 |             if match:
000048 |                 key, value = match.groups()
000049 |                 data[key] = value.strip('"').strip("'")
000050 |         return data
000051 | [blank]
000052 |     def secrets(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
000053 |         """Only the PRASH_SECRET_* entries, keys without the prefix."""
000054 |         all_data = self.load()
000055 |         return {
000056 |             k[len(_SECRET_PREFIX):]: str(v)
000057 |             for k, v in all_data.items()
000058 |             if k.startswith(_SECRET_PREFIX)
000059 |         }
000060 | [blank]
000061 |     def set_secret(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
000062 |         """Write a secret value to the local file. Appends; never rewrites."""
000063 |         self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
000064 |         self.path.touch(exist_ok=True)
000065 |         with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
000066 |             fh.write(f"{_SECRET_PREFIX}{name}={value}\n")
000067 | [blank]
000068 |     def sanitized(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
000069 |         """Credentials safe for display: secret values redacted."""
000070 |         return {k: ("<redacted>" if k.startswith(_SECRET_PREFIX) else v) for k, v in self.load().items()}
````

````text
000002 | [blank]
000003 | This is Track A's orchestrator. It owns the pipeline the CLI drives:
000004 | [blank]

000006 | 2. Build its Plan (dry-run safe, touches nothing).

000008 |    escalate to a human (day 7 safety rail), never execute.
000009 | 4. Ask the permission engine for a Decision (mode + tier + environment).
000010 | 5. REFUSE -> record in audit, return a refused result. Never executes.
000011 | 6. PROMPT -> hand the plan to the interface (CLI) to ask the user.
000012 | 7. Execute, then Verify honestly. Every actual execution is recorded in the
000013 |    circuit breaker so loops trip it.
000014 | 8. Append an audit entry for everything that happened.
000015 | """
````

````text
000087 | async def diagnose_k8s_pod(

000094 |     """Gather Track B's status/logs/events for a pod, feed them to Track D's
000095 |     brain, and return the Diagnosis. Raises FixTargetError if the pod isn't
000096 |     there — get_pod_status() is 404-as-empty-list by contract, so an empty
000097 |     list is the not-found signal, not an exception.
000098 | [blank]
000099 |     When ``repo`` + ``access_token`` are supplied, the brain additionally gets
000100 |     the investigation tools (fetch_file / list_directory / search_code) pointed
000101 |     at the repository holding the Deployment manifest, so it can read the
000102 |     manifest and propose a corrected one.
000103 | [blank]
000104 |     Why this exists (root cause found 2026-08-16, PRASH_V2.md §9): without a
000105 |     repo, a runtime diagnosis can only ever answer restart_pod / rollback /
000106 |     scale -- and since most real Kubernetes failures (missing config, bad image
000107 |     tag, OOM limits, unmounted ConfigMap) are fixed by editing a manifest, not
000108 |     by restarting, Prash correctly declined essentially every real case. Six
000109 |     live diagnoses, six honest "no action can help" verdicts. Correct every
000110 |     time, and useless every time. Reading the manifest is what turns that into
000111 |     a fix.
000112 |     """
000113 |     pods = get_pod_status(namespace, pod)
000114 |     if not pods:
000115 |         raise FixTargetError(f"pod {namespace}/{pod} not found")
000116 |     pod_status = pods[0]
000117 |     # get_pod_status() resolves a Deployment/friendly name (e.g. "broken-app")
000118 |     # to the actual running pod (e.g. "broken-app-6b58dc6d7b-fphhd") -- use
000119 |     # THAT resolved name from here on, not the original `pod` argument, or
000120 |     # get_pod_logs()/get_pod_events() below 404 on the very name
000121 |     # get_pod_status() just proved doesn't exist as a literal pod.
000122 |     pod = pod_status.name
000123 |     logs = get_pod_logs(namespace, pod)
000124 |     events = get_pod_events(namespace, pod)

000416 |     (the caller renders it and checks there is something to fix). This loop
000417 |     applies that fix, waits for the fix branch's CI run, and if it fails with
000418 |     the IDENTICAL error signature re-diagnoses with `repeated_failure=True`
000419 |     to force a different hypothesis — the previous fix did not address the
000420 |     real cause. If the signature CHANGED, the fix altered the failure, so
000421 |     re-diagnose normally against the new evidence.
000422 | [blank]

000424 |     language in the repeated-failure directive: "Repeating the same hypothesis
000425 |     will exhaust the remaining retry budget with no progress"). Stops the
000426 |     moment a run passes. Never silently drops a partial fix: if the budget is
000427 |     exhausted while runs still fail, the last result is returned and the
000428 |     already-open PR stays open for a human.

000431 |     result = first_result

000434 |     )
````

### `prash/intent.py`
````text
000001 | """REPL stage 2 (PRASH_V2.md §6b): free-text intent -> command resolution.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Stage 1 made the REPL a persistent session with context; stage 2 lets the
000004 | user type the way they'd talk to a person instead of the way they'd call a
000005 | CLI: "my api pod is sick, fix it" -> `fix prash-demo/api-...`. Deliberately
000006 | narrow and honest: if intent can't be resolved with real confidence, this
000007 | module says so and the caller asks a clarifying question rather than guessing
000008 | and running the wrong command against real infrastructure.
000009 | [blank]
000010 | Two-stage by design:
000011 |     resolve(text, session) -> Suggestion | Clarify | None
000012 |         Suggestion  -> argv to run (already context-resolved) + an explanation
000013 |         Clarify     -> a question to ask, with concrete known options
000014 |         None        -> genuinely couldn't resolve it, fast or otherwise
000015 | [blank]
000016 | The fast path (_verb_hit + the target regexes below) is pure and free --
000017 | zero latency, zero API cost, unit-testable headlessly. When it doesn't
000018 | recognize the text at all (Milestone 2, 2026-08-24), resolve() falls back
000019 | to routing it through the same tool-calling brain the diagnosis pipeline
000020 | uses (prash/brain/kimi_client.py's call_with_tool), built dynamically from
000021 | the real provider/action registries so a new connector never needs a
000022 | hand-added verb here. That fallback does real I/O and can fail (missing
000023 | credentials, model/network trouble) -- it degrades to None on any failure,
000024 | same contract as the fast path, never a crash.
000025 | """
000026 | [blank]
000027 | from __future__ import annotations
000028 | [blank]
000029 | import asyncio
000030 | import re
000031 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
000032 | [blank]
000033 | # A pod-ish token: lowercase start, dashes allowed, not too long. Anything
000034 | # containing "/" is treated as an already-qualified target (ns/pod or
000035 | # owner/repo) and never needs resolving.
000036 | _TARGETISH = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_.]{1,60}/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_.]{1,60}$")
000037 | [blank]
000038 | # A bare resource name must look like one -- k8s names are dash-y/nummer-y
000039 | # (api-7f9d, broken-app, web-3). Plain words like "api", "fix" or "pr" are
000040 | # talk, not targets; treating them as targets produces wrong guesses.
000041 | _BAREISH = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{2,40}$")
000042 | [blank]
000043 | [blank]
000044 | def _looks_like_bare_resource(w: str) -> bool:
000045 |     return bool(_BAREISH.fullmatch(w)) and ("-" in w or any(c.isdigit() for c in w))
000046 | [blank]
000047 | [blank]
000048 | # A bare resource name for a pod-needing verb (fix/restart/rollback/stats)
000049 | # is exactly as plausible as an AWS/GCP instance name as it is a k8s pod --
000050 | # "bithub-backend" and "broken-app" have the identical shape. Found live
000051 | # 2026-09-17: "bithub-backend seems down, nginx might not be running, can
000052 | # you check and fix it" matched the "fix" verb and got blindly qualified as
000053 | # a kubernetes pod, even though the sentence explicitly names an in-instance
000054 | # service (nginx), not a pod. The fast path has no provider-detection logic
000055 | # at all (only the LLM path does) -- these words are a cheap, deliberately
000056 | # imprecise signal to bail to the LLM rather than confidently guess wrong.
000057 | _NON_K8S_INSTANCE_HINTS = re.compile(
000058 |     r"\b(nginx|apache|ec2|instance|compute engine|droplet|vm|server|proxy|aws|gcp|azure)\b"
000059 | )
000060 | [blank]
000061 | # Words that are talk, not entity. Everything else that looks podish and
000062 | # isn't on this list is a candidate target.
000063 | _STOPWORDS = {
000064 |     "the", "a", "an", "my", "your", "is", "are", "was", "were", "be",
000065 |     "pod", "pods", "app", "application", "service", "deployment", "cluster",
000066 |     "broken", "sick", "down", "stuck", "crash", "crashing", "crashlooping",
000067 |     "failed", "failing", "and", "or", "but", "please", "can", "could", "you",
000068 |     "it", "that", "this", "with", "from", "for", "now", "quickly", "again",
000069 | }
000070 | [blank]
000071 | [blank]
000072 | @dataclass
000073 | class Clarify:
000074 |     """A question to ask the user, with concrete known options."""
000075 | [blank]
000076 |     question: str
000077 |     options: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
000078 | [blank]
000079 | [blank]
000080 | @dataclass
000081 | class Suggestion:
000082 |     """A resolved command line, ready to run."""
000083 | [blank]
000084 |     argv: list[str]
000085 |     explain: str
000086 | [blank]
000087 | [blank]
000088 | class _Context:
000089 |     """The slice of REPL session state intent parsing needs."""
000090 | [blank]
000091 |     def __init__(self, namespace: str | None = None, pod: str | None = None,
000092 |                  last_target: str | None = None) -> None:
000093 |         self.namespace = namespace
000094 |         self.pod = pod
000095 |         self.last_target = last_target
000096 | [blank]
000097 |     @classmethod
000098 |     def from_session(cls, session) -> _Context:
000099 |         return cls(session.namespace, session.pod, session.last_target)
000100 | [blank]
000101 | [blank]
000102 | def _words(text: str) -> list[str]:
000103 |     return [w.lower().strip(".,;:!?") for w in text.split()]
000104 | [blank]
000105 | [blank]
000106 | def _targets_in(text: str) -> list[str]:
000107 |     """Candidate target tokens, in the order they appeared. Qualified
000108 |     ns/pod and owner/repo targets win outright; bare podish words are the
000109 |     raw material for resolving against the session."""
000110 |     qualified, bare = [], []
000111 |     for w in _words(text):
000112 |         if _TARGETISH.fullmatch(w):
000113 |             qualified.append(w)
000114 |         elif _looks_like_bare_resource(w) and w not in _STOPWORDS:
000115 |             bare.append(w)
000116 |     return qualified + bare
000117 | [blank]
000118 | [blank]
000119 | # "what happened" style timeline questions -> get_stats (the `stats` verb).
000120 | # Kept separate from the word loop so they can be gated: a line that also
000121 | # carries an explicit action verb ("diagnose what happened") is a fix, not a
000122 | # read — stats must never hijack an execute intent.
000123 | _STATS_PHRASES = (
000124 |     "what's been happening", "whats been happening", "what has been happening",
000125 |     "what happened", "been happening", "recent events", "event history",
000126 |     "show me the events", "show me the history", "show me the timeline",
000127 | )
000128 | _ACTION_WORDS = ("fix", "diagnose", "restart", "reboot", "rollback", "revert")
000129 | [blank]
000130 | [blank]
000131 | def _verb_hit(text: str) -> str | None:
000132 |     """Return the intent verb, or None if the text doesn't read as intent."""
000133 |     low = text.lower()
000134 |     # Longer phrases first so "open a pr" wins over a bare "pr".
000135 |     if "open a pr" in low or "open pr" in low or "open a pull request" in low:
000136 |         return "open-pr"
000137 |     if "apply the ci fix" in low or "apply the fix" in low or "apply ci fix" in low:
000138 |         return "apply-ci-fix"
000139 |     if "what can you do" in low or "what do you do" in low or "list actions" in low:
000140 |         return "actions"
000141 |     # "keep an eye on X" is the canonical proactive-monitor phrasing (spec §4a)
000142 |     # and carries no verb keyword of its own -> map it to watch on the fast path.
000143 |     if "keep an eye on" in low or "keeping an eye on" in low or "eye on" in low:
000144 |         return "watch"
````

````text
000001 | """Team notification channels (Sprint 2 Tier 2, PRASH_V2.md §7b — Aryan).
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Closes the exact gap §7b's Team/notifications row flags: the watcher's plyer
000004 | ping reaches one laptop. Slack/Discord webhooks give the whole team the same

000007 | one, this just makes it real.
000008 | [blank]
000009 | Deliberately NOT a Connector. `base.Connector`'s shape (authenticate ->
000010 | locate -> fetch logs -> poll state) models *reading* infrastructure state; a
000011 | notification channel is a write-only sink, so forcing fetch_logs/poll_state
000012 | on it would be fake. Same spirit though: configured() -> send().
000013 | [blank]
000014 | Webhooks, deliberately: incoming-webhook URLs are the lowest-friction
000015 | mechanism both Slack and Discord expose for "POST a message to a channel" —
000016 | no OAuth app, no bot token, no permissions matrix, works from a plain CLI,
000017 | and matches the local-first posture (§4) exactly: the webhook URL lives in
000018 | the user's .env, is read locally, and is never sent to Drufiy. A richer
000019 | chat-bot API (threaded replies, slash commands) is real functionality nobody
000020 | has asked for yet — not built speculatively.
000021 | [blank]
000022 | Stdlib-only (urllib), matching github.py/gitlab.py's "zero network deps
000023 | beyond what ships with Python" convention.
000024 | [blank]
000025 | A failed webhook send never raises: it logs and returns False. The caller
000026 | (the watch loop in particular) must never die because a team channel is
````

### `prash/permissions.py`
````text
000001 | """Permission engine: the decision rule for whether an action may proceed.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Mirrors Claude Code's model:
000004 | [blank]
000005 |     read-only            -> investigate only; every write is refused
000006 |     ask                  -> prompt before every action (default)
000007 |     auto-safe            -> safe tier proceeds, approval tier prompts
000008 |     environment-scoped   -> safe tier auto on staging, always prompts on
000009 |                             production
000010 |     bypass               -> safe tier auto (CI/automation); approval tier
000011 |                             STILL prompts; never tier refused unconditionally
000012 | [blank]
000013 | Invariants enforced here:
000014 |     - NEVER tier is always REFUSE, regardless of mode or grant.
000015 |     - APPROVAL tier always requires an explicit per-action grant. In bypass
000016 |       mode it still prompts (never silently proceeds).
000017 | """
000018 | [blank]
000019 | from __future__ import annotations
000020 | [blank]
000021 | import enum
000022 | [blank]
000023 | from .actions.contract import Decision, RiskTier
000024 | [blank]
000025 | [blank]
000026 | class PermissionMode(enum.Enum):
000027 |     READ_ONLY = "read-only"
000028 |     ASK = "ask"
000029 |     AUTO_SAFE = "auto-safe"
000030 |     ENVIRONMENT_SCOPED = "environment-scoped"
000031 |     BYPASS = "bypass"
000032 | [blank]
000033 | [blank]
000034 | PRODUCTION = "production"
000035 | [blank]
000036 | [blank]
000037 | def decide(
000038 |     mode: PermissionMode,
000039 |     risk_tier: RiskTier,
000040 |     environment: str = "staging",
000041 |     grant: bool = False,
000042 | ) -> Decision:
000043 |     """Return ALLOW / PROMPT / REFUSE for a requested action.
000044 | [blank]
000045 |     ``grant`` is the explicit per-action grant. It is only meaningful for the
000046 |     APPROVAL tier (a user saying "yes, do this one thing"). It can never
000047 |     override the NEVER tier.
000048 |     """
000049 |     if risk_tier is RiskTier.NEVER:
000050 |         return Decision.REFUSE
000051 | [blank]
000052 |     if mode is PermissionMode.READ_ONLY:
000053 |         return Decision.REFUSE
000054 | [blank]
000055 |     if risk_tier is RiskTier.SAFE:
000056 |         if mode in (PermissionMode.AUTO_SAFE, PermissionMode.BYPASS):
000057 |             return Decision.ALLOW
000058 |         if mode is PermissionMode.ENVIRONMENT_SCOPED:
000059 |             return Decision.ALLOW if environment != PRODUCTION else Decision.PROMPT
000060 |         return Decision.PROMPT
000061 | [blank]
000062 |     # APPROVAL tier: always prompt unless an explicit per-action grant exists.
000063 |     # Mode can never auto-approve this tier.
000064 |     return Decision.ALLOW if grant else Decision.PROMPT
````

### `prash/repl.py`
````text
000001 | """Prash REPL (PRASH_V2.md §6b) — a persistent interactive session.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Not a new command set: the REPL re-invokes the existing argparse parser per
000004 | line, so every `cmd_*` entry point works exactly as in one-shot mode. What
000005 | makes it a session (and not just a prompt loop) is short-lived context that
000006 | is carried between lines:
000007 | [blank]
000008 |     prash repl
000009 |     prash> fix api-7f9d                 -> uses the remembered namespace
000010 |     prash> fix it                       -> stage 2: resolves to the remembered pod
000011 |     prash> restart the broken api pod   -> stage 2: free text -> run restart-pod
000012 |     prash> watch                        -> uses the remembered namespace
000013 |     prash> exit
000014 | [blank]
000015 | Stage 1 = the session + context. Stage 2 (`prash/intent.py`) = free-text
000016 | intent parsing with clarifying follow-ups when the target is ambiguous. A
000017 | line that parses as an exact command always wins; stage 2 only handles what
000018 | argparse can't. `q`/`exit`/`quit`/Ctrl+D end the session; `help` prints the
000019 | parser's usage.
000020 | """
000021 | [blank]
000022 | from __future__ import annotations
000023 | [blank]
000024 | import contextlib
000025 | import io
000026 | import shlex
000027 | from collections.abc import Iterable
000028 | [blank]
000029 | from . import ui
000030 | from .cli import build_parser
000031 | from .intent import (
000032 |     _STOPWORDS,
000033 |     Clarify,
000034 |     Suggestion,
000035 |     _Context,
000036 |     _verb_hit,
000037 |     complete,
000038 |     resolve,
000039 |     resolve_clarify_answer,
000040 | )
000041 | [blank]
000042 | # `run` only auto-fills the namespace for actions whose resource is a pod.
000043 | # open-pr/request-secret/apply-ci-fix take an owner/repo; rollback takes a
000044 | # deployment — guessing a namespace there would be wrong.
000045 | _POD_ACTIONS = {"restart-pod"}
000046 | [blank]
000047 | _PROMPT = "[bold yellow]prash>[/bold yellow] "
000048 | [blank]
000049 | [blank]
000050 | def _is_it_phrase(line: str) -> bool:
000051 |     """`fix it` / `restart that` — a known intent verb plus only a pronoun.
000052 |     These would parse as exact commands with garbage targets, so intercept
000053 |     them and let stage 2 resolve against the remembered context."""
000054 |     parts = line.strip().lower().split()
000055 |     return len(parts) == 2 and _verb_hit(parts[0]) is not None and parts[1] in ("it", "that")
000056 | [blank]
000057 | [blank]
000058 | def _looks_like_talk(line: str) -> bool:
000059 |     """A line that reads as natural language rather than an exact command:
000060 |     an intent verb plus conversational filler (stopwords) or pod/app talk.
000061 |     Routed to stage 2 before argparse so the parser's own "unrecognized
000062 |     arguments" noise never appears for obviously free-text input."""
000063 |     if _verb_hit(line) is None:
000064 |         return False
000065 |     return any(w in _STOPWORDS for w in line.strip().lower().split())
000066 | [blank]
000067 | [blank]
000068 | class ReplSession:
000069 |     """Carries the small amount of context that makes repeated commands
000070 |     bearable: the last namespace, the last pod, and the last full target."""
000071 | [blank]
000072 |     def __init__(self, console) -> None:
000073 |         self.console = console
000074 |         self.namespace: str | None = None
000075 |         self.pod: str | None = None
000076 |         self.last_target: str | None = None
000077 | [blank]
000078 |     def apply_context(self, args) -> None:
000079 |         """Fill in remembered context for a parsed command, in place, before
000080 |         its func runs. A bare pod name in `fix`/`run restart-pod` resolves
000081 |         against the remembered namespace; `watch` picks up the namespace too."""
000082 |         command = getattr(args, "command", None)
000083 |         if command == "fix" and not getattr(args, "ci", False):
000084 |             target = getattr(args, "target", "")
000085 |             if "/" not in target and self.namespace and target:
````

````text
000310 | def _verify_persisted_connector(connector_id: str, automatic: bool = False) -> Dict[str, Any]:

000314 |     credential already known to be bad on every tick is wasted work and,
000315 |     worse, extra failed-auth noise against the real provider."""

000317 |     if not is_connector_configured(connector_id, env_config):

000320 |     if automatic and current.get("status") in {"expired", "error"}:
000321 |         return dict(current)

000323 |     try:

000325 |             clear_connector_cache(connector_id)

000335 |         return _set_connection_state(connector_id, "expired", error=error, identity="")

001599 |                         "type": "pong",
001600 |                         "timestamp": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
001601 |                     }))
001602 |                 elif action == "pause":

001605 |                         _paused_watches.add(wid)

001609 |                             "type": "control_ack",
001610 |                             "action": "pause",
001611 |                             "watch_id": wid,
001612 |                             "success": True,
001613 |                         }))
001614 |                 elif action == "resume":
001615 |                     wid = msg.get("watch_id")
001616 |                     if wid and wid in _active_watches:
001617 |                         _paused_watches.discard(wid)
001618 |                         if wid in _watch_metadata:

001620 |                         await websocket.send_text(json.dumps({

001623 |                             "watch_id": wid,
001624 |                             "success": True,
001625 |                         }))
001626 |                 elif action == "stop":
001627 |                     wid = msg.get("watch_id")
001628 |                     cid = msg.get("connector_id") or (wid.split(":", 1)[0] if wid and ":" in wid else "")
001629 |                     target = msg.get("target") or (wid.split(":", 1)[1] if wid and ":" in wid else "")
001630 |                     if wid and wid in _active_watches:

001634 |                             "action": "stop",
001635 |                             "watch_id": wid,
001636 |                             "success": True,
001637 |                         }))
001638 |             except Exception as e:

002277 | def _gather_live_sre_telemetry(cid: Optional[str] = None, rid: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
002278 |     """Gathers real-time telemetry from live AWS EC2, CloudWatch, and Kubernetes."""
002279 |     sections = []
002280 |     
002281 |     # 1. AWS Telemetry
002282 |     try:
002283 |         import boto3
002284 |         session = boto3.Session(region_name="ap-south-1")
002285 |         ec2 = session.client("ec2")
002286 |         res = ec2.describe_instances(Filters=[{"Name": "instance-state-name", "Values": ["running"]}])
002287 |         insts = []
002288 |         inst_ids = []
002289 |         for r in res.get("Reservations", []):
002290 |             for i in r.get("Instances", []):
002291 |                 iid = i["InstanceId"]
002292 |                 itype = i.get("InstanceType", "t3.medium")
002293 |                 tags = {t["Key"]: t["Value"] for t in i.get("Tags", [])}
002294 |                 name = tags.get("Name", "lear-demo-node")
002295 |                 inst_ids.append(iid)
002296 |                 insts.append(f"Node `{iid}` (Name: {name}, Type: {itype}, State: Running)")
002297 |         if insts:
002298 |             sections.append("### Live AWS EC2 Nodes (ap-south-1 Mumbai):\n" + "\n".join(insts))
002299 |             
002300 |             # CloudWatch CPU
002301 |             cw = session.client("cloudwatch")
002302 |             end_t = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
002303 |             start_t = end_t - datetime.timedelta(hours=1)
002304 |             cpu_data = []
002305 |             for iid in inst_ids[:3]:
002306 |                 m = cw.get_metric_statistics(
002307 |                     Namespace="AWS/EC2", MetricName="CPUUtilization",
002308 |                     Dimensions=[{"Name": "InstanceId", "Value": iid}],
002309 |                     StartTime=start_t, EndTime=end_t, Period=300, Statistics=["Average", "Maximum"]
002310 |                 )
002311 |                 pts = m.get("Datapoints", [])
002312 |                 if pts:
002313 |                     avg_c = round(pts[-1]["Average"], 2)
002314 |                     max_c = round(pts[-1]["Maximum"], 2)
002315 |                     cpu_data.append(f"- Instance `{iid}`: Average CPU {avg_c}%, Max Peak {max_c}% (Sample window: last 60m)")
002316 |             if cpu_data:
002317 |                 sections.append("### Live CloudWatch CPU Telemetry:\n" + "\n".join(cpu_data))
002318 |     except Exception as e:
002319 |         logger.debug(f"AWS telemetry fetch skipped: {e}")
002320 | [blank]
002321 |     # 2. Kubernetes Pods
002322 |     try:
````

### `prash/tui.py`
````text
000001 | """Lear terminal app — one merged surface (2026-08-24), replacing the
000002 | repl/tui split.
000003 | [blank]
000004 | Until now `prash repl` (plain-text, conversational, but only understood ~12
000005 | hardcoded verbs and 2 of 10 connectors via prash/intent.py) and `prash tui`
000006 | (a real dashboard, but read-only -- no input widget existed anywhere in it)
000007 | were two disconnected binaries. Found live testing the REPL against a real
000008 | Grafana alert: a completely reasonable sentence failed because it wasn't in
000009 | the keyword table, and the good-looking surface couldn't have taken that
000010 | input at all. This is the fix: one app, chat as the primary view, the
000011 | existing dashboard panes reachable from inside it instead of a separate
000012 | process.
000013 | [blank]
000014 | The Chat pane does NOT reimplement REPL logic -- it drives repl.py's
000015 | `process_line()` (the exact function the plain-text `prash repl` loop now
000016 | also calls), in a worker thread so a real connector call never freezes the
000017 | UI. Two surfaces sharing one interaction engine is the whole point; forking
000018 | a second implementation here would repeat the mistake that split them in
000019 | the first place.
000020 | [blank]
000021 | Built on `textual` (same team as `rich`). Non-TTY and headless-safe: every
000022 | data read is the same `AuditLog` / `CircuitBreaker` / `CredentialStore` /
000023 | connector call the CLI already uses, so nothing here is a fake dashboard.
000024 | [blank]
000025 | Keys:
000026 |     q / ctrl+c   quit
000027 |     r            refresh all panes now
000028 |     c            switch to Chat
000029 |     t            switch to Overview
000030 |     a            switch to Actions
000031 |     d            switch to Audit
000032 |     k            switch to Kubernetes

000035 |                  config/circuit shortcuts; not model/mode, no runtime
000036 |                  switch for either exists yet)

000244 | class PrashCommandProvider(Provider):
000245 |     """ctrl+p command palette (Textual's own -- not a custom overlay).
000246 |     Scoped to things Prash actually does today: jump to a tab, or run a
000247 |     utility command already handled by process_line(). Deliberately does
000248 |     NOT list /model or /mode -- there is no runtime model/permission-mode
000249 |     switch implemented anywhere in this codebase yet; putting them in the
000250 |     palette would advertise a feature that doesn't exist."""
000251 | [blank]
000252 |     def _commands(self):
000253 |         app: PrashApp = self.app  # type: ignore[assignment]
000254 |         return [
000255 |             ("chat", "Switch to Chat", app.action_tab_chat),
000256 |             ("overview", "Switch to Overview", app.action_tab_overview),
000257 |             ("actions", "Switch to Actions — registered write actions", app.action_tab_actions),
000258 |             ("audit", "Switch to Audit — recent action history", app.action_tab_audit),
000259 |             ("kubernetes", "Switch to Kubernetes — live pod status", app.action_tab_k8s),
000260 |             ("connectors", "Check every configured connector's auth, right now", app.action_check_connectors),
000261 |             ("circuit status", "Run `circuit status` in Chat", lambda: app.run_chat_command("circuit status")),
000262 |             ("config", "Run `config` in Chat — show local settings", lambda: app.run_chat_command("config")),
000263 |             ("refresh", "Refresh dashboard data now", app.action_refresh),
000264 |         ]
000265 | [blank]
000266 |     async def search(self, query: str) -> Hits:
000267 |         matcher = self.matcher(query)
000268 |         for name, help_text, callback in self._commands():
000269 |             score = matcher.match(name)
000270 |             if score > 0:
000271 |                 yield Hit(score, matcher.highlight(name), callback, help=help_text)
000272 | [blank]
000273 | [blank]
000274 | class ChatInteraction:
000275 |     """Answers confirm/secret/choice prompts through the chat surface
000276 |     instead of blocking on real stdin (see the long comment above
000277 |     cli.py's `_confirm_action` for why a plain Prompt.ask() call hangs
000278 |     forever from a Textual worker thread -- found live 2026-08-26,
000279 |     `mute <monitor> for 30 minutes` never returned because
000280 |     datadog-mute-monitor needs approval).
000281 | [blank]
000282 |     Renders the question into the chat log from the worker thread via
000283 |     `call_from_thread`, then blocks *this worker thread only* (never the
000284 |     UI -- the app stays fully responsive) on a `threading.Event` that the
000285 |     main thread sets from `on_input_submitted` once the user's next typed
000286 |     line arrives. A generous timeout auto-declines rather than leaking a
000287 |     thread forever if the app is abandoned mid-question."""
000288 | [blank]
000289 |     _TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300
000290 | [blank]
000291 |     def __init__(self, app: "PrashApp") -> None:
000292 |         self.app = app
000293 | [blank]
000294 |     def _wait_for_answer(self, kind: str, lines: list[str]) -> str | None:
000295 |         log = self.app.query_one("#chat-log", RichLog)
000296 |         chat_input = self.app.query_one("#chat-input", Input)
000297 |         event = threading.Event()
000298 |         box: dict[str, str] = {}
000299 | [blank]
000300 |         def announce() -> None:
000301 |             for line in lines:
000302 |                 log.write(line)
000303 |             chat_input.placeholder = "y/n?" if kind == "confirm" else "type your answer"
000304 |             self.app._chat_awaiting = (kind, event, box)
000305 | [blank]
000306 |         self.app.call_from_thread(announce)
000307 |         answered = event.wait(self._TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
000308 | [blank]
000309 |         def restore() -> None:
000310 |             self.app._chat_awaiting = None
000311 |             chat_input.placeholder = "what's broken?"
000312 | [blank]
000313 |         if not answered:
000314 |             self.app.call_from_thread(restore)
000315 |             self.app.call_from_thread(log.write, "[no answer within 5 minutes -- treating as decline]")
000316 |             return None
000317 |         return box.get("value")
000318 | [blank]
000319 |     def confirm(self, action: Any, plan: Any, ctx: Any) -> bool:
000320 |         hint = f" ({action.spec.approval_hint})" if action.spec.approval_hint else ""
000321 |         lines = [
000322 |             f"? Target {ctx.target.resource} ({ctx.target.environment})",
000323 |             f"  {plan.describe()}",
000324 |             f"  Proceed with '{action.spec.id}'{hint}? [y/N]",
000325 |         ]
000326 |         value = self._wait_for_answer("confirm", lines)
000327 |         return value is not None and value.lower().startswith("y")
000328 | [blank]
000329 |     def secret(self, name: str, hint: str) -> str:
000330 |         prompt = f"? Value for secret '{name}'" + (f" ({hint})" if hint else "")
000331 |         value = self._wait_for_answer("secret", [prompt])
000332 |         return value or ""
000333 | [blank]
000334 |     def choose(self, question: str, choices: list[str], default: str) -> str | None:
000335 |         lines = [f"? {question} [{'/'.join(choices)}] (default {default})"]
000336 |         value = self._wait_for_answer("choice", lines)
000337 |         if value is None:
000338 |             return None
000339 |         return value if value in choices else default

000477 |     def on_input_submitted(self, event: Input.Submitted) -> None:
000478 |         if event.input.id != "chat-input":
000479 |             return
000480 |         line = event.value.strip()
000481 |         event.input.value = ""
000482 |         if not line:
000483 |             return
000484 |         log = self.query_one("#chat-log", RichLog)
000485 |         log.write(f"> {line}")
000486 |         if self._chat_awaiting is not None:
000487 |             # A confirm/secret/choice question is outstanding (see
000488 |             # ChatInteraction) -- this line answers it, not a new command.
000489 |             # Must be checked before _chat_busy: the worker that asked the
000490 |             # question is still running (blocked on the answer), so
000491 |             # _chat_busy is still True at this point.
000492 |             _kind, answer_event, box = self._chat_awaiting
000493 |             box["value"] = line
000494 |             self._chat_awaiting = None
000495 |             event.input.placeholder = "what's broken?"
000496 |             answer_event.set()
000497 |             return
000498 |         if self._chat_busy:
000499 |             log.write("(still working on the last one — hang on)")
000500 |             return
000501 |         self._chat_busy = True
000502 |         self._run_chat_line(line)
000503 | [blank]
000504 |     @work(thread=True)
000505 |     def _run_chat_line(self, line: str) -> None:
000506 |         # Redirect the one global console (prash/ui.py's `console` -- every
000507 |         # cmd_* function in cli.py prints through this same object) so real
000508 |         # command output lands in the chat log instead of the raw stdout
000509 |         # Textual has already taken over the screen buffer for. Runs off
000510 |         # the main thread so a real connector call never freezes the UI.
000511 |         buf = io.StringIO()
000512 |         old_file = ui_mod.console.file
000513 |         ui_mod.console.file = buf
000514 |         # Any approval/secret/choice prompt hit while running this line goes
000515 |         # through ChatInteraction instead of blocking on real stdin, which
000516 |         # this worker thread can never receive (see ChatInteraction's
000517 |         # docstring). Thread-local, so the plain CLI/REPL path is untouched.
000518 |         cli_mod.set_interaction(ChatInteraction(self))
000519 |         try:
000520 |             # Both streams: argparse's own usage/error output on a bad line
000521 |             # goes to stderr, not through ui_mod.console at all -- stdout
000522 |             # alone left it invisible (found live, 2026-08-25).
000523 |             with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf), contextlib.redirect_stderr(buf):
000524 |                 new_pending = repl_mod.process_line(
000525 |                     line, self._chat_session, self._chat_parser, ui_mod.console, self._chat_pending
000526 |                 )
000527 |         finally:
000528 |             ui_mod.console.file = old_file
000529 |             cli_mod.clear_interaction()
000530 |         self.call_from_thread(self._on_chat_result, new_pending, buf.getvalue())
000531 | [blank]
000532 |     def _on_chat_result(self, new_pending, output: str) -> None:
000533 |         self._chat_busy = False
000534 |         log = self.query_one("#chat-log", RichLog)
000535 |         text = output.rstrip("\n")
000536 |         if text:
000537 |             # cmd_* output carries real ANSI (the CLI's Rich-rendered tables/
000538 |             # panels, plus argparse's own help text via a Rich formatter) --
000539 |             # decode it into styled Text instead of writing the raw escape
000540 |             # sequences as literal characters.
000541 |             log.write(Text.from_ansi(text))
000542 |         if new_pending is repl_mod._EXIT:
000543 |             self.exit()
000544 |             return
000545 |         self._chat_pending = new_pending
````

### `prash/watcher.py`
````text
000001 | """Track E — the watcher. Owner: Aradhya. See PRASH_V2.md §6, days 9-11.
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Poll loop over Track B's Kubernetes connector, watching for the four states
000004 | Track D's brain is taught to diagnose (§8): CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled,
000005 | ImagePullBackOff, and stuck-pending — the connector's own _classify() already
000006 | does the hard detection work, so this module's job is narrower: poll on an
000007 | interval, remember what's already been reported so it doesn't re-notify every
000008 | cycle for an ongoing problem, and fire a desktop notification on the moment a
000009 | NEW problem appears. One source done properly, not many done shallowly (§6).
000010 | [blank]
000011 | Not a background daemon (§2's "always-on" framing is a later-sprint question,
000012 | explicitly out of scope this sprint per §7 — no hosted layer). This is a
000013 | foreground `prash watch` process the user runs and leaves open, matching the
000014 | CLI-only scope this sprint committed to.
000015 | """
000016 | from __future__ import annotations
000017 | [blank]
000018 | import logging
000019 | import os
000020 | import subprocess
000021 | import sys
000022 | import time
000023 | from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
000024 | [blank]
000025 | from prash.connectors.kubernetes import PodStatus, get_pod_status
000026 | from prash.connectors.terraform import TerraformConnector
000027 | from prash.connectors.aws import AWSConnector
000028 | from prash.connectors.datadog import DatadogConnector, DatadogError
000029 | from prash.connectors.pagerduty import PagerDutyConnector, PagerDutyError
000030 | from prash.connectors.grafana import GrafanaConnector, GrafanaError
000031 | from prash.connectors.github import GitHubConnector, GitHubError
000032 | from prash.connectors.gitlab import GitLabConnector, GitLabError
000033 | from prash.connectors.base import ConnectorEvent, ConnectorState
000034 | from prash.notifications import send_team_notifications
000035 | [blank]
000036 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
000037 | [blank]
000038 | DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30
000039 | [blank]
000040 | [blank]
000041 | def _interval_from_env() -> int:
000042 |     raw = os.environ.get("PRASH_WATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS")
000043 |     if raw:
000044 |         try:
000045 |             return int(raw)
000046 |         except ValueError:
000047 |             logger.warning(f"PRASH_WATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS={raw!r} is not an integer — using default")
000048 |     return DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS
000049 | [blank]
000050 | [blank]
000051 | def _pod_key(pod: PodStatus) -> str:
000052 |     return f"{pod.namespace}/{pod.name}"
000053 | [blank]
000054 | [blank]
000055 | def detect_changes(
000056 |     pods: list[PodStatus], previous_state: dict[str, str | None]
000057 | ) -> tuple[list[PodStatus], dict[str, str | None]]:
000058 |     """Compare this poll's pod statuses against the last known state.
000059 | [blank]
000060 |     Returns (pods with a newly-appeared or newly-changed problem, updated
000061 |     state). A pod stays silent across repeated polls once its problem has
000062 |     already been reported once -- only a transition (healthy -> problem, or
000063 |     problem A -> problem B) triggers a notification. A pod resolving
000064 |     (problem -> None) is recorded but never notified about -- there's
000065 |     nothing to alert on. A pod that disappears (deleted/recreated, e.g. by
000066 |     restart_pod) simply drops out of the state; its replacement starts fresh,
000067 |     which is correct -- a fresh notification if the new pod also breaks is
000068 |     exactly what should happen, not something to suppress.
000069 |     """
000070 |     new_state: dict[str, str | None] = {}
000071 |     changed: list[PodStatus] = []
000072 |     for pod in pods:
000073 |         key = _pod_key(pod)
000074 |         new_state[key] = pod.problem
000075 |         if pod.problem is not None and pod.problem != previous_state.get(key):
000076 |             changed.append(pod)
000077 |     return changed, new_state
000078 | [blank]
000079 | [blank]
000080 | def _notify(pod: PodStatus, console=None, creds: dict | None = None) -> None:
000081 |     title = f"Prash: {pod.problem} — {pod.name}"
000082 |     message = (
000083 |         f"{pod.namespace}/{pod.name} (restart_count={pod.restart_count}). "
000084 |         f"Run `prash fix {pod.namespace}/{pod.name}` to diagnose."
000085 |     )
000086 |     if not _send_desktop_notification(title, message):
000087 |         logger.warning("Desktop notification failed on every available path — console only")
000088 |     if creds:
000089 |         # Sprint 2 Tier 2: push the same ping to every configured team channel
000090 |         # (Slack/Discord webhooks). Never raises; a dead channel is logged by
000091 |         # send_team_notifications and reported here, it doesn't kill the loop.
000092 |         results = send_team_notifications(creds, title, message)
000093 |         failed = [channel for channel, ok in results.items() if not ok]
000094 |         if failed:
000095 |             logger.warning(f"team notification failed: {', '.join(failed)}")
000096 |         elif results:
000097 |             logger.info(f"team notification sent: {', '.join(results)}")
000098 |     if console is not None:
000099 |         console.print(f"[bold red]⚠ {title}[/bold red]\n  {message}")
000100 | [blank]
000101 | [blank]
000102 | def _send_desktop_notification(title: str, message: str) -> bool:
000103 |     """True if a real OS notification was sent. Tries plyer first (works on
000104 |     Windows/Linux); on macOS specifically it falls back to `osascript`.
000105 | [blank]
000106 |     Found live, verifying the watcher against the actual cluster (2026-08-09):
000107 |     plyer's macOS backend uses NSUserNotificationCenter, which returns None
000108 |     (AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'setDelegate_') for
000109 |     processes without a proper app-bundle identifier -- true of any plain CLI
000110 |     script, not fixable by installing more packages. `osascript -e 'display
000111 |     notification'` is the standard, dependency-free mechanism CLI tools use
000112 |     on macOS instead; it doesn't need a bundle identity.
000113 | [blank]
000114 |     Found live, verifying the Datadog loop on Windows (2026-09-07): plyer's
000115 |     win32 balloon backend packs the toast title/message into NOTIFYICONDATAW's
000116 |     fixed-size struct fields (packed at 64 chars in this build). Longer text
000117 |     raises "ValueError: string too long" inside plyer's own balloon_tip worker
000118 |     thread -- AFTER notify() has returned True -- so the caller can neither
000119 |     catch it nor know the toast never displayed. The only correct handling at
000120 |     this layer is to keep the strings within the packed limit: _toast_clamp
000121 |     below. The full text is unaffected everywhere else (console, team
000122 |     channels); the OS toast is the only surface with the hard cap.
000123 |     """
000124 |     try:
000125 |         from plyer import notification
000126 | [blank]
000127 |         notification.notify(
000128 |             title=_toast_clamp(title), message=_toast_clamp(message), timeout=10
000129 |         )
000130 |         return True
000131 |     except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — a failed OS notification must never kill the watch loop
000132 |         logger.info(f"plyer notification failed ({e}), trying platform fallback")
000133 | [blank]
000134 |     if sys.platform == "darwin":
000135 |         try:
000136 |             script = (
000137 |                 f'display notification "{_applescript_escape(message)}" '
000138 |                 f'with title "{_applescript_escape(title)}"'
000139 |             )
000140 |             subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script], check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=5)
000141 |             return True
000142 |         except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — same reasoning, never kill the loop
000143 |             logger.warning(f"osascript notification fallback also failed: {e}")
000144 | [blank]
000145 |     return False
000146 | [blank]
000147 | [blank]
000148 | def _toast_clamp(text: str, limit: int = 64) -> str:
000149 |     """Fit text into plyer's win32 balloon struct limit (see
000150 |     _send_desktop_notification's 2026-09-07 note). The trailing ellipsis
000151 |     marks truncation; the full text still reaches the console and every
000152 |     team channel -- only the OS toast is capped."""
000153 |     return text if len(text) <= limit else text[: limit - 1] + "…"
000154 | [blank]
000155 | [blank]
000156 | def _applescript_escape(s: str) -> str:
000157 |     return s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
000158 | [blank]
000159 | [blank]
000160 | def run_watch_loop(
000161 |     namespace: str,
000162 |     interval: int | None = None,
000163 |     console=None,
000164 |     max_iterations: int | None = None,
000165 |     creds: dict | None = None,
000166 | ) -> dict[str, str | None]:
000167 |     """The actual loop. `max_iterations` is None for the real `prash watch`
000168 |     command (runs until Ctrl+C, caught by cli.py's main()) -- set to a small
000169 |     int in tests so a single call can't hang forever. `creds` is the local
000170 |     .env dict; when present, each new-problem ping is also pushed to any
000171 |     configured Slack/Discord team channels."""
000172 |     interval = interval or _interval_from_env()
000173 |     state: dict[str, str | None] = {}
000174 |     iterations = 0
000175 | [blank]
000176 |     while max_iterations is None or iterations < max_iterations:
000177 |         pods = get_pod_status(namespace)
000178 |         changed, state = detect_changes(pods, state)
000179 |         for pod in changed:
000180 |             _notify(pod, console, creds)
000181 |         if console is not None and not changed:
000182 |             console.print(f"[dim]{namespace}: {len(pods)} pod(s), no new problems[/dim]")
000183 | [blank]
000184 |         iterations += 1

000191 | def _console_notify(console, text: str) -> None:
000192 |     """Render a console line without dying on consoles whose codepage can't
000193 |     encode it. Found live 2026-09-09: on a cp1252 legacy Windows console rich
000194 |     buffers the text and raises UnicodeEncodeError only at flush time -- the
000195 |     bad segment stays in the Console's buffer and kills the NEXT print too
000196 |     (even a plain-ASCII one), which is how the whole watch loop died on its
000197 |     first alert. So sanitize up front for the console's own encoding (the ⚠
000198 |     marker degrades to '?') and never hand rich an unencodable character."""
000199 |     if console is None:
000200 |         return
000201 |     try:
000202 |         text.encode(getattr(console, "encoding", None) or "ascii")
000203 |     except (UnicodeEncodeError, LookupError):
000204 |         text = text.encode("ascii", "replace").decode("ascii")
000205 |     console.print(text)
````
