000250 | # ── Shared loop for the WatchHandle.poll() model (Datadog, PagerDuty) ──
000251 | # Distinct from run_connector_watch_loop below: here dedup lives INSIDE the
000252 | # connector's WatchHandle (poll() returns only new events since last call --
000253 | # e.g. PagerDuty's "same incident, same state -> silence" contract), not in
000254 | # the loop. Datadog's and PagerDuty's watch loops were two ~90-line, ~90%
000255 | # identical copies of the same build-handles/poll/notify/sleep shape; this is
000256 | # that pattern's one home, same principle as run_connector_watch_loop unifying
000257 | # the poll_state()+get_stats() family. Each connector keeps its own handle-
000258 | # building (target resolution needs provider-specific errors) and its own
000259 | # notify_fn (each renders a different message) -- only the loop body is shared.
000260 | [blank]
000261 | def run_watchhandle_loop(
000262 |     handles: list,
000263 |     notify_fn,
000264 |     interval: int | None = None,
000265 |     console=None,
000266 |     max_iterations: int | None = None,
000267 |     creds: dict | None = None,
000268 | ) -> None:
000269 |     """Poll a list of WatchHandles each cycle; `notify_fn(event, console, creds)`
000270 |     is the provider-specific notification path. A poll error (rate limit
000271 |     exhausted, network down) warns and skips that handle for the cycle -- the
000272 |     loop never dies on a bad API day. A notification error (dead toast path, a
000273 |     console whose codepage can't render the alert) warns and moves on for the
000274 |     same reason. max_iterations is None for the real `prash watch` command
000275 |     (runs until Ctrl+C); set to a small int in tests."""
000276 |     interval = _interval_from_env() if interval is None else interval
000277 |     iterations = 0
000278 |     while max_iterations is None or iterations < max_iterations:
000279 |         for handle in handles:
000280 |             try:
000281 |                 events = handle.poll()
000282 |             except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — a bad API day can't kill the loop
000283 |                 logger.warning(f"poll failed for {handle.target!r}: {exc}")
000284 |                 continue
000285 |             for event in events:
000286 |                 try:
000287 |                     notify_fn(event, console, creds)
000288 |                 except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — nor can a bad notification day
000289 |                     logger.warning(f"notify failed for {handle.target!r}: {exc}")
000290 |             if console is not None and not events:
000291 |                 _console_notify(console, f"[dim]{handle.target}: poll OK, no state changes[/dim]")
000292 | [blank]
000293 |         iterations += 1
000294 |         if max_iterations is None or iterations < max_iterations:
000295 |             time.sleep(interval)

000675 | # ── M5 (spec §4d): one multi-connector watch loop over the Connector interface ──

000682 | # and terraform's drift model stay specialized — they aren't get_stats time

000704 | def _read_watch(connector, target: str, since):
000705 |     """Read one connector's poll_state + get_stats for `target`. Never raises —
000706 |     a single flaky connector must not take down a multi-connector cycle; it

000714 |         err = exc
000715 |     try:
000716 |         events = connector.get_stats(target, since=since)
000717 |     except NotImplementedError:

000719 |     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001

### `pyproject.toml`
````text
000001 | [build-system]
000002 | requires = ["setuptools>=68"]
000003 | build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
000004 | [blank]
000005 | [project]
000006 | name = "prash-v2"
000007 | version = "0.2.0"
000008 | description = "Lear - local-first AI DevOps agent"
000009 | requires-python = ">=3.10"
000010 | dependencies = [
000011 |     "rich>=13.0",
000012 |     "kubernetes>=29.0",
000013 |     "pydantic>=2.0",
000014 |     "httpx>=0.27",
000015 |     "openai>=1.0",
000016 |     "plyer>=2.1",
000017 |     "textual>=8.0",
000018 |     # plyer's macOS notification backend needs pyobjus (a PyObjC-style bridge)
000019 |     # that isn't pulled in automatically -- without it, notify() raises and
000020 |     # _notify() falls back to console-only, which is silent-but-safe, not a
000021 |     # crash, but it means real desktop notifications never actually fire on
000022 |     # macOS. Found live, verifying the watcher against the actual cluster.
000023 |     "pyobjus>=1.2.3; sys_platform == 'darwin'",
000024 |     "boto3>=1.34",
000025 |     # GCP connector (prash/connectors/gcp.py) imports these at module level
000026 |     # inside a try/except -- never declared anywhere, so authenticate() always
000027 |     # failed with "GCP SDK is required" on a clean install. Found live testing
000028 |     # real GCP credentials, 2026-09-16.
000029 |     "google-auth>=2.0",
000030 |     "google-api-python-client>=2.0",
000031 |     "fastapi>=0.100.0",
000032 |     "uvicorn>=0.20.0",
000033 |     "python-dotenv>=1.0.0",
000034 |     "pyyaml>=6.0",
000035 | ]
000036 | [blank]
000037 | # The desktop app's local backend (prash/server.py + prash/connector_registry.py)
000038 | # is the only code that needs these -- the core `prash` CLI never imports either
000039 | # module, so they stay an opt-in extra rather than weight every CLI install.
000040 | # uvicorn[standard] pulls the websockets stack that /ws/events needs at runtime.
000041 | [project.optional-dependencies]
000042 | desktop = [
000043 |     "fastapi>=0.110",
000044 |     "python-dotenv>=1.0",
000045 |     "uvicorn[standard]>=0.27",
000046 | ]
000047 | # dev pulls desktop because the test suite imports the desktop-server modules at
000048 | # collection time (tests/test_desktop_api.py, test_connector_registry.py,
000049 | # test_widget_generation.py) -- so `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, which CI already
000050 | # runs, is enough to collect and run them with no extra CI step.
000051 | dev = [
000052 |     "pytest>=7.0",
000053 |     "prash-v2[desktop]",
000054 | ]
000055 | [blank]
000056 | [project.scripts]
000057 | prash = "prash.cli:main"
000058 | [blank]
000059 | [tool.setuptools.packages.find]
000060 | include = ["prash*"]
000061 | [blank]
000062 | [tool.pytest.ini_options]
000063 | testpaths = ["tests"]
000064 | # Without this, CI (which invokes the bare `pytest` binary, not `python -m
000065 | # pytest`) never puts the repo root on sys.path, so tests/test_eval_env_loading.py
000066 | # importing the sibling `evals` package fails with ModuleNotFoundError even
000067 | # though it works locally (python -m pytest adds the cwd automatically).
000068 | pythonpath = ["."]
````

000016 |     import json

000024 |     CONCURRENCY = int(os.environ.get("CONCURRENCY", "10"))

000026 | [blank]
000027 |     SUCCESS_COUNT = 0
000028 |     FAILURE_COUNT = 0
000029 |     START_TIME = time.time()
000030 | [blank]
000031 |     def send_order():
000032 |         global SUCCESS_COUNT, FAILURE_COUNT
000033 |         url = f"{TARGET_URL}/api/checkout"
000034 |         payload = json.dumps({
000035 |             "item": random.choice(["Cloud Tier 1", "Enterprise Suite", "Agent License", "Pro Monitoring"]),
000036 |             "price": round(random.uniform(29.99, 199.99), 2),
000037 |             "user_id": f"usr_{random.randint(1000, 9999)}"
000038 |         }).encode("utf-8")
000039 |         req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=payload, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
000040 | [blank]
000041 |         try:
000042 |             with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=4) as resp:
000043 |                 if resp.status == 200:
000044 |                     SUCCESS_COUNT += 1
000045 |                 else:
000046 |                     FAILURE_COUNT += 1
000047 |         except Exception:
000048 |             FAILURE_COUNT += 1
000049 | [blank]
000050 |     def print_stats():
000051 |         last_success = 0
000052 |         last_failure = 0
000053 |         last_time = time.time()
000054 |         while True:
000055 |             time.sleep(3)
000056 |             now = time.time()
000057 |             dt = now - last_time
000058 |             succ_diff = SUCCESS_COUNT - last_success
000059 |             fail_diff = FAILURE_COUNT - last_failure
000060 |             rate = succ_diff / dt if dt > 0 else 0
000061 |             fail_rate = fail_diff / dt if dt > 0 else 0
000062 | [blank]
000063 |             print(
000064 |                 f"[loadgen] Traffic: {rate:.1f} req/s | "
000065 |                 f"Total Orders: {SUCCESS_COUNT} | "
000066 |                 f"Errors: {FAILURE_COUNT} (Rate: {fail_rate:.1f} err/s)",
000067 |                 flush=True
000068 |             )
000069 |             last_success = SUCCESS_COUNT
000070 |             last_failure = FAILURE_COUNT
000071 |             last_time = now
000072 | [blank]
000073 |     def worker_loop():
000074 |         while True:
000075 |             send_order()
000076 |             if REQUEST_DELAY > 0:
000077 |                 time.sleep(REQUEST_DELAY)
000078 | [blank]
000079 |     def main():
000080 |         print(f"[loadgen] Starting load generator against {TARGET_URL}", flush=True)
000081 |         print(f"[loadgen] Concurrency: {CONCURRENCY} workers | Base Delay: {REQUEST_DELAY}s", flush=True)
000082 | [blank]
000083 |         executor = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=CONCURRENCY + 1)
000084 |         # Background stats reporter
000085 |         executor.submit(print_stats)
000086 | [blank]
000087 |         # Worker threads

### `scripts/demo/scripts/inject-failure.sh`

000001 | #!/usr/bin/env bash

000003 | [blank]
000004 | NS="lear-demo"

000006 | [blank]

000009 |   kubectl -n "$NS" patch configmap checkout-api-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"DATABASE_HOST":"postgres-wrong"}}'
000010 |   kubectl -n "$NS" rollout restart deployment/checkout-api
000011 |   echo "checkout-api restarted, entering CrashLoopBackOff"
000012 | elif [ "$TYPE" = "oom" ]; then

000014 |   kubectl -n "$NS" patch deployment checkout-api --type merge -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"checkout-api","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"8Mi"}}}]}}}}'
000015 |   echo "checkout-api restarted, will trigger OOMKilled"
000016 | else
000017 |   echo "Unknown failure type: $TYPE. Supported: config, oom"
000018 | fi
````

### `scripts/testing/break_aws.py`

000001 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
000002 | """Reusable AWS EC2 failure fixture (TESTING_SETUP.md).
000003 | [blank]
000004 | Owns one EC2 instance end to end (tagged Name=prash-test-fixture, or the
000005 | instance id given via EC2_INSTANCE_ID / --instance-id). Force a REAL
000006 | failure state on demand -- an unhealthy systemd-ish unit simulated by a
000007 | marker file plus a runaway background process -- then heal it back.
000008 | [blank]
000009 | The failure is deliberately service-level, not instance-level: the box
000010 | stays reachable so the diagnose path has real logs to read, while
000011 | poll_state() can report degraded/failed. No mock -- this is a genuine
000012 | broken service on a real instance.
000013 | [blank]
000014 |     python3 scripts/testing/break_aws.py [--instance-id i-xxxx]          # force failure
000015 |     python3 scripts/testing/break_aws.py [--instance-id i-xxxx] --heal   # restore
000016 | [blank]
000017 | Resource name to investigate with: the instance Name tag, "prash-test-fixture"
000018 | (or its instance id -- poll_state() resolves by either, same as every other
000019 | connector's resource shape here).
000020 | """
000021 | from __future__ import annotations
000022 | [blank]
000023 | import argparse
000024 | import os
000025 | import subprocess
000026 | import sys
000027 | import time
000028 | [blank]
000029 | sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", ".."))
000030 | [blank]
000031 | import boto3  # noqa: E402  # import after sys.path manipulation
000032 | [blank]
000033 | INSTANCE_TAG = "prash-test-fixture"
000034 | MARKER = "/tmp/prash-test-fixture-break"
000035 | WATCHDOG = "/tmp/prash-test-fixture-watchdog.log"
000036 | SERVICE = "prash-test-fixture.service"
000037 | [blank]
000038 | [blank]
000039 | def _env(path: str) -> dict[str, str]:
000040 |     out: dict[str, str] = {}
000041 |     if not os.path.exists(path):
000042 |         return out
000043 |     for line in open(path):
000044 |         line = line.strip()
000045 |         if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
000046 |             continue
000047 |         k, v = line.split("=", 1)
000048 |         out[k.strip()] = v.strip()
000049 |     return out
000050 | [blank]
000051 | [blank]
000052 | def _load_creds() -> dict[str, str]:
000053 |     repo_env = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "..", ".env")
000054 |     env = {**_env(repo_env), **os.environ}
000055 |     return {
000056 |         "aws_access_key_id": env.get("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"),
000057 |         "aws_secret_access_key": env.get("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"),
000058 |         "region": env.get("AWS_REGION", "us-east-1"),
000059 |     }
000060 | [blank]
000061 | [blank]
000062 | def _ec2_client(creds):
000063 |     return boto3.client(
000064 |         "ec2",
000065 |         aws_access_key_id=creds["aws_access_key_id"],
000066 |         aws_secret_access_key=creds["aws_secret_access_key"],
000067 |         region_name=creds["region"],
000068 |     )
000069 | [blank]
000070 | [blank]
000071 | def _ssm_client(creds):
000072 |     return boto3.client(
000073 |         "ssm",
000074 |         aws_access_key_id=creds["aws_access_key_id"],
000075 |         aws_secret_access_key=creds["aws_secret_access_key"],
000076 |         region_name=creds["region"],
000077 |     )
000078 | [blank]
000079 | [blank]
000080 | def _resolve_instance(ec2, instance_id: str | None) -> str | None:
000081 |     if instance_id:
000082 |         return instance_id
000083 |     # EC2_INSTANCE_ID env override, then a Name-tagged fixture
000084 |     env_id = os.environ.get("EC2_INSTANCE_ID")
000085 |     if env_id:
000086 |         return env_id
000087 |     resp = ec2.describe_instances(
000088 |         Filters=[
000089 |             {"Name": "tag:Name", "Values": [INSTANCE_TAG]},
000090 |             {"Name": "instance-state-name", "Values": ["running"]},
000091 |         ]
000092 |     )
000093 |     instances = [
000094 |         i["InstanceId"]
000095 |         for r in resp.get("Reservations", [])
000096 |         for i in r.get("Instances", [])
000097 |         if i.get("State", {}).get("Name") == "running"
000098 |     ]
000099 |     if not instances:
000100 |         print(
000101 |             f"No running EC2 instance tagged Name={INSTANCE_TAG} found. "
000102 |             "Create one, or pass --instance-id / set EC2_INSTANCE_ID.",
000103 |             file=sys.stderr,
000104 |         )
000105 |         return None
000106 |     return instances[0]
000107 | [blank]
000108 | [blank]
000109 | def _run_ssm(ssm, instance_id: str, command: str) -> dict:
000110 |     """Run a command via SSM and wait for completion. Returns {status, stdout, stderr}."""
000111 |     send = ssm.send_command(
000112 |         InstanceIds=[instance_id],
000113 |         DocumentName="AWS-RunShellScript",
000114 |         Parameters={"commands": [command]},
000115 |         TimeoutSeconds=60,
000116 |     )
000117 |     command_id = send["Command"]["CommandId"]
000118 |     # Poll until the invocation finishes (in a subprocess we can block; this is a CLI script).
000119 |     for _ in range(30):
000120 |         time.sleep(2)
000121 |         inv = ssm.get_command_invocation(CommandId=command_id, InstanceId=instance_id)
000122 |         status = inv.get("Status")
000123 |         if status not in ("Pending", "InProgress"):
000124 |             return {
000125 |                 "status": status,
000126 |                 "stdout": inv.get("StandardOutputContent", ""),
000127 |                 "stderr": inv.get("StandardErrorContent", ""),
000128 |             }
000129 |     return {"status": "Timeout", "stdout": "", "stderr": "timed out waiting for SSM"}
000130 | [blank]
000131 | [blank]
000132 | def _ensure_ssm_agent(ssm, instance_id: str) -> bool:
000133 |     """Make sure the SSM agent is present; if not, fall back to SSH via a PEM."""
000134 |     res = _run_ssm(ssm, instance_id, "echo ssm-ok")
000135 |     return res.get("status") == "Success"
000136 | [blank]
000137 | [blank]
000138 | def _public_ip(ec2, instance_id: str) -> str:
000139 |     """Resolve the instance's public IPv4 address (required for SSH)."""
000140 |     resp = ec2.describe_instances(InstanceIds=[instance_id])
000141 |     try:
000142 |         ip = resp["Reservations"][0]["Instances"][0]["PublicIpAddress"]
000143 |     except (KeyError, IndexError):
000144 |         raise SystemExit(
000145 |             f"Instance {instance_id} has no public IP assigned -- cannot use the SSH fallback path."
000146 |         )
000147 |     if not ip:
000148 |         raise SystemExit(
000149 |             f"Instance {instance_id} has no public IP assigned -- cannot use the SSH fallback path."
000150 |         )
000151 |     return ip
000152 | [blank]
000153 | [blank]
000154 | def main() -> int:
000155 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Force/heal a real failure state on the prash AWS test instance.")
000156 |     parser.add_argument("--instance-id", help="Target EC2 instance id (default: EC2_INSTANCE_ID env, else Name tag).")
000157 |     parser.add_argument("--pem", help="Path to an SSH .pem for the SSH-fallback path (only if SSM agent is absent).")
000158 |     parser.add_argument("--heal", action="store_true", help="Restore the instance instead of breaking it.")
000159 |     args = parser.parse_args()
000160 | [blank]
000161 |     creds = _load_creds()
000162 |     if not creds["aws_access_key_id"] or not creds["aws_secret_access_key"]:
000163 |         print("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY not set", file=sys.stderr)
000164 |         return 1
000165 | [blank]
000166 |     ec2 = _ec2_client(creds)
000167 |     instance_id = _resolve_instance(ec2, args.instance_id)
000168 |     if not instance_id:
000169 |         return 1
000170 | [blank]
000171 |     ssm = _ssm_client(creds)
000172 | [blank]
000173 |     # Establish reachability. Prefer SSM; if the agent is missing, use SSH
000174 |     # (the exact fallback path execute-aws exercises) when a --pem is given.
000175 |     use_ssh = False
000176 |     if not _ensure_ssm_agent(ssm, instance_id):
000177 |         if not args.pem:
000178 |             print(
000179 |                 "SSM agent not reachable and no --pem given -- cannot run commands. "
000180 |                 "Pass --pem to exercise the SSH fallback path.",
000181 |                 file=sys.stderr,
000182 |             )
000183 |             return 1
000184 |         use_ssh = True
000185 | [blank]
000186 |     def run(command: str) -> dict:
000187 |         if use_ssh:
000188 |             ssh_cmd = [
000189 |                 "ssh", "-i", args.pem,
000190 |                 "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=no",
000191 |                 "-o", "ConnectTimeout=10",
000192 |                 f"ubuntu@{_public_ip(ec2, instance_id)}",
000193 |                 command,
000194 |             ]
000195 |             result = subprocess.run(ssh_cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
000196 |             return {"status": "Success" if result.returncode == 0 else "Failed",
000197 |                     "stdout": result.stdout, "stderr": result.stderr}
000198 |         return _run_ssm(ssm, instance_id, command)
000199 | [blank]
000200 |     if args.heal:
000201 |         script = f"""
000202 | set -e
000203 | rm -f {MARKER}
000204 | if systemctl list-unit-files | grep -q '{SERVICE}'; then
000205 |   systemctl stop {SERVICE} 2>/dev/null || true
000206 |   systemctl disable {SERVICE} 2>/dev/null || true
000207 |   rm -f /etc/systemd/system/{SERVICE}
000208 |   systemctl daemon-reload 2>/dev/null || true
000209 | fi
000210 | pkill -f 'prash-test-fixture-loop' 2>/dev/null || true
000211 | rm -f {WATCHDOG}
000212 | echo healed

000214 |         res = run(script)
000215 |         print(f"heal command status: {res.get('status')}")
000216 |         if res.get("stderr", "").strip():

000218 |         print("instance restored -- poll_state() should settle back to HEALTHY shortly")
000219 |         return 0
000220 | [blank]
000221 |     # Break: install a fake systemd unit whose ExecStart is a background loop
000222 |     # that logs a watchdog line each second to BOTH journald and the on-disk
000223 |     # watchdog file. The unit's Type is simple and it keeps running, so
000224 |     # systemctl sees it as "active (running)" while the app it simulates is

000226 |     # (and execute-aws / fetch_logs) real lines to read.

000229 | cat > /etc/systemd/system/{SERVICE} <<'EOF'

000231 | Description=Prash test fixture simulated service
000232 | After=network.target
000233 | [blank]
000234 | [Service]
000235 | Type=simple
000236 | ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'while true; do echo "prash-test-fixture-loop watchdog tick: $(date -u +%%H:%%M:%%S)"; echo "prash-test-fixture-loop watchdog tick: $(date -u +%%H:%%M:%%S)" >> {WATCHDOG}; sleep 1; done'
000237 | Restart=always
000238 | EOF
000239 | systemctl daemon-reload
000240 | systemctl enable {SERVICE} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
000241 | systemctl start {SERVICE}
000242 | touch {MARKER}

000244 | systemctl status {SERVICE} --no-pager | head -n 8 || true

000247 | """

000252 |     print(f"failure state forced on {instance_id} -- a fake service is now 'running' but wedged")

000255 | [blank]
000256 | [blank]

### `scripts/testing/break_datadog.py`
````text
000001 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
000002 | """Reusable Datadog failure fixture (TESTING_SETUP.md).
000003 | [blank]
000004 | Creates (idempotently) one monitor, `prash-test-synthetic-error-rate`, on a
000005 | synthetic custom metric this script owns end to end -- no real service is
000006 | touched. Has both a warning and a critical threshold, so the same monitor
000007 | can be driven into three real states by how high a value is submitted.
000008 | Safe to re-run any number of times.
000009 | [blank]
000010 |     python3 scripts/testing/break_datadog.py          # force Alert (critical)
000011 |     python3 scripts/testing/break_datadog.py --warn   # force Warn (degraded)
000012 |     python3 scripts/testing/break_datadog.py --heal   # back to OK
000013 | [blank]
000014 | Found live 2026-09-07: this script submits ONE point per run, and Datadog's
000015 | monitor evaluation is sticky over sparse data -- a state change only lands
000016 | once a fresh point sits inside the monitor's 5m evaluation window (and, for
000017 | a recovery, once the earlier high value has aged out of it). If `investigate`
000018 | still shows the old state a couple of minutes after a run, just run the same
000019 | command again so a second fresh point lands, and give it ~1-5 minutes.
000020 | """
000021 | from __future__ import annotations
000022 | [blank]
000023 | import json
000024 | import os
000025 | import sys
000026 | import time
000027 | import urllib.error
000028 | import urllib.request
000029 | [blank]
000030 | MONITOR_NAME = "prash-test-synthetic-error-rate"
000031 | METRIC_NAME = "prash.test.synthetic_error_rate"
000032 | [blank]
000033 | [blank]
000034 | def _env(path: str) -> dict[str, str]:
000035 |     out: dict[str, str] = {}
000036 |     if not os.path.exists(path):
000037 |         return out
000038 |     for line in open(path):
000039 |         line = line.strip()
000040 |         if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
000041 |             continue
000042 |         k, v = line.split("=", 1)
000043 |         out[k.strip()] = v.strip().strip("'").strip('"')
000044 |     return out
000045 | [blank]
000046 | [blank]
000047 | def _request(base_url: str, headers: dict, method: str, path: str, body=None):
000048 |     data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
000049 |     req = urllib.request.Request(f"{base_url}{path}", data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
000050 |     try:
000051 |         with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
000052 |             raw = resp.read()
000053 |             return json.loads(raw) if raw else {}
000054 |     except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
000055 |         raise RuntimeError(f"Datadog API {exc.code}: {exc.read().decode(errors='replace')[:400]}") from exc
000056 | [blank]
000057 | [blank]
000058 | def main() -> int:
000059 |     env = {**_env(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "..", ".env")), **os.environ}
000060 |     api_key = env.get("DATADOG_API_KEY")
000061 |     app_key = env.get("DATADOG_APP_KEY")
000062 |     site = env.get("DATADOG_SITE") or "datadoghq.com"
000063 |     if not api_key or not app_key:
000064 |         print("DATADOG_API_KEY / DATADOG_APP_KEY not set", file=sys.stderr)
000065 |         return 1
000066 | [blank]
000067 |     base_url = f"https://api.{site}"
000068 |     headers = {
000069 |         "DD-API-KEY": api_key,
000070 |         "DD-APPLICATION-KEY": app_key,
000071 |         "Content-Type": "application/json",
000072 |     }
000073 | [blank]
000074 |     heal = "--heal" in sys.argv
000075 |     warn = "--warn" in sys.argv
000076 |     # Thresholds: warning=20, critical=50. 0 settles OK, 30 sits between the
000077 |     # two (Warn), 999 clears critical outright (Alert).
000078 |     value = 0 if heal else (30 if warn else 999)
000079 | [blank]
000080 |     now = int(time.time())
000081 |     _request(base_url, headers, "POST", "/api/v1/series", {
000082 |         "series": [{
000083 |             "metric": METRIC_NAME,
000084 |             "type": "gauge",
000085 |             "points": [[now, value]],
000086 |             "tags": ["source:prash-test-fixture"],
000087 |         }]
000088 |     })
000089 |     print(f"submitted {METRIC_NAME}={value}")
000090 | [blank]
000091 |     monitors = _request(base_url, headers, "GET", "/api/v1/monitor")
000092 |     existing = next((m for m in monitors if m.get("name") == MONITOR_NAME), None)
000093 | [blank]
000094 |     # A single query (critical threshold) plus a separate `warning` value in
000095 |     # options -- Datadog reports Warn once the metric crosses `warning` but
000096 |     # hasn't reached the query's own (critical) condition yet.
000097 |     query = f"avg(last_5m):avg:{METRIC_NAME}{{*}} > 50"
000098 |     payload = {
000099 |         "name": MONITOR_NAME,
000100 |         "type": "metric alert",
000101 |         "query": query,
000102 |         "message": "Prash test fixture -- safe to ignore/mute, owned by scripts/testing/break_datadog.py",
000103 |         "tags": ["prash:test-fixture"],
000104 |         "options": {"thresholds": {"critical": 50, "warning": 20}, "notify_no_data": False},
000105 |     }
000106 |     if existing:
000107 |         _request(base_url, headers, "PUT", f"/api/v1/monitor/{existing['id']}", payload)
000108 |         monitor_id = existing["id"]
000109 |         print(f"monitor exists: id={monitor_id}")
000110 |     else:
000111 |         created = _request(base_url, headers, "POST", "/api/v1/monitor", payload)
000112 |         monitor_id = created["id"]
000113 |         print(f"monitor created: id={monitor_id}")
000114 | [blank]
000115 |     if heal:
000116 |         print("submitted a clean value -- monitor will settle to OK within ~5min")
000117 |     elif warn:
000118 |         print("submitted a between-thresholds value -- monitor should show Warn within ~1-5min")
000119 |         print(f"check state: prash investigate '{MONITOR_NAME}' --provider datadog")
000120 |     else:
000121 |         print("submitted an over-threshold value -- monitor should show Alert within ~1-5min")
000122 |         print(f"check state: prash investigate '{MONITOR_NAME}' --provider datadog")
000123 | [blank]
000124 |     return 0
000125 | [blank]
000126 | [blank]
000127 | if __name__ == "__main__":
000128 |     raise SystemExit(main())
````

000021 | Requires VERCEL_TOKEN in .env (and optionally VERCEL_PROJECT, or pass

000078 |     items = resp.get("deployments", []) if isinstance(resp, dict) else []

000086 |     -- the rollback target, NOT the most-recent deployment."""

000089 | [blank]
000090 | [blank]
000091 | def main() -> int:
000092 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Force/heal real Vercel deployment churn (redeploy vs rollback).")
000093 |     parser.add_argument("--project", help="Vercel project id or name (default: VERCEL_PROJECT env).")
000094 |     parser.add_argument("--heal", action="store_true", help="Roll production back to the pre-break deployment instead of redeploying.")
000095 |     args = parser.parse_args()
000096 | [blank]
000097 |     creds = _load_creds()
000098 |     if not creds["token"]:

000100 |         return 1
000101 |     project = args.project or creds["project"]
000102 |     if not project:
000103 |         print(

000107 |             file=sys.stderr,

000117 |         items = deploys.get("deployments", []) if isinstance(deploys, dict) else []
000118 |         if len(items) < 2:

000120 |             return 1

### `scripts/testing/k8s-recovery-demo/README.md`
````text
000001 | # k8s-recovery demo fixture
000002 | [blank]
000003 | Reproduces the exact bug the `edit_configmap` action was built and live-verified
000004 | against: a `checkout-api` pod fails to reach Postgres because its ConfigMap's
000005 | `DATABASE_HOST` points at a nonexistent host (`postgres-wrong`), and recovers
000006 | the moment that key is corrected back to `postgres`.
000007 | [blank]
000008 | Runs against a dedicated `lear-demo` kind cluster/namespace — separate from the
000009 | `kind-prash-dev` / `prash-demo` cluster the rest of `scripts/testing/` uses.
000010 | [blank]
000011 | ```bash
000012 | ./setup-demo.sh          # creates kind cluster 'lear-demo', deploys postgres + checkout-api
000013 | ./inject-failure.sh       # patches DATABASE_HOST to the broken value, restarts the deployment
000014 | # ... diagnose it: prash fix lear-demo/checkout-api-... (recommends edit_configmap)
000015 | ./reset-demo.sh           # restores DATABASE_HOST, waits for recovery
000016 | ```
000017 | [blank]
000018 | `manifests/postgres.yaml`'s `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=demo` is a throwaway value for
000019 | this local-only cluster, not a real credential.
````

000001 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
000002 | """checkout-api demo app.
000003 | [blank]
000004 | On startup, tries to open a TCP connection to DATABASE_HOST:5432. If it
000005 | succeeds, serves a /healthz endpoint on :8080 and stays up. If it fails,
000006 | logs a clear error to stdout (visible via `kubectl logs`) and exits
000007 | non-zero, which causes CrashLoopBackOff under a Deployment -- the
000008 | intended failure mode for this demo.
000009 | """
000010 | import http.server
000011 | import os
000012 | import socket
000013 | import sys
000014 | import time
000015 | [blank]
000016 | DATABASE_HOST = os.environ.get("DATABASE_HOST", "")
000017 | DATABASE_PORT = int(os.environ.get("DATABASE_PORT", "5432"))
000018 | CONNECT_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT", "3"))
000019 | [blank]
000020 | [blank]
000021 | RETRIES = int(os.environ.get("DB_CONNECT_RETRIES", "8"))
000022 | RETRY_DELAY = float(os.environ.get("DB_RETRY_DELAY", "1.5"))
000023 | [blank]
000024 | [blank]
000025 | def check_database():
000026 |     print(f"[checkout-api] starting up, DATABASE_HOST={DATABASE_HOST!r} DATABASE_PORT={DATABASE_PORT}", flush=True)
000027 |     last_err = None
000028 |     for attempt in range(1, RETRIES + 1):
000029 |         try:
000030 |             with socket.create_connection((DATABASE_HOST, DATABASE_PORT), timeout=CONNECT_TIMEOUT):
000031 |                 print(f"[checkout-api] connected to {DATABASE_HOST}:{DATABASE_PORT} OK (attempt {attempt})", flush=True)
000032 |                 return True
000033 |         except Exception as e:
000034 |             last_err = e
000035 |             print(f"[checkout-api] attempt {attempt}/{RETRIES}: could not reach {DATABASE_HOST}:{DATABASE_PORT} -- {type(e).__name__}: {e}", flush=True)
000036 |             if attempt < RETRIES:
000037 |                 time.sleep(RETRY_DELAY)
000038 |     print(f"[checkout-api] FATAL: could not connect to database at {DATABASE_HOST}:{DATABASE_PORT} after {RETRIES} attempts -- {type(last_err).__name__}: {last_err}", flush=True)
000039 |     print(f"[checkout-api] check configmap/checkout-api-config key DATABASE_HOST -- current value is {DATABASE_HOST!r}", flush=True)
000040 |     return False

### `scripts/testing/measure_correlation_accuracy.py`
````text
000001 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
000002 | """Measures the §3 quantitative metric M6 couldn't close: single-source vs
000003 | 2-source false-positive rate on GENUINELY ambiguous incidents.
000004 | [blank]
000005 | The M6 combined fixture (break_combined.py) proved the correlation MECHANISM
000006 | live (real k8s crash + real Datadog spike -> one incident) but its two legs
000007 | are semantically unrelated to each other, so there was no scenario where a
000008 | single-source diagnosis is plausibly *wrong* to compare against. This script
000009 | is that missing piece: N scenarios, each with a KNOWN true root cause that is
000010 | only identifiable when a k8s signal is combined with a Datadog signal --
000011 | single-source evidence alone plausibly leads the brain to the wrong (or an
000012 | incomplete/unhelpful) hypothesis.
000013 | [blank]
000014 | Why the evidence is constructed, not read from a live cluster/Datadog account
000015 | (unlike break_combined.py): this measures the DIAGNOSIS BRAIN's reasoning
000016 | over given evidence, not the connectors' read path -- that's already covered
000017 | by the connector test suites and the M6 mechanism-proof fixture. The inputs
000018 | below are built in the exact shape the real connectors produce (same
000019 | PodStatus/get_pod_events dict shape, same ConnectorEvent TypedDict), so
000020 | `format_k8s_context()` and `diagnose_failure()` run for real, unmocked --
000021 | only the evidence's origin is synthetic, not the diagnosis call itself.
000022 | [blank]
000023 |     python3 scripts/testing/measure_correlation_accuracy.py
000024 | [blank]
000025 | Real LLM calls (2 per scenario: single-source, multi-source). Not free, not
000026 | instant -- this is a measurement run, not a unit test.
000027 | """
000028 | from __future__ import annotations
000029 | [blank]
000030 | import asyncio
000031 | import datetime
000032 | [blank]
000033 | from prash.brain.diagnosis_agent import diagnose_failure, format_k8s_context
000034 | from prash.cli import _export_cluster_env
000035 | from prash.connectors.kubernetes import PodStatus
000036 | from prash.credentials import CredentialStore
000037 | [blank]
000038 | # The brain reads KIMI_API_KEY/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY etc. from os.environ, not
000039 | # from .env directly -- cli.py's _export_cluster_env() does this for every
000040 | # real command; a standalone script must do it too or every call 404s on
000041 | # "API key not set" even with a fully populated .env.
000042 | _export_cluster_env(CredentialStore.from_env().load())
000043 | [blank]
000044 | UTC = datetime.timezone.utc
000045 | [blank]
000046 | [blank]
000047 | def _event(connector: str, event_type: str, summary: str, ts: datetime.datetime) -> dict:
000048 |     return {"timestamp": ts, "connector": connector, "event_type": event_type, "summary": summary, "raw": {}}
000049 | [blank]
000050 | [blank]
000051 | # ── Scenario A: DB connection-pool saturation, misread as an app-side issue ──
000052 | _NOW = datetime.datetime.now(UTC)
000053 | [blank]
000054 | SCENARIO_A = {

000056 |     "pod_status": PodStatus(
000057 |         name="checkout-api-7f9d2", namespace="prod", phase="Running",
000058 |         problem="CrashLoopBackOff", restart_count=11, ready=False,
000059 |     ),
000060 |     "logs": (

000062 |         "connecting to database...\n"
000063 |         "ERROR: dial tcp 10.0.4.12:5432: i/o timeout\n"
000064 |         "starting checkout-api v2.3.1\n"
000065 |         "connecting to database...\n"
000066 |         "ERROR: dial tcp 10.0.4.12:5432: i/o timeout\n"
000067 |     ),
000068 |     "k8s_events": [
000069 |         {"type": "Warning", "reason": "BackOff", "message": "Back-off restarting failed container", "count": 11, "last_timestamp": str(_NOW)},
000070 |     ],
000071 |     "datadog_event": _event(

000074 |         _NOW,
000075 |     ),

000081 | [blank]

000087 |         problem=None, restart_count=0, ready=True,
000088 |     ),
000089 |     "logs": (

000093 |         "ERROR: upstream request failed: context deadline exceeded\n"
000094 |         "processing checkout for order 88215\n"
000095 |         "ERROR: upstream request failed: context deadline exceeded\n"
000096 |     ),
000097 |     "k8s_events": [],
000098 |     "datadog_event": _event(
000099 |         "datadog", "monitor_alert",
000100 |         "payment-service error rate at 82% (baseline 0.5%) -- service degraded",
000101 |         _NOW,
000102 |     ),

000106 |     "true_cause_keywords": ["payment-service", "payment service", "upstream", "degraded"],
000107 |     "wrong_if_recommends": {"restart_pod"},
000108 | }
000109 | [blank]
000110 | SCENARIOS = [SCENARIO_A, SCENARIO_B]
000111 | [blank]
000112 | [blank]
000113 | def _single_source_context(scenario: dict) -> str:
000114 |     return format_k8s_context(scenario["pod_status"], scenario["logs"], scenario["k8s_events"])
000115 | [blank]
000116 | [blank]
000117 | def _multi_source_context(scenario: dict) -> str:
000118 |     """k8s context + the correlated Datadog signal appended as additional
000119 |     evidence -- mirrors how a real caller would fold correlation.
000120 |     format_incident_context()'s unified timeline into the diagnosis prompt."""
000121 |     base = _single_source_context(scenario)
000122 |     dd = scenario["datadog_event"]
000123 |     correlated = (
000124 |         "\n\n=== CORRELATED SIGNAL (Datadog, same incident window) ===\n"
000125 |         f"[{dd['timestamp']}] {dd['event_type']}: {dd['summary']}\n"
000126 |         "This event occurred in the same time window as the pod issue above and "
000127 |         "very likely shares one root cause -- consider both signals together, "

000129 |     )

000131 | [blank]
000132 | [blank]
000133 | def _grade(scenario: dict, diagnosis) -> tuple[bool, str]:
000134 |     """True if the diagnosis correctly names the true cause and doesn't
000135 |     recommend an action that only makes sense if the cause were something
000136 |     else. Returns (correct, reason)."""
000137 |     text = f"{diagnosis.root_cause} {diagnosis.fix_description}".lower()
000138 |     names_cause = any(kw.lower() in text for kw in scenario["true_cause_keywords"])
000139 |     wrong_action = diagnosis.recommended_action in scenario["wrong_if_recommends"]
000140 |     if wrong_action:
000141 |         return False, f"recommended {diagnosis.recommended_action!r}, which only fixes the wrong cause"
000142 |     if not names_cause:
000143 |         return False, "root cause doesn't name the true issue (expected one of: " + ", ".join(scenario["true_cause_keywords"]) + ")"
000144 |     return True, "correctly identifies the true cause and doesn't propose a wrong-cause fix"
000145 | [blank]
000146 | [blank]
000147 | async def _run_scenario(scenario: dict) -> dict:
000148 |     single_ctx = _single_source_context(scenario)
000149 |     multi_ctx = _multi_source_context(scenario)
000150 | [blank]
000151 |     single_diag = await diagnose_failure(
000152 |         logs=single_ctx, repo_full_name=f"prod/{scenario['pod_status'].name}",
000153 |         commit_message="(no commit -- Kubernetes pod diagnosis)", workflow_name="kubernetes",
000154 |     )
000155 |     multi_diag = await diagnose_failure(
000156 |         logs=multi_ctx, repo_full_name=f"prod/{scenario['pod_status'].name}",
000157 |         commit_message="(no commit -- Kubernetes pod diagnosis)", workflow_name="kubernetes",
000158 |     )
000159 | [blank]
000160 |     single_correct, single_reason = _grade(scenario, single_diag)
000161 |     multi_correct, multi_reason = _grade(scenario, multi_diag)
000162 | [blank]
000163 |     return {
000164 |         "name": scenario["name"],
000165 |         "single": (single_correct, single_reason, single_diag),
000166 |         "multi": (multi_correct, multi_reason, multi_diag),
000167 |     }
000168 | [blank]
000169 | [blank]
000170 | async def main() -> int:
000171 |     results = []
000172 |     for scenario in SCENARIOS:
000173 |         print(f"\n{'=' * 78}\n{scenario['name']}\n{'=' * 78}")
000174 |         result = await _run_scenario(scenario)
000175 |         results.append(result)
000176 | [blank]
000177 |         for label, (correct, reason, diag) in (("SINGLE-SOURCE (k8s only)", result["single"]),
000178 |                                                  ("MULTI-SOURCE (k8s + Datadog)", result["multi"])):
000179 |             mark = "CORRECT" if correct else "WRONG"

000001 | # Demo Failure Injection — Pre-Scripted Breaks & Resets
000002 | [blank]

000011 | [blank]
000012 | ---
000013 | [blank]
000014 | ### Failure 1: ConfigMap Break (PRIMARY — use this in the demo)
000015 | [blank]
000016 | **What breaks:** `checkout-api` ConfigMap `DATABASE_HOST` is patched from `postgres` to `postgres-wrong`. Pod can't reach the database, enters `CrashLoopBackOff`.
000017 | [blank]
000018 | **Why this one:** Already proven — this is the exact scenario the `edit-configmap` action was built and live-verified against. Zero risk of it not working.
000019 | [blank]
000020 | **Inject:**
000021 | ```bash
000022 | # scripts/demo/scripts/inject-configmap-break.sh
000023 | kubectl patch configmap checkout-api-config -n lear-demo \
000024 |   --type merge -p '{"data":{"DATABASE_HOST":"postgres-wrong"}}'
000025 | kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout-api -n lear-demo
000026 | echo "💥 Failure injected: checkout-api will CrashLoopBackOff (DATABASE_HOST → postgres-wrong)"
000027 | ```
000028 | [blank]
000029 | **What Prash does:**
000030 | 1. Watcher detects CrashLoopBackOff (~15-30s)
000031 | 2. `prash fix lear-demo/checkout-api-xxx` diagnoses: "ConfigMap DATABASE_HOST points to nonexistent host"
000032 | 3. Recommends `edit-configmap` (APPROVAL tier)
000033 | 4. On approval: patches ConfigMap back to `postgres`, restarts deployment
000034 | 5. Verifies: pod recovers, readiness probe passes
000035 | [blank]
000036 | **Reset:**
000037 | ```bash
000038 | # scripts/demo/scripts/reset-configmap.sh
000039 | kubectl patch configmap checkout-api-config -n lear-demo \
000040 |   --type merge -p '{"data":{"DATABASE_HOST":"postgres"}}'
000041 | kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout-api -n lear-demo
000042 | echo "✅ Reset: DATABASE_HOST restored to 'postgres'"
000043 | ```
000044 | [blank]
000045 | **Tested:** ✅ Live-verified against real Kind cluster (see `k8s-recovery-demo/README.md`)
000046 | [blank]
000047 | ---
000048 | [blank]
000049 | ### Failure 2: OOMKill (BACKUP — shows different failure type)
000050 | [blank]
000051 | **What breaks:** `checkout-api` memory limit set to 16Mi. Under load, pod gets OOMKilled.
000052 | [blank]
000053 | **Inject:**
000054 | ```bash

000056 | kubectl set resources deployment/checkout-api -n lear-demo \
000057 |   --limits=memory=16Mi

000059 | ```
000060 | [blank]
000061 | **What Prash does:**

000063 | 2. Diagnosis: "Container killed by OOM (memory limit 16Mi too low for workload)"

000066 | [blank]
000067 | **Reset:**

000070 | kubectl set resources deployment/checkout-api -n lear-demo \
000071 |   --limits=memory=128Mi --requests=memory=64Mi
000072 | echo "✅ Reset: memory limits restored to 128Mi"
000073 | ```
000074 | [blank]
000075 | ---
000076 | [blank]
000077 | ### Failure 3: Combined K8s + Datadog Correlation (ADVANCED — if time permits)
000078 | [blank]

000081 | **Inject:**

000095 | **What Prash does:**

000001 | # Demo Episodic Memory — "I've Seen This Before"
000002 | [blank]
000003 | **Owner:** Aradhya (memory) / Anant (integration)  
000004 | **Time to complete:** ~2 hours

000008 | [blank]
000009 | ## Why This Matters for the Demo
000010 | [blank]
000011 | The AWS engineer explicitly called out **episodic memory** as critical: "if an agent resolved an incident before and the environment is unchanged, it should replay the same steps rather than re-derive a solution." This is one of the sharpest things we can show an investor.
000012 | [blank]
000013 | **Demo flow:**
000014 | 1. Break `checkout-api` (ConfigMap) → Prash diagnoses from scratch → fixes it
000015 | 2. Break `checkout-api` the SAME WAY → Prash says "I've seen this before" → replays the fix instantly
000016 | [blank]
000017 | ---

000019 | ## Current State
000020 | [blank]
000021 | `RepoMemory` in [`brain/repo_memory.py`](file:///c:/Users/anant/Downloads/Lear-Backend/Lear-Backend/prash/brain/repo_memory.py) already has the data model:
000022 | - `similar_fixes: list[dict]` — previous verified fixes
000023 | - `repeated_error_signatures: list[dict]` — error patterns seen before
000024 | - `as_prompt_context()` → formats for the diagnosis brain prompt
000025 | [blank]
000026 | **Problem:** The builder (`build_repo_memory()`) was Supabase-backed in v1. v2 has no database. The dataclass and formatter exist, but there's no way to populate them locally.
000027 | [blank]

000029 | [blank]
000030 | ## Tasks
000031 | [blank]
000032 | ### T1. Build local JSON-backed memory store
000033 | [blank]
000034 | Create `prash/brain/local_memory.py`:
000035 | [blank]
000036 | ```python
000037 | """Local JSON-backed episodic memory for Lear.
000038 | [blank]
000039 | Stores verified fixes and error signatures in .prash/memory.json.
000040 | No database dependency — works entirely from the local filesystem.
000041 | """
000042 | import json
000043 | import os
000044 | from pathlib import Path
000045 | from typing import Optional
000046 | from .repo_memory import RepoMemory
000047 | [blank]
000048 | MEMORY_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("PRASH_MEMORY_PATH", ".prash/memory.json"))
000049 | [blank]
000050 | def load_memory(repo_id: str = "default") -> RepoMemory:
000051 |     """Load episodic memory from local JSON store."""
000052 |     if not MEMORY_PATH.exists():
000053 |         return RepoMemory(repo_id=repo_id)
000054 |     data = json.loads(MEMORY_PATH.read_text())
000055 |     return RepoMemory(
000056 |         repo_id=repo_id,
000057 |         similar_fixes=data.get("similar_fixes", []),
000058 |         repeated_error_signatures=data.get("repeated_error_signatures", []),
000059 |         category_outcomes=data.get("category_outcomes", {}),
000060 |     )
000061 | [blank]
000062 | def save_fix(diagnosis_summary: dict, verified: bool = True) -> None:
000063 |     """Append a verified fix to the local memory store."""
000064 |     data = {}
000065 |     if MEMORY_PATH.exists():
000066 |         data = json.loads(MEMORY_PATH.read_text())
000067 |     
000068 |     fixes = data.setdefault("similar_fixes", [])
000069 |     fixes.append(diagnosis_summary)
000070 |     
000071 |     # Also update error signature tracking
000072 |     signatures = data.setdefault("repeated_error_signatures", [])
000073 |     sig = diagnosis_summary.get("error_signature")
000074 |     if sig:
000075 |         existing = next((s for s in signatures if s["error_signature"] == sig), None)
000076 |         if existing:
000077 |             existing["count"] += 1
000078 |             existing["last_category"] = diagnosis_summary.get("category")
000079 |             existing["last_status"] = "verified" if verified else "unverified"
000080 |         else:
000081 |             signatures.append({
000082 |                 "error_signature": sig,
000083 |                 "count": 1,
000084 |                 "last_category": diagnosis_summary.get("category"),
000085 |                 "last_status": "verified" if verified else "unverified",
000086 |             })
000087 |     
000088 |     MEMORY_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
000089 |     MEMORY_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, default=str))
000090 | ```

000001 | # Connector Rewrite — Task Overview
000002 | [blank]
000003 | **Goal:** Fully autonomous **watch → diagnose → fix → verify → notify** loop for every connector in the Lear system.
000004 | [blank]
000005 | **Source of truth:** [`CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC.md`](file:///c:/Users/anant/Downloads/Lear-Backend/Lear-Backend/CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC.md) · [`PRASH_V2.md`](file:///c:/Users/anant/Downloads/Lear-Backend/Lear-Backend/PRASH_V2.md)
000006 | [blank]
000007 | ---
000008 | [blank]
000009 | ## The Autonomous Loop (every connector must complete this)
000010 | [blank]
000011 | ```
000012 | ┌─────────┐     ┌───────────┐     ┌──────┐     ┌────────┐     ┌────────┐
000013 | │  WATCH  │ ──▶ │ DIAGNOSE  │ ──▶ │ FIX  │ ──▶ │ VERIFY │ ──▶ │ NOTIFY │
000014 | │ watch() │     │ get_stats │     │Action│     │verify()│     │ alert  │
000015 | │ polls   │     │ brain     │     │ exec │     │re-check│     │ Action │
000016 | └─────────┘     └───────────┘     └──────┘     └────────┘     └────────┘
000017 |      ▲                                                              │
000018 |      └──────────────────── loop back ◀─────────────────────────────┘
000019 | ```
000020 | [blank]
000021 | Every connector rewrite must implement **all five stages** to close the loop.
000022 | [blank]
000023 | ---
000024 | [blank]
000025 | ## Shared Interface Contract (from §4 of CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC)
000026 | [blank]
000027 | ### Read layer additions to `Connector` ABC (`connectors/base.py`)
000028 | [blank]
000029 | | Method | Purpose | Returns |
000030 | |---|---|---|
000031 | | `watch(target)` | Begin monitoring a target; feeds the shared watcher loop | `WatchHandle` |
000032 | | `get_stats(target, since?)` | Time-series of normalized events for a target | `list[ConnectorEvent]` |
000033 | [blank]
000034 | ### `ConnectorEvent` — the cross-provider join shape
000035 | [blank]
000036 | ```python
000037 | class ConnectorEvent(TypedDict):

000041 |     summary: str           # one human-readable line
000042 |     raw: dict              # untouched provider payload
000043 | ```
000044 | [blank]
000045 | ### Write layer — `alert()` as a gated Action per provider
000046 | [blank]
000047 | Each provider that can alert gets a new `Action` subclass (e.g. `DatadogAlertAction`, `PagerDutyPageAction`) with `risk_tier=APPROVAL` by default.
000048 | [blank]

000014 | ## ⚠️ Critical Architectural Decision Required (M0/M1b)
000015 | [blank]
000016 | **Kubernetes is the odd one out:** it uses module-level functions (`get_pod_status()`, `get_pod_logs()`, etc.) instead of the `Connector` class pattern every other connector follows. The watcher (`watcher.py`) imports directly from these module-level functions.
000017 | [blank]
000018 | **Options (decide at M0, record in CONNECTOR_REWRITE_SPEC §8):**
000019 | [blank]
000020 | | Option | Pros | Cons |
000021 | |---|---|---|
000022 | | **Full convert to `KubernetesConnector(Connector)`** | Clean, consistent, natural `watch()`/`get_stats()` home | Largest refactor, touches watcher.py heavily |
000023 | | **Thin adapter wrapping existing functions** | Minimal disruption, existing code stays | Two interfaces to maintain, adapter adds indirection |
000024 | [blank]
000025 | **Recommendation:** Full convert. The watcher refactor (M5) needs to happen anyway, and the adapter just delays the inevitable.

000035 | ```

000101 | [blank]
000102 | ## Anti-Hardcoding Mandate
000103 | [blank]
000104 | > **CRITICAL RULE:** Every piece of code built for the desktop app MUST be verified against hardcoding. No mock data, no placeholder values, no simulated responses in production code paths.
000105 | [blank]
000106 | Every spec includes an **Anti-Hardcoding Test Suite** that specifically checks:
000107 | [blank]

### `tasks/questions.md`
````text
000001 | # Meeting Questions — AWS Engineer & DevOps Engineer (Hong Kong)
000002 | [blank]
000003 | **Context:** Lear is an AI DevOps agent (local-first, credentials never leave the user's machine) that watches infrastructure (K8s, CI, cloud), diagnoses failures, and acts with human approval. We're a 3-person startup building this. 20-25 min per meeting — every question must earn its time.
000004 | [blank]
000005 | ---
000006 | [blank]
000007 | ## For the AWS Engineer
000008 | [blank]
000009 | ### Escalation Management (5 min)
000010 | [blank]
000011 | 1. **When an automated system (like Lear) triggers a wrong action in prod — what does AWS's internal escalation chain actually look like in the first 5 minutes?** We have a circuit breaker (5 actions/60s cap) and a permission-tier system, but we've never had a real mis-action in prod. What do teams that handle this well do that we might not be thinking about?
000012 | [blank]
000013 | 2. **How does AWS decide which automated remediations are safe to run without human approval vs. which always need a human?** We have a SAFE/APPROVAL/NEVER tier system — is there a framework or set of heuristics your teams use that we should steal?
000014 | [blank]
000015 | 3. **When an AI agent has access to write to prod (restart pods, scale, exec, rollback) — what's the minimum telemetry/audit trail you'd want to see before you'd trust it?** Our audit log records every action, tier, approval status, and outcome — is that enough, or are we missing something critical?
000016 | [blank]
000017 | ### Architecture & Infrastructure (5 min)
000018 | [blank]
000019 | 4. **We run entirely local-first — credentials never touch our servers. If a startup customer wants Lear running 24/7 as "autopilot" (watching prod while the team sleeps), what's the cheapest reliable way to host a lightweight Python polling agent in AWS?** Fargate? A t3.micro? Lambda on a schedule? What would you actually recommend for a team of 5 that doesn't want to babysit infra for their infra tool?
000020 | [blank]
000021 | 5. **Our watcher polls K8s/cloud APIs on intervals (5s-60s). At what scale does polling become a problem, and what's the migration path?** We're targeting startups (5-50 engineers, a few clusters). Is there a threshold where we'd need to move to event-driven (CloudWatch Events, K8s informers)?
000022 | [blank]
000023 | ### Moat & What AWS Won't Build (7-8 min — the most important section)
000024 | [blank]
000025 | 6. **AWS has re:Invent every year. What's the realistic version of "Amazon builds this"?** Is an AI agent that diagnoses and acts on your own infrastructure something AWS would productize — or does their business model (you use more services = they earn more) structurally prevent them from building something that *reduces* cloud resource consumption by fixing problems faster? Where's the ceiling on what Amazon actually has incentive to solve for a startup?
000026 | [blank]
000027 | 7. **AWS DevOps Guru exists. Amazon Q for DevOps exists. In your experience using these — what do they not do?** We're not trying to beat AWS at observability. We're trying to be the thing that *acts* after they've told you something is wrong. Is that gap real in practice, or does AWS already close it for most teams?
000028 | [blank]
000029 | 8. **What's a problem your team hits with AWS infrastructure that you'd never expect AWS to build a product for — because it's too specific to your stack, your team's processes, or your own internal systems?** These are the exact cracks Lear can fill. A platform vendor builds for the median user; an agent configured by your team acts for *you*. We want to know what the median misses.
000030 | [blank]
000031 | 9. **The "credentials never leave your machine" model is our core trust argument. Does that actually matter to you, or is it just good marketing?** If you had to choose between a product that's slightly better but holds your keys, vs. a product that's slightly worse but you hold your own keys — how do you actually make that call? What's the real weight of that tradeoff for a startup vs. an enterprise?
000032 | [blank]
000033 | 10. **What's something you've automated internally that no vendor tool could've done for you — because it required knowing your specific team's runbook, your naming conventions, your blast radius?** That's the kind of customization Lear is built to support (the brain can be taught your environment). Is that actually valuable, or does it just shift the config burden onto the customer?
000034 | [blank]
000035 | ### Product/Trust (2-3 min)
000036 | [blank]
000037 | 11. **If you were evaluating Lear for your own team — what would make you say "no" in the first 5 minutes of a demo?** What's the trust-killer for an AI agent that touches infra?
000038 | [blank]
000039 | ---
000040 | [blank]
000041 | ## For the DevOps Engineer (Hong Kong Company)
000042 | [blank]
000043 | ### How Escalations Actually Work (5 min)
000044 | [blank]
000045 | 1. **Walk me through your last real production incident — from the first alert to resolution. What were the handoff points, and where did time get wasted?** We're building Lear to compress that timeline. Knowing where the real friction is tells us where to focus.
000046 | [blank]
000047 | 2. **When your monitoring (Datadog/Grafana/PagerDuty) fires an alert at 3am — what's the actual human workflow?** Who gets paged? What do they check first? What tools do they open? How long before they know if it's real or noise? Lear is supposed to do that first-pass triage automatically.
000048 | [blank]
000049 | 3. **How many of your incidents in a typical month could have been fixed by a restart, a rollback, or a config change — vs. needing a real engineer to think?** We're trying to validate our bet that most DevOps incidents are rote actions wrapped in diagnosis time.
000050 | [blank]
000051 | ### Team & Tooling Reality (5 min)
000052 | [blank]

000054 | [blank]

000056 | [blank]

### `tasks/week1/backend/B-01_SPLIT_SERVER.md`
````text
000001 | # B-01 — Split `server.py` into Route Modules
000002 | [blank]
000003 | **Owner:** Anant
000004 | **Priority:** P0
000005 | **Status:** ⬜ Not Started
000006 | **Estimated effort:** 2–3 days
000007 | **Depends on:** B-03 (extract shared state first — route modules should import from `AppState`, not use globals)
000008 | **Blocks:** B-04 (API versioning needs route modules to exist), S-02 (rate limiting is easier with routers)
000009 | [blank]
000010 | ---
000011 | [blank]
000012 | ## Objective
000013 | [blank]
000014 | Decompose the 3,896-line `prash/server.py` monolith into focused route modules using FastAPI's `APIRouter`. After this task, `server.py` is the app factory only (under 200 lines), and all endpoint logic lives in `prash/routes/*.py`.
000015 | [blank]
000016 | ---
000017 | [blank]
000018 | ## Why This Matters
000019 | [blank]
000020 | - **Currently:** `server.py` is 165 KB / 3,896 lines containing 83 endpoint handlers, global state, helper functions, middleware, lifespan management, and business logic all in one file. This makes it:
000021 |   - Impossible to review PRs that touch the file (merge conflicts guaranteed)
000022 |   - Difficult to test individual route groups in isolation
000023 |   - Hard to navigate (finding a specific endpoint requires searching 4K lines)
000024 | - **After:** Each route group is a self-contained module. Endpoints are organized by domain. `server.py` is a thin app factory that registers routers and middleware.
000025 | [blank]
000026 | ---
000027 | [blank]
000028 | ## Route Module Breakdown
000029 | [blank]
000030 | Based on the 83 endpoints currently in `server.py`, split into these modules:
000031 | [blank]
000032 | | Module | Endpoints | Approximate Lines |
000033 | |---|---|---|
000034 | | `routes/connectors.py` | `/api/connectors`, `/api/connectors/{id}/*`, `/api/connect/{id}` | ~600 |
000035 | | `routes/watcher.py` | `/api/connectors/{id}/watch`, `/api/watch/*`, WebSocket `/ws/events` | ~400 |
000036 | | `routes/chat.py` | `/api/chat/*`, `/api/chat/sessions/*`, `/api/chat/upload` | ~500 |
000037 | | `routes/dashboard.py` | `/api/dashboard/*`, `/api/status`, `/api/metrics/*` | ~300 |
000038 | | `routes/settings.py` | `/api/settings`, `/api/config` | ~150 |
000039 | | `routes/notifications.py` | `/api/notifications/*` | ~100 |
000040 | | `routes/projects.py` | `/api/projects/*` | ~300 |
000041 | | `routes/widgets.py` | `/api/connectors/{id}/widgets`, `/api/connectors/{id}/generate-widgets` | ~200 |
000042 | | `routes/activity.py` | `/api/activity` | ~50 |
000043 | | `routes/system.py` | `/api/system/*`, `/api/auth/*` | ~50 |
000044 | | `routes/demo.py` | `/demo`, `/store`, `/admin`, `/api/demo/*` | ~800 |
000045 | | `routes/incidents.py` | `/incident/*`, `/api/incident/*`, `/api/incidents` | ~400 |
000046 | | `routes/email.py` | `/api/email/*` | ~100 |
000047 | | `routes/slack.py` | `/api/slack/*` | ~100 |
000048 | [blank]
000049 | ---
000050 | [blank]
000051 | ## Implementation Plan
000052 | [blank]
000053 | ### Step 1: Create the `routes/` package
000054 | [blank]
000055 | ```
000056 | prash/
000057 |   routes/
000058 |     __init__.py          # Empty or router registration helper
000059 |     connectors.py
000060 |     watcher.py
000061 |     chat.py
000062 |     dashboard.py
000063 |     settings.py
000064 |     notifications.py
000065 |     projects.py
000066 |     widgets.py
000067 |     activity.py
000068 |     system.py
000069 |     demo.py
000070 |     incidents.py
000071 |     email.py
000072 |     slack.py
000073 | ```
000074 | [blank]
000075 | ### Step 2: Extract one module at a time (NOT all at once)
000076 | [blank]
000077 | The safest approach is to extract one route group, run all tests, commit, then move to the next.
000078 | [blank]
000079 | **Order of extraction** (easiest/least-coupled first):
000080 | [blank]
000081 | 1. `routes/system.py` — `/api/system/version` (small, no dependencies)
000082 | 2. `routes/activity.py` — `/api/activity` (small, reads from `_activity_log`)
000083 | 3. `routes/notifications.py` — `/api/notifications/*` (isolated)
000084 | 4. `routes/settings.py` — `/api/settings`, `/api/config` (reads/writes `.env`)
000085 | 5. `routes/projects.py` — `/api/projects/*` (reads/writes `prash.yaml`)
000086 | 6. `routes/widgets.py` — widget-related endpoints
000087 | 7. `routes/dashboard.py` — dashboard summary + activity
000088 | 8. `routes/connectors.py` — **largest group, most coupling to shared state**
000089 | 9. `routes/watcher.py` — watcher management + WebSocket
000090 | 10. `routes/chat.py` — chat/streaming endpoints
000091 | 11. `routes/demo.py` — demo/store/admin pages
000092 | 12. `routes/incidents.py` — incident management
000093 | 13. `routes/email.py` — email endpoints
000094 | 14. `routes/slack.py` — Slack endpoints
000095 | [blank]
000096 | ### Step 3: Pattern for each extraction
000097 | [blank]
000098 | Each route module follows this exact pattern:
000099 | [blank]
000100 | ```python
000101 | # prash/routes/system.py
000102 | """System information and health endpoints."""
000103 | from __future__ import annotations
000104 | [blank]
000105 | from fastapi import APIRouter
000106 | [blank]
000107 | router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["system"])
000108 | [blank]
000109 | [blank]
000110 | @router.get("/system/version")
000111 | async def get_system_version():
000112 |     """Return system version and configuration info."""
000113 |     return {
000114 |         "name": "Lear",
000115 |         "version": "2.0.0",
000116 |         "engine": "FastAPI + Prash Core",
000117 |         # ... rest of the existing implementation
000118 |     }
000119 | ```
000120 | [blank]
000121 | ### Step 4: Register routers in `server.py`
000122 | [blank]
000123 | After all extractions, `server.py` becomes:
000124 | [blank]
000125 | ```python
000126 | """Lear Backend — FastAPI Application Factory.
000127 | [blank]
000128 | This file creates the FastAPI app, registers middleware, and mounts
000129 | route modules. All endpoint logic lives in prash/routes/*.
000130 | """
000131 | from __future__ import annotations
000132 | [blank]
000133 | from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
000134 | from fastapi import FastAPI
000135 | from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
000136 | [blank]
000137 | from prash.routes import (
000138 |     activity, chat, connectors, dashboard, demo, email,
000139 |     incidents, notifications, projects, settings, slack,
000140 |     system, watcher, widgets,
000141 | )
000142 | from prash.state import AppState
000143 | [blank]
000144 | [blank]
000145 | @asynccontextmanager
000146 | async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
000147 |     # Startup logic (restore watches, start polling, etc.)
000148 |     state: AppState = app.state.app_state
000149 |     await state.startup()
000150 |     yield
000151 |     await state.shutdown()
000152 | [blank]
000153 | [blank]
000154 | def create_app() -> FastAPI:
000155 |     app = FastAPI(title="Lear Desktop API", version="2.0.0", lifespan=lifespan)
000156 | [blank]
000157 |     # -- State --
000158 |     app.state.app_state = AppState()
000159 | [blank]
000160 |     # -- Middleware --
000161 |     app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, ...)
000162 | [blank]
000163 |     # -- Routers --
000164 |     app.include_router(system.router)
000165 |     app.include_router(connectors.router)
000166 |     app.include_router(watcher.router)
000167 |     app.include_router(chat.router)
000168 |     app.include_router(dashboard.router)
000169 |     app.include_router(settings.router)
000170 |     app.include_router(notifications.router)
000171 |     app.include_router(projects.router)
000172 |     app.include_router(widgets.router)
000173 |     app.include_router(activity.router)
000174 |     app.include_router(demo.router)
000175 |     app.include_router(incidents.router)
000176 |     app.include_router(email.router)
000177 |     app.include_router(slack.router)
000178 | [blank]
000179 |     return app
000180 | [blank]
000181 | [blank]
000182 | app = create_app()
000183 | ```
000184 | [blank]
000185 | ### Step 5: Verify after each extraction
000186 | [blank]
000187 | After extracting each module:
000188 | [blank]
000189 | ```bash
000190 | # Run ALL tests — not just the ones you think are related
000191 | pytest tests/ -x -q
000192 | [blank]
000193 | # Verify endpoint count hasn't changed
000194 | python -c "

000001 | # B-03 — Extract Shared State from `server.py`
000002 | [blank]
000003 | **Owner:** Aryan
000004 | **Priority:** P0
000005 | **Status:** ⬜ Not Started
000006 | **Estimated effort:** 1–2 days

000009 | [blank]
000010 | ---
000011 | [blank]

After this task, zero global mutable state exists in `server.py` — all state is accessed through `request.app.state.app_state`.
000015 | [blank]

000017 | [blank]

000019 | [blank]
000020 | - **Currently:** `server.py` has 10+ global mutable variables (lines 141–169) shared across all endpoints. This creates:
000021 |   - **Race conditions:** Multiple concurrent requests modify `_notifications` or `_ws_clients` without locks
000022 |   - **Testing difficulty:** Tests can't reset state between runs without monkeypatching globals
000023 |   - **Decomposition blocker:** Route modules can't import globals from `server.py` without creating circular imports
000024 | - **After:** One `AppState` object holds all runtime state with thread-safe access. Route modules receive it via dependency injection. Tests create fresh state per test.
000025 | [blank]

000273 | ## Checklist
000274 | [blank]
000275 | ### Preparation

000280 | ### Implementation
000281 | - [ ] Create `prash/state.py` with `AppState` class

000294 | [blank]
000295 | ---
000296 | [blank]
000297 | ## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
000298 | [blank]
000299 | > **🚫 DO NOT use `asyncio.Lock` for everything.** Some state access happens from sync threads (watcher callbacks, connector SDK callbacks). Use `threading.RLock` which works in both sync and async contexts.
000300 | [blank]
000301 | > **🚫 DO NOT make AppState a singleton.** Tests need fresh state per test. The app creates ONE AppState and assigns it to `app.state.app_state`. Tests create their own.
000302 | [blank]
000303 | > **🚫 DO NOT hold locks while doing I/O.** Lock acquisition → mutate in-memory state → release lock. File I/O (`_save_notifications_to_disk`) happens AFTER the lock is released.
000304 | [blank]
000305 | > **🚫 DO NOT use `@property` for mutable collections.** Returning `self.notifications` gives the caller a reference to the internal list — they can mutate it without the lock. Use methods that return copies or perform the mutation inside the lock.
000306 | [blank]
000307 | > **🚫 DO NOT move business logic into AppState.** AppState is a state CONTAINER with thread-safe accessors. Business logic (formatting notifications, checking watcher health) stays in the route modules.
000308 | [blank]

000001 | # B-04 — API Versioning
000002 | [blank]
000003 | **Owner:** Parv

000010 | ---
000011 | [blank]
000012 | ## Objective
000013 | [blank]
000014 | Prefix all API endpoints with `/api/v1/`. Maintain backward compatibility by keeping the existing `/api/...` paths as redirects. Prepare the pattern for future `/api/v2/` without breaking existing desktop app clients.
000015 | [blank]
000016 | ---
000017 | [blank]
000018 | ## Why This Matters
000019 | [blank]
000020 | - **Currently:** Endpoints live under `/api/...` with no version prefix. Any breaking change to an endpoint requires coordinating backend and desktop app deployments simultaneously. There's no way to run an old desktop app against a new backend.
000021 | - **After:** The canonical path is `/api/v1/...`. The legacy `/api/...` paths redirect to v1. The desktop app is updated to call `/api/v1/...` directly. Adding v2 later is straightforward.
000022 | [blank]
000023 | ---
000024 | [blank]
000025 | ## Implementation Plan
000026 | [blank]
000027 | ### Step 1: Add version prefix to all routers
000028 | [blank]
000029 | After B-01, each route module has an `APIRouter`. Update their prefix:
000030 | [blank]
000031 | ```python
000032 | # prash/routes/connectors.py
000033 | # Before:
000034 | router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["connectors"])
000035 | [blank]
000036 | # After:
000037 | router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1", tags=["connectors"])
000038 | ```
000039 | [blank]
000040 | ### Step 2: Create legacy redirect middleware
000041 | [blank]
000042 | ```python
000043 | # prash/middleware/api_versioning.py
000044 | """Redirect unversioned /api/... to /api/v1/... for backward compatibility."""
000045 | from __future__ import annotations
000046 | [blank]
000047 | from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware, RequestResponseEndpoint
000048 | from starlette.requests import Request
000049 | from starlette.responses import RedirectResponse, Response
000050 | import re
000051 | [blank]
000052 | [blank]
000053 | class APIVersionRedirectMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
000054 |     """Redirect /api/... (without version) to /api/v1/...
000055 |     
000056 |     This allows old desktop app versions to keep working while
000057 |     new versions call /api/v1/... directly.
000058 |     """
000059 | [blank]
000060 |     async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next: RequestResponseEndpoint) -> Response:
000061 |         path = request.url.path
000062 | [blank]
000063 |         # Only redirect /api/... that doesn't already have a version
000064 |         if path.startswith("/api/") and not re.match(r"/api/v\d+/", path):
000065 |             # Redirect to /api/v1/...
000066 |             new_path = "/api/v1/" + path[len("/api/"):]
000067 |             # Use 307 to preserve the HTTP method (POST stays POST)
000068 |             return RedirectResponse(
000069 |                 url=new_path + ("?" + request.url.query if request.url.query else ""),
000070 |                 status_code=307,
000071 |             )
000072 | [blank]
000073 |         return await call_next(request)
000074 | ```
000075 | [blank]

000124 | ## Checklist
000125 | [blank]

000139 | ## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
000140 | [blank]
000141 | > **🚫 DO NOT use 301 or 302 redirects.** These cause browsers/clients to downgrade POST/PUT/DELETE to GET. Use `307 Temporary Redirect` which preserves the original HTTP method.

000256 | > **🚫 DO NOT change endpoint behavior.** This task is ONLY about input validation. If an endpoint currently accepts `{"foo": "bar"}` and works, the Pydantic model must accept the same shape. Do not rename fields.
000257 | [blank]
000258 | > **🚫 DO NOT add response models yet.** Response typing is a separate concern (tracked separately). This task is request-side only.
000259 | [blank]
000260 | > **🚫 DO NOT add auth/permission checks in this task.** That's S-07 and the existing permissions system.
000261 | [blank]
000262 | > **🚫 DO NOT use `model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}` globally.** Some endpoints intentionally accept extra fields (e.g., connector credentials are dynamic per connector). Use `extra = "forbid"` only where the schema is fully known and fixed.
000263 | [blank]
000264 | > **🚫 DO NOT suppress Pydantic's default 422 error format.** Let FastAPI's built-in validation error handler return the standard `{"detail": [{"loc": [...], "msg": "...", "type": "..."}]}` structure. Clients already handle this.
000265 | [blank]
000266 | ---
000267 | [blank]
000268 | ## Exit Criteria
000269 | [blank]
000270 | - [ ] **Every endpoint has a typed Pydantic request model** (for those that accept bodies) or constrained `Path()`/`Query()` parameters
000271 | - [ ] **Zero raw `dict` bodies accepted** — grep for `Body(...)` with no type annotation returns 0 hits
000272 | - [ ] **Fuzz test with 50 malformed payloads — 0 crashes** — `test_input_validation.py` passes, no 500s
000273 | - [ ] **All 800+ existing tests pass** without modification
````

### `tasks/week1/security/S-02_RATE_LIMITING.md`
````text
000001 | # S-02 — Rate Limiting Middleware
000002 | [blank]
000003 | **Owner:** Agrim
000004 | **Priority:** P0
000005 | **Status:** ⬜ Not Started
000006 | **Estimated effort:** 1–2 days
000007 | **Depends on:** Nothing (can start immediately, but easier after B-01 route split)
000008 | **Blocks:** Nothing
000009 | [blank]
000010 | ---
000011 | [blank]
000012 | ## Objective
000013 | [blank]
000014 | Add rate limiting middleware to the FastAPI backend. Implement per-IP rate limits on auth-sensitive endpoints and a global rate limit on all endpoints. Exceeding the limit must return `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header.
000015 | [blank]
000016 | ---
000017 | [blank]
000018 | ## Why This Matters
000019 | [blank]
000020 | - **Currently:** Every endpoint accepts unlimited requests. A single client can flood the server, causing denial of service for other users, or brute-force connector credentials via `/api/connectors/{id}/connect`.
000021 | - **After:** Auth-sensitive endpoints have tight limits (e.g., 10 req/min). Other endpoints have a reasonable global cap. The server stays responsive under abuse.
000022 | [blank]
000023 | ---
000024 | [blank]
000025 | ## Current State
000026 | [blank]
000027 | - No rate limiting exists anywhere in the codebase
000028 | - `server.py` (line 397–405) has only the `CORSMiddleware` — no other middleware
000029 | - The app is single-user local-first, but the API is network-exposed when the desktop app runs
000030 | [blank]
000031 | ---
000032 | [blank]
000033 | ## Implementation Plan
000034 | [blank]
000035 | ### Step 1: Choose and install the rate limiting library
000036 | [blank]
000037 | Use **`slowapi`** — it's the de facto rate limiter for FastAPI, built on `limits`.
000038 | [blank]
000039 | ```bash
000040 | pip install slowapi
000041 | ```
000042 | [blank]
000043 | Add to `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml`.
000044 | [blank]
000045 | ### Step 2: Create rate limiting configuration
000046 | [blank]
000047 | Create `prash/middleware/rate_limit.py`:
000048 | [blank]
000049 | ```python
000050 | """Rate limiting middleware configuration.
000051 | [blank]
000052 | Tiered rate limits:
000053 | - Auth-sensitive endpoints:  10 requests/minute per IP
000054 | - Chat/streaming endpoints:  30 requests/minute per IP
000055 | - General API endpoints:    120 requests/minute per IP
000056 | """
000057 | from __future__ import annotations
000058 | [blank]
000059 | import os
000060 | from slowapi import Limiter
000061 | from slowapi.util import get_remote_address
000062 | from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded
000063 | from fastapi import Request
000064 | from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
000065 | [blank]
000066 | # Allow override via environment for dev/testing
000067 | AUTH_RATE_LIMIT = os.getenv("LEAR_RATE_LIMIT_AUTH", "10/minute")
000068 | CHAT_RATE_LIMIT = os.getenv("LEAR_RATE_LIMIT_CHAT", "30/minute")
000069 | GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT = os.getenv("LEAR_RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL", "120/minute")
000070 | [blank]
000071 | limiter = Limiter(
000072 |     key_func=get_remote_address,
000073 |     default_limits=[GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT],
000074 |     storage_uri="memory://",  # In-memory for single-instance; swap to Redis for multi-instance
000075 | )
000076 | [blank]
000077 | [blank]
000078 | def rate_limit_exceeded_handler(request: Request, exc: RateLimitExceeded) -> JSONResponse:
000079 |     """Return a structured 429 response with Retry-After header."""
000080 |     retry_after = getattr(exc, "retry_after", 60)
000081 |     return JSONResponse(
000082 |         status_code=429,
000083 |         content={
000084 |             "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
000085 |             "message": f"Rate limit exceeded. Try again in {retry_after} seconds.",
000086 |             "retry_after": retry_after,
000087 |         },
000088 |         headers={"Retry-After": str(retry_after)},
000089 |     )
000090 | ```
000091 | [blank]
000092 | ### Step 3: Apply to auth-sensitive endpoints
000093 | [blank]
000094 | These endpoints are the highest risk for abuse:
000095 | [blank]
000096 | | Endpoint | Why it's sensitive | Limit |
000097 | |---|---|---|
000098 | | `POST /api/connectors/{id}/connect` | Credential submission — brute-force target | 10/minute |
000099 | | `POST /api/chat/stream` | LLM call — expensive compute | 30/minute |
000100 | | `POST /api/chat/execute` | Action execution — can modify external systems | 10/minute |
000101 | | `POST /api/chat` | LLM call | 30/minute |
000102 | | `POST /api/connect/{service_id}` | Legacy connector auth | 10/minute |
000103 | [blank]
000104 | Apply the decorator:
000105 | [blank]
000106 | ```python
000107 | from prash.middleware.rate_limit import limiter, AUTH_RATE_LIMIT, CHAT_RATE_LIMIT
000108 | [blank]
000109 | @app.post("/api/connectors/{connector_id}/connect")
000110 | @limiter.limit(AUTH_RATE_LIMIT)
000111 | async def connect_connector(request: Request, connector_id: str, ...):
000112 |     ...
000113 | [blank]
000114 | @app.post("/api/chat/stream")
000115 | @limiter.limit(CHAT_RATE_LIMIT)
000116 | async def chat_stream(request: Request, ...):
000117 |     ...
000118 | ```
000119 | [blank]
000120 | ### Step 4: Wire into the FastAPI app
000121 | [blank]
000122 | In `server.py` (or the app factory after B-01):
000123 | [blank]
000124 | ```python
000125 | from slowapi import _rate_limit_exceeded_handler
000126 | from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded
000127 | from prash.middleware.rate_limit import limiter, rate_limit_exceeded_handler
000128 | [blank]
000129 | app.state.limiter = limiter
000130 | app.add_exception_handler(RateLimitExceeded, rate_limit_exceeded_handler)
000131 | ```
000132 | [blank]
000133 | ### Step 5: Write integration tests
000134 | [blank]
000135 | Create `tests/test_rate_limiting.py`:
000136 | [blank]
000137 | ```python
